          "text": "ERes2NetV2 Chinese common for Sherpaw\nEmscripten preload assets for local speaker embedding extraction with Sherpaw. The model consumes 16 kHz speech through sherpa-onnx and produces a 192-dimensional embedding. Speaker names and enrollment storage belong to the application.\nSource and packaging\n- Original model: ERes2NetV2 Chinese common, published by the 3D-Speaker / iic team under Apache-2.0.\n- ONNX asset:\n3dspeaker_speech_eres2netv2_sv_zh-cn_16k-common.onnx, distributed by sherpa-onnx. - ONNX SHA-256:\n\nWeights are unchanged. Packaging renames the virtual file to /speaker-embedding.onnx and uses emscripten/emsdk:4.0.23. preload.data is byte-for-byte identical to the source ONNX file. manifest.json records source and artifact hashes.\nFiles and use\n\nUse these with Sherpaw's separately built speaker-embedding WASM runtime and preload support. These are model assets, not a standalone runtime or a Transformers pipeline.",

          "text": "polyvoice 0.12.0\n\nSpeaker diarization for Rust — who spoke when. ONNX path optional: default features are empty (ort-free BYO-embedder core); enable onnx for Silero VAD, WeSpeaker embeddings, and Pyannote segmentation.\nDocumentation\n#![allow(deprecated)] // legacy embedding API; see polyvoice::embedder\n//! ONNX-based speaker embedding extractor with a session pool.\n//!\n//! # Runtime boundary\n//!\n//! All `ort::` imports live in the private `ort_session` module. The optional\n\nNnapi,\n    Cuda,\n    XnnPack,\n}\n\nimpl ExecutionProvider {\n    /// Best default for the current target: CoreML on Apple Silicon, XNNPACK on\n    /// aarch64 Linux, plain CPU elsewhere. Unwired providers fall back to CPU\n\n/// when the build carries the `coreml` feature on macOS aarch64, else warns\n/// and runs on CPU. `Nnapi`/`Cuda`/`XnnPack` are not wired yet — they warn\n/// and run on CPU. EP registration failure is deliberately not an error:\n/// ort's built-in CPU fallback keeps inference correct. tract always uses\n/// pure-Rust CPU and ignores EP.\npub fn build_session_with_ep(\n    model_path: &Path,\n    ep: ExecutionProvider,\n    intra_threads: Option<usize>,\n\n/// Opens a short-lived CPU session solely to query model metadata, then drops\n/// it. Used by `models::metadata::load_model_config` so stage adapters can take\n/// geometry / license / adapter_type from the model itself (sherpa-onnx pattern).\n///\n\nlet session = OrtSession::from_path(path, ExecutionProvider::Cpu, Some(1))\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"open for metadata: {e}\"))?;\n    session.custom_metadata_props()\n}\n\n/// Error raised when an ONNX file fails structural header validation.\n\ndetail: \"ONNX magic bytes not found and file does not start with a valid ONNX protobuf header\".to_string(),\n        });\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// A pooled ONNX session for speaker embedding extraction.\n///",

          "text": "sci-ml/sherpa-onnx-bin\nSpeech-to-text, TTS, speaker diarization etc. using onnxruntime (binary wheels)\nChangeLog\ncommit 94bfc9a219cb882fbd7e508fce2fb790e63df3ab\nAuthor: Ivan S. Titov <iohann.s.titov@gmail.com>\nDate: Sat May 16 13:41:35 2026 +0200\nsci-ml/sherpa-onnx-bin: new package, add 1.13.2\nONNX-Runtime-based speech stack from k2-fsa: ASR, TTS, speaker\ndiarization, VAD, source separation, KWS. Standalone alternative\nto sci-ml/pyannote-audio for users who don't want the pytorch\nstack — runs CPU-only, uses ONNX-converted pyannote+3D-Speaker\nmodels that aren't HuggingFace-gated.\n-bin route via upstream manylinux2014 wheels. Two co-installable\nwheels: sherpa-onnx-core (Python-version-agnostic C++ libs) +\nsherpa-onnx (per-CPython-ABI bindings); SRC_URI gates the latter\non PYTHON_SINGLE_TARGET. Both unpack into the same sherpa_onnx/\ntree so the binding's RPATH=$ORIGIN dlopen resolves libonnxruntime.so.\n\nBuild + import smoke-tested on python3_13; OfflineSpeakerDiarization\nclass loads end-to-end. Runtime model files (pyannote-segmentation-3.0\nONNX + 3D-Speaker embeddings) live on HuggingFace, ungated.\nAuthor: Ivan S.           "text": "- Best-in-class at ~250M: TranscribePsy-250M-EU leads every similar-size model tested on all three benchmark suites: 8.02 word error rate on the Open ASR Leaderboard, 6.58 on Multilingual LibriSpeech and 21.56 on Common Voice, against 12.34 / 11.51\n\n- Beats models three to four times its size: on Multilingual LibriSpeech it scores 6.58 against 12.60 for Qwen3-ASR-0.6B (782M), 7.71 for omniASR-CTC-1B-v2 (976M), 7.76 for Whisper-Medium (764M) and 10.65 for OWSM-CTC-v4 (1.01B).\n\n| Open ASR Leaderboard | Mean of the English short-form and multilingual suites | 8.02 | 12.34 | 15.31 | 9.72 |\n| Multilingual LibriSpeech | 8-language mean | 6.58 | 11.51 | 11.89 | 11.84 |\n\nalone.\nA full technical report with the complete results will follow.             "type": "webpage_metadata",

            "favicon_url": "https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?sz=64&domain=arxiv.org",
            "site_name": "arxiv"
          },
          "is_missing": false,
          "text": "We tested 5 ASR models: Whisper (medium.en) [89]<sup>6</sup>, Whisper (turbo)<sup>7</sup>, NVIDIA NeMo<sup>8</sup> Quartznet [90] implementation, NVIDIA NeMo Fastconformer Transducer\n\n<sup>&</sup>lt;sup>6</sup>https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-medium.en\n\n<sup>&</sup>lt;sup>7</sup>https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo\n\n<sup>&</sup>lt;sup>8</sup>https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo\n\ncharacters correctly matching the ground truth tran-\n\n<sup>&</sup>lt;sup>10</sup>https://huggingface.co/facebook/wav2vec2-base-960h\n\n| Model | $\\mathbf{WER}\\downarrow$ | $\\mathbf{CER}\\downarrow$ | $\\mathbf{PER}\\downarrow$ |\n| Whisper - medium.en | 31.15% | 15.13% | 14.23% |\n| Whisper - turbo | <b>29.55</b> % | $\\boldsymbol{13.72\\%}$ | <b>12.67</b> % |\n| NeMo Quartznet | 65.16% | 32.20% | 32.80% |\n| NeMo Fastconformer Transducer | 40.61% | 22.33% | 21.49% |\n| Wav2Vec2-Base-960h | 76.21% | 35.28% | 36.52% |\n\nTable 4: ASR benchmark results over all data.\n\n $<sup>^{*}</sup>$ Same as other Whisper models but with 4 instead of 32 decoding layers. $^{**}$ Multilingual.\n\n<sup>&</sup>lt;sup>9</sup>https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/teams/nemo/models/ $stt_en_fastconformer_transducer_large$\n\nWe see both the Whisper models showing the best performance, followed by the Fastconformer Transducer. Yet, all the models perform worse (between 29.55 and 76.21% WER) than the usual reported WERs, which are often below 10%.\n\n| No Shout | <b>23.29</b> % | 10.32% | 10.01% |\n\nTable 5: ASR benchmark results for Whis- Table 6: ASR benchmark results for Whisper medium.en.\n\nper turbo.\n\nWe further investigated the performance of these ASR models to better understand how performance differs over different distances and for different emotions and shout levels. The results can be seen in Tables 5 - 9 and in Figures 8 - 9.           "text": "import nemo.collections.asr as nemo_asr asr_model = nemo_asr.models.ASRModel.from_pretrained(\"happyman11/TacRFC-fastconformer\") transcriptions = asr_model.transcribe([\"file.wav\"]) - Notebooks\n- Google Colab\n- Kaggle\nFastConformer Hybrid (RNNT+CTC) β Fine-tuned for Tactical Radio ASR (Hindi-English Code-Switched)\n\nIt is one of eight architectures (FastConformer, SeamlessM4T v2 Large, IndicConformer, Whisper base/small/medium/large-v3, and wav2vec2-XLSR-53) benchmarked on the TacRFC dataset.\nUpdated September 2026.\n\nASR_SET 3.0English corpus), this checkpoint is consistent with NVIDIA'sstt_en_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc. The exact base checkpoint name is not recorded in the exported archive.\nModel Details\n- Architecture:\n\nComparison with the other retrained models (same 138-chunk test set)\n| Model | WER zero-shot β fine-tuned | CER zero-shot β fine-tuned |\n|---|---|---|\n| Whisper Large-v3 | 0.7553 β 0.5779 | 0.6630 β 0.4847 |\n| FastConformer Hybrid (RNNT+CTC) (this model) | 0.9643 β 0.6174 | 0.9302 β 0.5636 |\n| Whisper Medium | 0.8417 β 0.6263 | 0.7543 β 0.4945 |\n| Whisper Small | 0.8761 β 0.6532 | 0.7522 β 0.5230 |\n| wav2vec2-XLSR-53 | 0.9717 β 0.8799 | 0.7068 β 0.5769 |\n\nThese values were logged during training. They use the training loop's own decoding and scoring, not the normalized test-time evaluation above, so compare models on the test numbers.\nHow to Use\nfrom huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download\nimport nemo.collections.asr as nemo_asr\nmodel_path = hf_hub_download(repo_id=\"happyman11/TacRFC-fastconformer\", filename=\"model.nemo\")\nmodel = nemo_asr.models.EncDecHybridRNNTCTCBPEModel.restore_from(model_path)\nmodel.eval()\n\nIf you use this model, please cite the corresponding paper.\n@misc{tacrfc_fastconformer,\ntitle = {TacRFC: A Hindi-English Code-Mixed Tactical Radio Frequency Communication Corpus for Low-Resource Domain ASR},\nauthor = {[Your name / lab]",

          "text": "Home / Companies / Hugging Face / Blog / Post Details\nContent Deep Dive\n\nArmBench-ASR: A Benchmark for Armenian ASR\n\nBlog post from Hugging Face\n\nPost Details\nCompany\nDate Published\nAuthor\nAlexander Shahramanyan, Mariam Avetisyan, and Hrant Davtyan\n\nArmBench-ASR v0.1 is a benchmark designed to make Armenian automatic speech recognition systems easier to compare by evaluating nearly 30 open-weight and closed models across 10,113 audio clips, totaling about 20.7 hours, from five datasets\n\nIt reports both strict and normalized word and character error rates using consistent preprocessing, with Gemini 2.5 Pro achieving the best combined strict WER of 14.31%, while NVIDIA’s Armenian FastConformer is the highest-ranking open model at 20.21%. Results vary substantially by domain, with movie dialogue proving the most difficult category and normalization showing that punctuation, capitalization, and orthographic variation contribute significantly to measured errors. Closed systems occupy the eight best aggregate positions, although Armenian open models lead on Common Voice and HiSpeech models perform strongly on poetry.",

          "text": "---\ntitle: \"Benchmarking Open ASR Models on NVIDIA L4: Parakeet vs Whisper vs Nemotron Speech\"\ndescription: >\n  Open-weight ASR has reached a point where the model choice is only half\n  the decision. The other half is configuration — and most teams get it\n  wrong by ...\nslug: \"benchmarking-asr-models-nvidia-l4-parakeet-whisper-nemotron\"\ndate: \"2026-03-27\"\nfeatured_image: \"https://strapi-main-website.objectstore.e2enetworks.net/Benchmarking_Open_ASR_ae8905ec50.png\"\n---\n\n# Benchmarking Open ASR Models on NVIDIA L4: Parakeet vs Whisper vs Nemotron Speech\n\nOpen-weight ASR has reached a point where the model choice is only half\nthe decision. The other half is configuration — and most teams get it\nwrong by default.\n\nBatch size, precision, attention implementation, chunk length, decoding\n\nWe wanted concrete answers for the hardware we offer. So we took the\nthree most widely used open ASR models, spun up an NVIDIA L4 (23 GB)\ninstance on [E2E Cloud](https://www.e2enetworks.com/gpus), and\n\n- All three models fit on 23 GB with significant headroom\n\n## The Problem with Default ASR Configurations\n\nEvery ASR library ships with defaults. Those defaults are reasonable\nstarting points, but they are not production configurations.\n\n| openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo            | 809 M      | Encoder-Decoder Transformer      | OpenAI Whisper |\n| nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3              | 600 M      | FastConformer + TDT Decoder      | NVIDIA NeMo    |\n\nwhen it sees it. The practical implication is significant and shows up\ndirectly in the benchmark results.\n\n## 2. Test Setup\n\nGPU: NVIDIA L4 — 23,034 MiB VRAM\n\nCUDA: 12.4\n\nPyTorch: 2.6.0\n\nStack: HuggingFace Transformers 4.43+ \\| NVIDIA NeMo 2.7.0\n\nwithin each model are fully valid; cross-model WER comparison should\naccount for this.\n\n## 3.           "is_missing": false,
          "text": "# 4.2 Helsinki-NLP Opus-MT\n\nOPUS-MT (Tiedemann and Thottingal, 2020) supports both bilingual and multilingual models. It is a project that focuses on the development of free resources and tools for machine translation. The current status is a repository of over 1,000 pretrained neural MT models. We fine-tune a transformer-align model that was fine-tuned for the Tatoeba-Challenge<sup>10</sup>. Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-en-ga model from the HuggingFace Transformers (Wolf et al., 2020) for English $\\rightarrow$ Irish and Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-ga-en for Irish $\\rightarrow$ English were used.\n\n| Language pair | Method | BLEU |\n| English→Marathi | IndicTrans baseline | 14.0 |\n| English→Marathi | IndicTrans TRA | 17.8 |\n| English→Marathi | IndicTrans CVIT-PIB | 23.4 |\n| English→Marathi | IndicTrans bible-uedin | 27.7 |\n| English→Irish | Opus MT | 30.4 |\n| English→Irish | M2M100 | 25.6 |\n| Irish→English | Opus MT | 37.2 |\n| Irish→English | M2M100 | 30.4 |\n\nTable 2: BLEU scores obtained for the various models for the development set",

        {
          "type": "knowledge",
          "title": "hy simulmt 30b a3b vs helsinki opus mt",
          "url": "https://www.orcarouter.ai/blog/hy-simulmt-30b-a3b-vs-helsinki-opus-mt",
          "metadata": {
            "type": "webpage_metadata",
            "site_domain": "orcarouter.ai",
            "favicon_url": "https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?sz=64&domain=orcarouter.ai",
            "site_name": "orcarouter"
          },
          "is_missing": false,
          "text": "A hero title card for Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B vs Helsinki-NLP OPUS-MT, subtitled 'A live interpreter against a folder of specialists', showing on the left one card with an audio waveform turning into a subtitle line labelled 'one streaming model' and on\n\nper checkpoint - CPU-capable', and the OrcaRouter logo bottom right.\nGuides & Insights\n\nHy-SimulMT-30B-A3B vs Helsinki-NLP OPUS-MT: A Live Interpreter Against a Folder of Specialists\n\nAuthor\n\nElias Hawthorne\n\nDate Published\n\nHelsinki-NLP OPUS-MT is the most widely deployed open translation system in the world and is built for a narrower version of the first: it translates text, one sentence at a time, one language direction per checkpoint, and it has been downloaded\n\nOPUS-MT is maintained by the University of Helsinki's NLP group and built on the MarianMT encoder-decoder architecture.\n\nIf your requirement is Mandarin to English in a live meeting, Hy-SimulMT is aimed exactly at you. If your requirement is Polish to Finnish on a static document, OPUS-MT has a checkpoint for it and Hy-SimulMT does not.\n\nIt says nothing about speech, and it does not involve Hy-SimulMT, because no independent lab has evaluated Hy-SimulMT at all.\n\nA two-column scoreboard for Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B and Helsinki-NLP OPUS-MT across six rows: parameters, footprint, input, latency, speech languages and licence.\n\nThe footer reads 'OPUS-MT BLEU per a published Fassa Ladin study; Hy-SimulMT figures vendor-reported.'\n\nCost and deployment, side by side\n\n• Parameters — Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B: 30.4B total, roughly 3B active, sparse MoE; Helsinki-NLP OPUS-MT: about 70–80M per checkpoint, dense.\n\n• Latency model — Hy-SimulMT: streaming, approximately 3 s StreamLAAL on long-form audio. OPUS-MT: sentence-at-a-time; streaming requires an ASR and a segmentation policy you build.\n\n• Languages — Hy-SimulMT: Chinese and English documented for speech, 36 tagged in metadata. OPUS-MT: roughly a hundred languages across more than a thousand directional checkpoints.",

          "text": "TranslateGemma 4B — ONNX Runtime GenAI, int4, CPU\n\nONNX Runtime GenAI build (int4 weights, fp32 activations, CPU execution provider) of the text component of google/translategemma-4b-it, Google's translation-specialized Gemma 3 model covering 55 languages.\n\nConversion notes\n\n  • Text decoder extracted from the multimodal checkpoint (Gemma3ForCausalLM, model type gemma3_text); the vision tower is not included.\n  • Converted with the onnxruntime-genai model builder (python -m onnxruntime_genai.models.builder -p int4 -e cpu).\n  • genai_config.json ships with eos_token_id: [1, 106] so that <end_of_turn> terminates generation (the stock config only stopped on <eos>).\n\nPrompt format\n\nGemma requires the <bos> token at the start of the prompt — without it the output degenerates.           "text": "# Fast-Inference with Ctranslate2\n\nSpeedup inference while reducing memory by 2x-4x using int8 inference in C++ on CPU or GPU.\n\nquantized version of facebook/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B\n\npip install ctranslate2\n\nCheckpoint compatible to ctranslate2>=3.22.0\n\n  • compute_type=int8_float16 for device=\"cuda\"\n  • compute_type=int8 for device=\"cpu\"\n\nConverted on 2023-11-30 using CTranslate2==3.22.0 and\n\nfrom ctranslate2.converters import TransformersConverter\nTransformersConverter(\n    \"facebook/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B\",\n    activation_scales=None,\n    copy_files=['tokenizer.json', 'generation_config.json', 'README.md', 'special_tokens_map.json', 'tokenizer_config.json', '.gitattributes'],\n    load_as_float16=True,\n    revision=None,\n    low_cpu_mem_usage=True,\n    trust_remote_code=True,\n).convert(\n    output_dir=str(tmp_dir),\n    vmap = None, \n    quantization=\"int8\",\n    force = True,\n)\n\nLicence and other remarks:\n\nThis is just a quantized version. Licence conditions are intended to be idential to original huggingface repo.\n\nOriginal description\n\nNLLB-200\n\nThis is the model card of NLLB-200's distilled 1.3B variant.\n\nThe exact training algorithm, data and the strategies to handle data imbalances for high and low resource languages that were used to train NLLB-200 is described in the paper.\n\n• Primary intended uses: NLLB-200 is a machine translation model primarily intended for research in machine translation, - especially for low-resource languages. It allows for single sentence translation among 200 languages.\n\n• Model performance measures: NLLB-200 model was evaluated using BLEU, spBLEU, and chrF++ metrics widely adopted by machine translation community.\n\n• Motivation: We used Flores-200 as it provides full evaluation coverage of the languages in NLLB-200\n  • Preprocessing: Sentence-split raw text data was preprocessed using SentencePiece.           "text": "Translation Model\n\nCTranslate2 is a C++ and Python library for efficient inference with Transformer models. Models converted from CTranslate2 can run with lower resources and faster speed.\n\nName | Parameters | Size | type/quantize | Required VRAM |\n---|---|---|---|---|\nfacebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M | 600M | 2.46 GB | float32 | ≈2.5 GB |\nfacebook/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B | 1.3B | 5.48 GB | float32 | ≈5.9 GB |\n\nmichaelfeil/ct2fast-nllb-200-distilled-1.3B | 1.3B | 1.38 GB | int8_float16 | ≈1.3 GB |\nmichaelfeil/ct2fast-nllb-200-3.3B | 3.3B | 3.36 GB | int8_float16 | ≈3.2 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-1.3B-ct2-int8 | 1.3B | 1.38 GB | int8 | ≈1.3 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-1.3B-ct2-float16 | 1.3B | 2.74 GB | float16 | ≈1.3 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-distilled-600M-ct2 | 600M | 2.46 GB | float32 | ≈0.6 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-distilled-600M-ct2-float16 | 600M | 1.23 GB | float16 | ≈0.6 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-distilled-600M-ct2-int8 | 600M | 623 MB | int8 | ≈0.6 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B-ct2-float16 | 1.3B | 2.74 GB | float16 | ≈1.3 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B-ct2-int8 | 1.3B | 1.38 GB | int8 | ≈1.3 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B-ct2 | 1.3B | 5.49 GB | float32 | ≈1.3 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-1.3B-ct2 | 1.3B | 5.49 GB | float32 | ≈1.3 GB |\nJustFrederik/nllb-200-3.3B-ct2-float16 | 3.3B | 6.69 GB | float16 | ≈3.2 GB |\nMT5\n\nDue to the poor support of GPTQ for CPUs, the execution time per iteration exceeds a thousand seconds when operating on a CPU.           "text": "NLLB-200 Distilled 600M (CTranslate2 INT8)\n\nThis repository contains the Facebook NLLB-200 Distilled 600M model converted to the CTranslate2 format using INT8 quantization.\n\nConversion\n\nct2-transformers-converter \\\n    --model facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M \\\n    --output_dir nllb-600m-ct2 \\\n    --quantization int8\n\nHow to use?\n\nimport ctranslate2\nfrom transformers import AutoTokenizer\nfrom huggingface_hub import snapshot_download\n\nREPO_ID = \"pulkitchowdry/nllb-600m-ct2-int8\"\n\n# Download model from Hugging Face\nmodel_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id=REPO_ID)\n\nprint(\"Model downloaded to:\", model_dir)\n\n# Load translator\ntranslator = ctranslate2.Translator(\n    model_dir,\n    device=\"cpu\"\n)\n\n# Load tokenizer\ntokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_dir, fix_mistral_regex=True)\n\nsrc_lang = \"eng_Latn\"\ntgt_lang = \"fra_Latn\"\n\ntext = \"Hello, how are you today?\"\n\ntokenizer.src_lang = src_lang\n\n# Tokenize\n\nThis model isn't deployed by any Inference Provider. 🙋 Ask for provider support\n\nModel tree for pulkitchowdry/nllb-600m-ct2-int8\n\nFinetuned\n(342)\nthis model",

        "content": "# PLAN — Live Armenian → English transcription with speaker labels\n\nStatus: planning only. Nothing installed or implemented yet.\nTarget machine: Windows 11, i5-13500H, 8 GB RAM, Intel Iris Xe (no CUDA). Everything runs on CPU.\n\n## 1. Goal\n\nBuild a Python terminal program that:\n- captures the **microphone** (labelled `Me`) and the **system audio** (the call side) at the same time;\n- cuts each stream into spoken phrases and transcribes them as Armenian text;\n- translates each phrase into English;\n- labels call-side phrases `Speaker 1`, `Speaker 2`, … and keeps each label stable for the whole session;\n- prints `[time] speaker / HY / EN`. The target is ≤ 5 s from the end of a phrase to its English line. This is **a target to measure, not a promise.**\n\nLocal models only. Keep it small. Spare time goes to reliability, not features.\n\n## 2. What the research changes\n\n| Finding | Source | Consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| NVIDIA FastConformer-Hybrid (hy), 115M params, is the **best open model** on the independent ArmBench-ASR v1.0 (combined WER 19.9; Whisper-large-v3 zero-shot 65.1). | ArmBench-ASR leaderboard; Karpov et al., Interspeech 2025 | Primary ASR candidate. It is small enough for CPU. |\n| Even that model scores **~61% WER on movie dialogue**, against 7.7% on Common Voice read speech. It was trained on read speech and its card calls it noise-sensitive. | ArmBench-ASR; model card | Conversational call audio is the **main quality risk**. The README must state this honestly. |\n| An **ONNX export** exists (CTC head, fp32) that runs with `onnx-asr` and ONNX Runtime. It needs **no NeMo or PyTorch**. There is no int8 version. | `OpenVoiceOS/stt_hy_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc_onnx` | It avoids installing NeMo on Windows. The paper's numbers are for the RNN-T head, so CTC quality must be measured. |\n| The model card says it is **non-streaming**. | model card | Run it once per VAD segment, not as a stream. |\n| Armenian fine-tunes of Whisper exist (turbo ~0.8B, large-v3) but rank **below** FastConformer on ArmBench and are 7–13× larger. | ArmBench-ASR | Fallback only, if FastConformer fails on our audio. |\n| Coria et al. (diart): rolling-buffer segmentation plus **incremental clustering**. New speaker if distance > δ_new. Update a centroid **only from long-enough segments** (ρ_update). Speaker confusion rises as latency drops. Labels improve as the conversation goes on. | Paper provided | Borrow the clustering rules and nothing else. Expect labels to be shaky in the first minute. |\n| Newer streaming diarizers exist (FASTDIAR 2026, ~10M params, 5× real-time on one CPU thread). | microsoft/fastdiar | Fallback only, if the simple approach measurably fails. |\n| sherpa-onnx ships ungated ONNX speaker-embedding models (3D-Speaker CAM++, WeSpeaker) for CPU. | sherpa-onnx docs | Gives speaker embeddings without pyannote or a Hugging Face token. |\n| Translation: NLLB-200 distilled 600M is available as CTranslate2 int8 (~0.6 GB). TranslateGemma-4B (Gemma terms) Q4 is ~2.5 GB. Gemma-3/NLLB-3.3B score well on hye→eng, but those sizes are too big here. | HF model cards; OpenWHO eval | NLLB-600M int8 is primary. TranslateGemma-4B is an optional experiment, only if RAM and latency allow. |\n| ArmBench and almost all training data are **Eastern Armenian**. | ArmBench; Chakmakjian & Wang 2022 | Your Western-influenced pronunciation on the mic is a specific risk. Test it explicitly. |\n\n**Not taken from the papers:** data collection, pseudo-labelling, fine-tuning, overlap-aware segmentation models, hyper-parameter optimisation pipelines.\n\n## 3. Architecture\n\n```\n mic (WASAPI)       ─► Capture ─► VAD/Segmenter ─┐\n loopback (WASAPI)  ─► Capture ─► VAD/Segmenter ─┤\n                                                 ▼\n                                        segment queue (FIFO)\n                                                 ▼\n                       Worker: Speaker → ASR → Translate → Printer\n```\n\n- One capture thread per source. One shared inference worker, because parallel models on 4 performance cores would fight each other. If measurement shows ASR and MT pipelining helps, that becomes a two-stage worker.\n- The pipeline is the same for live audio and for **WAV replay**, so every test can be repeated.\n- Every segment carries timestamps, logged at each stage, so latency is measured rather than guessed.\n\n## 4. Modules and their inputs/outputs\n\n| Module | Input | Output | Initial choice (to confirm in M1) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `audio/devices.py` | — | printed device list; resolved device IDs from `--mic` / `--loopback` | PyAudioWPatch (WASAPI loopback, no virtual cable) |\n| `audio/capture.py` | device ID | `(source, float32 mono 16 kHz chunk, t_capture)` | downmix + resample (soxr) |\n| `audio/segmenter.py` | chunks of one source | `Segment(source, t_start, t_end, audio)` | Silero VAD (ONNX); silence hang-over ~0.5 s; max segment length ~10 s (both tunable) |\n| `speakers.py` | `Segment` | `\"Me\"` for mic; `\"Speaker N\"` for loopback | CAM++ or ECAPA embedding + online cosine clustering with δ_new; centroid updated only for segments ≥ ~1.5 s |\n| `asr.py` | segment audio | Armenian text (punctuated) | FastConformer-hy ONNX (CTC) via onnx-asr |\n| `translate.py` | Armenian text | English text | NLLB-200-distilled-600M, CTranslate2 int8 |\n| `output.py` | labelled result + timings | terminal lines; optional `--debug-latency` column | plain print |\n| `pipeline.py` / `main.py` | CLI flags | wiring, threads, queue, shutdown | stdlib `threading` + `queue` |\n| `tools/replay.py`, `tools/bench_*.py` | WAV files | the same pipeline offline; metric tables | jiwer, sacrebleu |\n\nEach model module exposes one function so it can be swapped (`transcribe(audio) -> str`, `translate(text) -> str`, `assign(segment) -> label`). There are no plugin frameworks.\n\n## 5. Major risks\n\n1. **ASR quality on conversational and call audio.** The domain gap from read speech is large (ArmBench Movies ~61% WER). Codecs, noise, and short replies like «հա», «լավ» make it worse.\n2. **Western-accented speech on the mic.** The model is Eastern-trained and the accent effect is unmeasured.\n3. **CPU contention and latency.** Both sides plus the call app share one laptop. Backlog in the queue directly breaks the 5 s budget.\n4. **8 GB RAM.** Models (~2 GB estimated, *to measure*) plus Windows plus the call app plus a browser.\n5. **CTC vs RNN-T.** The ONNX export uses the CTC head. Quality may be below the published numbers.\n6. **Diarization on short segments.** Embeddings from segments under ~1–1.5 s are unreliable. Cold start produces label churn. A VAD segment may contain two speakers if there's no pause. Overlap is ignored. Codec audio can make voices sound alike.\n7. **Translation of noisy or fragmentary ASR output.** NLLB can hallucinate on very short or broken input. NLLB is CC-BY-NC, which is fine for this challenge but must be noted.\n8. **Windows audio quirks.** The loopback device changes when output switches between headphones, Bluetooth and speakers. Sample rates and channel counts vary.\n9. **Audio leakage without headphones.** Echo handling is out of scope, but leakage causes duplicate `Me` lines. This will be documented rather than fixed.\n\n## 6. Milestones and how each is tested\n\n| # | Milestone | Done when / test |\n|---|---|---|\n| M0 | **Audio capture.** List devices, pick them by flag, record mic and loopback together to WAV. | Record 60 s of a real call (Meet, Zoom, Telegram) with headphones and with speakers. Both WAVs are audible, there are no dropouts, and they are time-aligned. Unplugging or switching the device gives a clear error, not a hang. |\n| M1 | **Model spike (offline benchmark, decision gate).** No live code yet. | ASR: ~50 FLEURS `hy_am` + ~20 Common Voice clips + your own recordings, split into Eastern speakers and your voice. Report CER/WER, real-time factor and peak RAM for FastConformer-CTC, plus Whisper-turbo-hy as a reference. MT: ~100 FLORES hye→eng sentences, clean and with ASR output as input. Report chrF and ms per sentence for NLLB-600M, with TranslateGemma-4B only if RAM allows. Speakers: cosine-score distributions for same vs. different speaker at 1, 2 and 4 s. **Outputs: a choice of models plus written numbers for the README.** |\n| M2 | **Live segmentation.** VAD on both streams prints `[time] source segment-length`. | Replay WAVs at real-time speed and count segments against hand-marked phrases. Live: speaking short and long phrases creates no merged or chopped segments. Tune the hang-over and the maximum length here. |\n| M3 | **ASR in the loop.** Live Armenian text with latency logging. | Replay test set: CER matches M1, which shows the integration adds no errors. The latency log shows p50/p95 from end of segment to text. If p95 is already near 5 s, stop and re-plan before adding MT. |\n| M4 | **Translation in the loop.** | Same replay with EN output. Spot-check ~30 lines by hand (you're fluent in both languages). The p95 end-to-end latency is reported. |\n| M5 | **Speaker labels on loopback.** | Build a replay file of 3 known speakers taking alternating turns (from your recordings or CV clips with different `client_id`s). Report segment-level label accuracy and the number of spurious new speakers. Tune δ_new and the minimum update duration on this file only, then confirm on a second file. |\n| M6 | **Full live run and hardening.** | 30-min session with both sides active: RAM is stable, the queue doesn't grow, Ctrl+C exits cleanly. Rehearse the interview setup with ≥ 2 people on the call side, including you speaking with your accent. Record the honest results. |\n| M7 | **Deliverables.** | README: setup, devices, models with alternatives and numbers, architecture, limitations. Export every chat session to `chats/` as separate `.md` files. Confirm the repo contains no weights, audio or keys (`.gitignore` plus a final check). |\n\n**Decision gates:**\n- After M1: if FastConformer-CTC is clearly worse than expected, try exporting the RNN-T head or switching to the Whisper fallback.\n- After M3/M4: if latency is too high, shorten the maximum segment length, cut thread counts or use a smaller MT model.\n- After M5: only if label accuracy is clearly poor, consider a streaming diarizer (diart or FASTDIAR).\n\n## 7. Explicitly not doing\nGUI, packaging, echo cancellation, named or persistent speakers, saving transcripts, non-Armenian input, fine-tuning, LLM post-editing, or GPU/OpenVINO work. The last one is revisited only if M3/M4 latency forces it.\n\n## 8. References\n- Coria, Bredin, Ghannay, Rosset — *Overlap-aware low-latency online speaker diarization based on end-to-end local segmentation* (diart).\n- Karpov et al. — *From Scarcity to Sufficiency: Speech Recognition Pipeline for Zero-resource Language*, Interspeech 2025.\n- Metric AI Lab — ArmBench-ASR v1.0 leaderboard (metric-ai-armbench-asr.static.hf.space).\n- nvidia/stt_hy_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc; OpenVoiceOS ONNX export.\n- Torgashov & Köpüklü — FASTDIAR (arXiv 2610.02941), as a fallback only.\n- Chakmakjian & Wang — *Towards a Unified ASR System for the Armenian Standards*, DigitAm 2022.\n"

      "text": "PLAN.md is ready. Three findings shaped it most, and you should check them before we build on them.\n\n**1. The ASR choice has independent backing, but quality is the risk.** The NVIDIA Armenian FastConformer from the Interspeech paper ranks first among open models on ArmBench-ASR, a 2026 benchmark from Metric AI Lab:\n- combined WER 19.86, with 7.70 on Common Voice but 60.78 on movie dialogue\n- whisper-large-v3 zero-shot, for comparison: 65.12\n\nThat gap between read speech and dialogue is the biggest quality risk for a live call, so the plan says this openly instead of promising accuracy.\n\n**2. There's a Windows-friendly way to run that model.** An existing ONNX export runs offline with ONNX Runtime; PyTorch and NeMo are not required. Two catches:\n- It uses the CTC head, while the paper reports RNN-T numbers.\n- There is no int8 variant.\n\nThe model card also says the model is non-streaming, so we transcribe one VAD segment at a time. All of this gets measured in M1 before anything is committed.\n\n**3. Diarization stays simple.** From the diart paper I'm taking only the clustering rules:\n- a new-speaker threshold;\n- centroids updated only from long-enough segments.\n\nTheir segmentation model and tuning pipeline are left out. Newer streaming diarizers like FASTDIAR are listed as a fallback only if measured label accuracy is poor.\n\n**Dialect risk for your mic side.** The benchmark currently covers mainly Eastern Armenian and excludes Western Armenian and regional dialects. So M1 measures your voice separately from Eastern speakers. That's where your recordings come in.\n\nThe first step that needs installing anything is M0 (capturing mic and loopback). I can't run it for you either, because my shell there can't reach Windows audio devices, so the steps below are for you.

## What was built
- `tools\m0_record.py` lists your devices and records the mic and system audio to two WAV files.
  - It refuses to start unless you pass both `--mic` and `--loopback`.
  - In `--guided` mode it runs a 60-second test script with live level meters for both streams.
- `tools\m0_check.py` analyses a recording and writes `m0_report.txt` with PASS or FAIL for each check:
  - whether speech landed in the right stream in each phase, including the overlap phase;
  - mic dropouts, buffer overflows, clipping, file length against the clock;
  - remote voice leaking into the mic.
- Both streams are aligned to one shared clock, so second 30 in one file is second 30 in the other.
- I tested the logic here with simulated audio. A clean run passes. Injected faults are caught: a 0.6 s mic dropout and remote voice leaking into the mic.

**One Windows behaviour to know about:** the loopback stream sends nothing while no sound is playing. The recorder fills those stretches with silence and the checker labels them "idle", so they don't count as dropouts. A hole while sound is playing does count, and gets flagged.

## Installations (please read before running)
Everything goes into a `.venv` folder inside the project. It doesn't touch Anaconda or system Python, and deleting `.venv` undoes it. No admin rights, drivers or virtual cable are needed, because Windows' built-in WASAPI loopback does the job BlackHole does on a Mac.
- **PyAudioWPatch**: a version of the standard audio library (PortAudio) that can record from output devices. It's a small prebuilt Windows package under the MIT licence.
- **numpy**: for the level meters and the analysis.

In PowerShell:
```
cd $HOME\GitHub\live-armenian-translation
python --version
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python tools\m0_record.py --list-devices
```
You need Python 3.10–3.13. If `Activate.ps1` is blocked, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass` first; it only applies to that window. Send me the device list if you'd like a second opinion on which indices to pick.

## Google Meet test with headphones
1. **Setup.**
   - In Windows sound settings and in Meet's audio settings, set the output to your headphones and the microphone to the one you'll pass with `--mic`.
   - Wired headphones are best. With Bluetooth, using the headset's own mic switches it into a low-quality "Hands-Free" mode, and the loopback then has to be that "Headset" device.
   - The remote person must be on another device **in another room**, or their voice reaches your mic through the air.
2. **Agree on a signal beforehand.** When you wave, they start talking and keep going for about 30 seconds until you wave again. Reading any text aloud works.
3. **Run:** `python tools\m0_record.py --mic N --loopback M --guided` and follow the cues on screen:
   - 0–5 s: silence
   - 5–20 s: you talk
   - at 20 s: you wave; they talk and you stay silent
   - 35–50 s: you start talking too, so both of you talk at once
   - at 50 s: you wave; they stop
   - 50–60 s: silence

   While it runs, the MIC bar should move only for your voice and the SYS bar only for theirs.
4. **Check:** `python tools\m0_check.py recordings\<folder it printed>`

Then tell me it's done. I can read `m0_report.txt` directly in that folder and report every dropout or capture error; no audio needs to leave your laptop.

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Audio device discovery for Windows (WASAPI) using PyAudioWPatch.\n\nOnly WASAPI devices are listed: the same physical device also appears under\nMME / DirectSound, which would just add duplicates. A loopback device is the\n\"recording\" twin of an output device (speakers / headphones), so capturing it\nrecords whatever Windows plays there, e.g. the other side of a call.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nimport pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Device:\n    index: int\n    name: str\n    kind: str          # \"mic\" or \"loopback\"\n    channels: int\n    rate: int\n    is_default: bool\n\n\ndef _wasapi(pa: pyaudio.PyAudio) -> dict:\n    try:\n        return pa.get_host_api_info_by_type(pyaudio.paWASAPI)\n    except OSError as e:  # WASAPI missing would be very unusual on Windows 10/11\n        raise RuntimeError(\"WASAPI host API not available on this system\") from e\n\n\ndef _default_loopback_index(pa: pyaudio.PyAudio, wasapi: dict) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Loopback twin of the current default output device, if found.\"\"\"\n    out_idx = wasapi.get(\"defaultOutputDevice\", -1)\n    if out_idx < 0:\n        return None\n    speakers = pa.get_device_info_by_index(out_idx)\n    if speakers.get(\"isLoopbackDevice\"):\n        return speakers[\"index\"]\n    for lb in pa.get_loopback_device_info_generator():\n        if speakers[\"name\"] in lb[\"name\"]:\n            return lb[\"index\"]\n    return None\n\n\ndef list_devices(pa: pyaudio.PyAudio) -> list[Device]:\n    wasapi = _wasapi(pa)\n    default_mic = wasapi.get(\"defaultInputDevice\", -1)\n    default_lb = _default_loopback_index(pa, wasapi)\n    devices: list[Device] = []\n    for i in range(pa.get_device_count()):\n        info = pa.get_device_info_by_index(i)\n        if info[\"hostApi\"] != wasapi[\"index\"] or info[\"maxInputChannels\"] <= 0:\n            continue\n        is_lb = bool(info.get(\"isLoopbackDevice\"))\n        devices.append(Device(\n            index=info[\"index\"],\n            name=info[\"name\"],\n            kind=\"loopback\" if is_lb else \"mic\",\n            channels=int(info[\"maxInputChannels\"]),\n            rate=int(info[\"defaultSampleRate\"]),\n            is_default=info[\"index\"] == (default_lb if is_lb else default_mic),\n        ))\n    return devices\n\n\ndef print_devices(devices: list[Device]) -> None:\n    for kind, title in ((\"mic\", \"MICROPHONES  (use with --mic)\"),\n                        (\"loopback\", \"SYSTEM AUDIO / LOOPBACK  (use with --loopback)\")):\n        print(f\"\\n{title}\")\n        rows = [d for d in devices if d.kind == kind]\n        if not rows:\n            print(\"  (none found)\")\n        for d in rows:\n            star = \"*\" if d.is_default else \" \"\n            print(f\" {star}[{d.index:>3}] {d.name}  ({d.channels} ch, {d.rate} Hz)\")\n    print(\"\\n * = current Windows default. Pick the loopback that matches the output \"\n          \"device your call app plays to (e.g. your headphones).\")\n\n\ndef resolve(devices: list[Device], index: int, kind: str) -> Device:\n    \"\"\"Return the device with this index, checking it is the expected kind.\"\"\"\n    for d in devices:\n        if d.index == index:\n            if d.kind != kind:\n                raise ValueError(\n                    f\"Device [{index}] '{d.name}' is a {d.kind} device, not a {kind} device. \"\n                    \"Run with --list-devices to see the right indices.\")\n            return d\n    raise ValueError(f\"No WASAPI {kind} device with index {index}. Run with --list-devices.\")\n",
        "file_path": "/home/claude/repo/livetrans/audio/devices.py"
      },

    {

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Capture one audio device and keep its samples aligned to a shared wall clock.\n\nTwo pieces:\n- CaptureStream: opens a PyAudio callback stream. The callback only time-stamps\n  the buffer and puts it on a queue (never blocks, never does work).\n- ChunkAligner: consumes those buffers in another thread and turns them into a\n  continuous signal that starts at the session's t0. When buffers stop arriving\n  (a dropout, or -- normal for WASAPI loopback -- nothing is playing), the time\n  is filled with zeros and logged as a gap. Because both sources are aligned to\n  the same t0, sample n of the mic and sample n of the loopback refer to the\n  same moment (to within the devices' own latency, typically tens of ms).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport queue\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n# Buffers can arrive late and then in a burst; only treat a hole longer than\n# this as a gap. Shorter jitter is absorbed.\nGAP_TOLERANCE_S = 0.2\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Gap:\n    start_s: float        # seconds since session t0\n    duration_s: float\n    db_before: float      # level just before / after the gap; lets us tell an\n    db_after: float       # idle loopback (silence both sides) from a glitch\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StreamStats:\n    callbacks: int = 0\n    frames: int = 0\n    overflows: int = 0\n    underflows: int = 0\n    first_buffer_s: float | None = None   # when the first buffer arrived, since t0\n    gaps: list[Gap] = field(default_factory=list)\n    filled_s: float = 0.0                  # total zeros inserted inside the recording\n    max_queue: int = 0\n\n\ndef to_db(mean_square: float) -> float:\n    return 10.0 * np.log10(mean_square + 1e-12)\n\n\nclass ChunkAligner:\n    \"\"\"Turns time-stamped int16 buffers into an aligned stream. Pure Python + numpy,\n    so it can be tested without audio hardware.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, rate: int, channels: int, t0: float, sink):\n        self.rate = rate\n        self.channels = channels\n        self.t0 = t0\n        self.sink = sink              # callable(np.ndarray int16, shape (n, channels))\n        self.written = 0              # frames handed to sink, including filled zeros\n        self.stats = StreamStats()\n        self._recent: deque[tuple[float, float, int]] = deque()   # (t, mean_sq, n)\n        self._last_db = -120.0\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    # -- level meter (read from the main thread) --------------------------------\n    def level_db(self, window_s: float = 0.3) -> float:\n        now = time.perf_counter()\n        with self._lock:\n            while self._recent and now - self._recent[0][0] > window_s:\n                self._recent.popleft()\n            if not self._recent:\n                return -120.0\n            num = sum(ms * n for _, ms, n in self._recent)\n            den = sum(n for _, _, n in self._recent)\n        return to_db(num / den)\n\n    def _fill(self, seconds: float) -> None:\n        n = int(round(seconds * self.rate))\n        if n > 0:\n            self.sink(np.zeros((n, self.channels), dtype=np.int16))\n            self.written += n\n\n    def push(self, t_arrival: float, data: bytes, status: int = 0,\n             overflow_flag: int = 2, underflow_flag: int = 1) -> None:\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(data, dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, self.channels)\n        n = pcm.shape[0]\n        st = self.stats\n        st.callbacks += 1\n        st.frames += n\n        if status & overflow_flag:\n            st.overflows += 1\n        if status & underflow_flag:\n            st.underflows += 1\n\n        chunk_start = t_arrival - n / self.rate          # buffer is full when callback fires\n        expected = self.t0 + self.written / self.rate\n        hole = chunk_start - expected\n        ms = float(np.mean((pcm.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0) ** 2)) if n else 0.0\n\n        if st.first_buffer_s is None:\n            st.first_buffer_s = t_arrival - self.t0\n            self._fill(max(hole, 0.0))                   # lead-in: device started late\n        elif hole > GAP_TOLERANCE_S:\n            st.gaps.append(Gap(round(expected - self.t0, 3), round(hole, 3),\n                               round(self._last_db, 1), round(to_db(ms), 1)))\n            st.filled_s += hole\n            self._fill(hole)\n\n        self.sink(pcm)\n        self.written += n\n        self._last_db = to_db(ms)\n        with self._lock:\n            self._recent.append((t_arrival, ms, n))\n\n    def pad_to(self, t_end: float) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pad with zeros up to t_end so all sources end at the same time.\"\"\"\n        self._fill(max(t_end - (self.t0 + self.written / self.rate), 0.0))\n\n\nclass CaptureStream:\n    \"\"\"One PyAudio input stream feeding a ChunkAligner via a worker thread.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, pa, device, t0: float, sink, buffer_s: float = 0.02):\n        import pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio   # imported here so ChunkAligner works without it\n        self._pyaudio = pyaudio\n        self.pa = pa\n        self.device = device\n        self.aligner = ChunkAligner(device.rate, device.channels, t0, sink)\n        self._q: queue.Queue = queue.Queue()\n        self._stop = threading.Event()\n        self._worker = threading.Thread(target=self._drain, daemon=True,\n                                         name=f\"drain-{device.kind}\")\n        self.last_callback = None\n        self.stream = None\n        self.error: str | None = None\n        self._fpb = max(int(device.rate * buffer_s), 64)\n\n    def _callback(self, in_data, frame_count, time_info, status):\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        self.last_callback = t\n        self._q.put((t, in_data, status))\n        return (None, self._pyaudio.paContinue)\n\n    def _drain(self) -> None:\n        pa = self._pyaudio\n        while not (self._stop.is_set() and self._q.empty()):\n            try:\n                t, data, status = self._q.get(timeout=0.1)\n            except queue.Empty:\n                continue\n            self.aligner.stats.max_queue = max(self.aligner.stats.max_queue, self._q.qsize() + 1)\n            try:\n                self.aligner.push(t, data, status, pa.paInputOverflow, pa.paInputUnderflow)\n            except Exception as e:  #         "content": "\"\"\"M0: check a recording made by m0_record.py.\n\n  python tools/m0_check.py recordings/<timestamp>\n\nReports, per guided phase, whether speech landed in the right stream, plus any\ndropouts, buffer overflows, clipping and length mismatches. Prints the report\nand saves it as m0_report.txt next to the recording (text only, no audio).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport wave\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nFRAME_S = 0.05          # level is measured in 50 ms frames\nEDGE_S = 1.5            # ignore the first/last 1.5 s of each phase (people react late)\nACTIVE_ABOVE_FLOOR = 15  # dB above the noise floor counts as \"active\"\nACTIVE_MIN_DB = -60.0   # ...and never below this absolute level\nSPEECH_MIN = 0.30       # a talking phase needs >= 30 % active frames (speech has pauses)\nQUIET_MAX = 0.10        # a quiet phase allows <= 10 % active frames\nIDLE_EDGE_DB = -50.0    # loopback gap with quiet edges = nothing was playing\n\n\ndef load(path: Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"rb\") as w:\n        rate, ch = w.getframerate(), w.getnchannels()\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, ch)\n    return pcm, rate\n\n\ndef frame_db(pcm: np.ndarray, rate: int) -> np.ndarray:\n    mono = pcm.astype(np.float32).mean(axis=1) / 32768.0\n    n = int(rate * FRAME_S)\n    usable = len(mono) // n * n\n    ms = (mono[:usable].reshape(-1, n) ** 2).mean(axis=1)\n    return 10 * np.log10(ms + 1e-12)\n\n\ndef phase_slice(db: np.ndarray, start: float, end: float) -> np.ndarray:\n    a, b = int((start + EDGE_S) / FRAME_S), int((end - EDGE_S) / FRAME_S)\n    return db[a:max(a, b)]\n\n\ndef check(session_dir: Path) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n    meta = json.loads((session_dir / \"session.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    ok = True\n\n    def verdict(passed: bool, warn_only: bool = False) -> str:\n        nonlocal ok\n        if passed:\n            return \"PASS\"\n        if not warn_only:\n            ok = False\n        return \"WARN\" if warn_only else \"FAIL\"\n\n    lines.append(f\"M0 capture check - {session_dir}\")\n    lines.append(f\"Recorded {meta['created']}, wall time {meta['wall_seconds']:.1f} s\")\n    if meta[\"errors\"]:\n        ok = False\n        lines.append(\"Runtime errors: \" + \"; \".join(meta[\"errors\"]))\n\n    db, raw = {}, {}\n    lines.append(\"\\n== Streams ==\")\n    for name in (\"mic\", \"loopback\"):\n        st = meta[\"streams\"][name]\n        pcm, rate = load(session_dir / f\"{name}.wav\")\n        raw[name] = pcm\n        db[name] = frame_db(pcm, rate)\n        dur = len(pcm) / rate\n        clip = float(np.mean(np.abs(pcm.astype(np.int32)) >= 32767)) * 100\n        dev = st[\"device\"]\n        lines.append(f\"{name.upper():9} [{dev['index']}] {dev['name']} ({dev['channels']} ch, {dev['rate']} Hz)\")\n        lines.append(f\"  length {dur:.2f} s vs wall {meta['wall_seconds']:.2f} s  \"\n                     f\"[{verdict(abs(dur - meta['wall_seconds']) < 0.1)}]\")\n        lines.append(f\"  first buffer after {st['first_buffer_s']:.3f} s; \"\n                     f\"{st['callbacks']} buffers; max queue {st['max_queue']}\")\n        lines.append(f\"  input overflows {st['overflows']}  [{verdict(st['overflows'] == 0)}]\")\n        lines.append(f\"  clipped samples {clip:.3f} %  [{verdict(clip < 0.1, warn_only=True)}]\")\n        gaps = st[\"gaps\"]\n        if name == \"mic\":\n            lines.append(f\"  dropouts {len(gaps)} totalling {st['filled_s']:.2f} s  [{verdict(not gaps)}]\")\n            for g in gaps:\n                lines.append(f\"    gap at {g['start_s']:.2f} s for {g['duration_s']:.2f} s\")\n        else:\n            idle = [g for g in gaps if g[\"db_before\"] < IDLE_EDGE_DB and g[\"db_after\"] < IDLE_EDGE_DB]\n            odd = [g for g in gaps if g not in idle]\n            lines.append(f\"  gaps {len(gaps)}: {len(idle)} idle (nothing playing - expected for WASAPI loopback), \"\n                         f\"{len(odd)} during sound  [{verdict(not odd)}]\")\n            for g in odd:\n                lines.append(f\"    gap at {g['start_s']:.2f} s for {g['duration_s']:.2f} s \"\n                             f\"(level before {g['db_before']} dB, after {g['db_after']} dB)\")\n\n    if not meta[\"phases\"]:\n        lines.append(\"\\n(free recording: no phase checks)\")\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines), ok\n\n    quiet_ids = {\"ready\", \"silence\"}\n    floor = {}\n    for name in db:\n        quiet = np.concatenate([phase_slice(db[name], p[\"start\"], p[\"end\"])\n                                for p in meta[\"phases\"] if p[\"id\"] in quiet_ids])\n        floor[name] = float(np.percentile(quiet, 50)) if quiet.size else -90.0\n    thr = {n: max(floor[n] + ACTIVE_ABOVE_FLOOR, ACTIVE_MIN_DB) for n in db}\n\n    expect = {  # phase -> (mic should talk?, loopback should talk?)\n        \"ready\": (False, False), \"me\": (True, False), \"remote\": (False, True),\n        \"both\": (True, True), \"silence\": (False, False),\n    }\n    lines.append(\"\\n== Guided phases ==\")\n    lines.append(f\"noise floor: mic {floor['mic']:.1f} dB, loopback {floor['loopback']:.1f} dB \"\n                 f\"(active = above {thr['mic']:.1f} / {thr['loopback']:.1f} dB)\")\n    lines.append(f\"{'phase':8} {'mic active':>10} {'mic med':>8} {'sys active':>11} {'sys med':>8}  result\")\n    notes = []\n    for p in meta[\"phases\"]:\n        want_mic, want_sys = expect[p[\"id\"]]\n        cells, results = [], []\n        for name, want in ((\"mic\", want_mic), (\"loopback\", want_sys)):\n            seg = phase_slice(db[name], p[\"start\"], p[\"end\"])\n            frac = float(np.mean(seg > thr[name])) if seg.size else 0.0\n            med = float(np.median(seg)) if seg.size else -120.0\n            cells += [f\"{frac * 100:9.0f}%\", f\"{med:8.1f}\"]\n            results.append(frac >= SPEECH_MIN if want else frac <= QUIET_MAX)\n            if not (frac >= SPEECH_MIN if want else frac <= QUIET_MAX):\n                label = \"mic\" if name == \"mic\" else \"system audio\"\n                if want:\n                    notes.append(f\"'{p['id']}': expected speech on {label}, found {frac:.0%} active frames.\")\n                else:\n                    hint = (\" Remote voice may be leaking into the mic (speakers or loud headphones).\"\n                            if name == rem = ph in (\"remote\",\"both\")\n            if name == \"mic\":\n                if mic_dropout and mic_dropout[0] <= t < mic_dropout[1]:\n                    t += n/rate; continue                       # buffers lost\n                x = (speech(ts, rng) if me else 0.001*rng.standard_normal(n)) + (leak*speech(ts+0.1, rng) if rem else 0)\n            else:\n                if not rem: t += n/rate; continue               # WASAPI loopback idle: no buffers at all\n                x = speech(ts+0.2, rng)\n            pcm = np.clip(np.tile(x[:,None], (1,ch))*32767, -32768, 32767).astype(np.int16)\n            jitter = rng.uniform(0, 0.03)\n            al[name].push(t + n/rate + jitter*0, pcm.tobytes())\n            t += n/rate\n    for name in cfg:\n        al[name].pad_to(60.0); wavs[name].close()\n    meta = {\"created\": \"sim\", \"wall_seconds\": 60.0, \"guided\": True, \"errors\": [],\n            \"phases\": [dict(start=a,end=b,id=p,text=\"\") for a,b,p in PH],\n            \"streams\": {name: {\"device\": {\"index\": i, \"name\": f\"fake {name}\", \"kind\": name,\n                                          \"channels\": cfg[name][1], \"rate\": cfg[name][0], \"is_default\": True},\n                               **asdict(al[name].stats), \"written_seconds\": al[name].written/cfg[name][0]}\n                        for i, name in enumerate(cfg)}}\n    (out/\"session.json\").write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2))\n    rep, ok = m0_check.check(out)\n    print(rep); A loopback device is the\n\"recording\" twin of an output device (speakers / headphones), so capturing it\nrecords whatever Windows plays there, e.g. the other side of a call.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nimport pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Device:\n    index: int\n    name: str\n    kind: str          # \"mic\" or \"loopback\"\n    channels: int\n    rate: int\n    is_default: bool\n\n\ndef _wasapi(pa: pyaudio.PyAudio) -> dict:\n    try:\n        return pa.get_host_api_info_by_type(pyaudio.paWASAPI)\n    except OSError as e:  # WASAPI missing would be very unusual on Windows 10/11\n        raise RuntimeError(\"WASAPI host API not available on this system\") from e\n\n\ndef _default_loopback_index(pa: pyaudio.PyAudio, wasapi: dict) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Loopback twin of the current default output device, if found.\"\"\"\n    out_idx = wasapi.get(\"defaultOutputDevice\", -1)\n    if out_idx < 0:\n        return None\n    speakers = pa.get_device_info_by_index(out_idx)\n    if speakers.get(\"isLoopbackDevice\"):\n        return speakers[\"index\"]\n    for lb in pa.get_loopback_device_info_generator():\n        if speakers[\"name\"] in lb[\"name\"]:\n            return lb[\"index\"]\n    return None\n\n\ndef list_devices(pa: pyaudio.PyAudio) -> list[Device]:\n    wasapi = _wasapi(pa)\n    default_mic = wasapi.get(\"defaultInputDevice\", -1)\n    default_lb = _default_loopback_index(pa, wasapi)\n    devices: list[Device] = []\n    for i in range(pa.get_device_count()):\n        info = pa.get_device_info_by_index(i)\n        if info[\"hostApi\"] != wasapi[\"index\"] or info[\"maxInputChannels\"] <= 0:\n            continue\n        is_lb = bool(info.get(\"isLoopbackDevice\"))\n        devices.append(Device(\n            index=info[\"index\"],\n            name=info[\"name\"],\n            kind=\"loopback\" if is_lb else \"mic\",\n            channels=int(info[\"maxInputChannels\"]),\n            rate=int(info[\"defaultSampleRate\"]),\n            is_default=info[\"index\"] == (default_lb if is_lb else default_mic),\n        ))\n    return devices\n\n\ndef print_devices(devices: list[Device]) -> None:\n    for kind, title in ((\"mic\", \"MICROPHONES  (use with --mic)\"),\n                        (\"loopback\", \"SYSTEM AUDIO / LOOPBACK  (use with --loopback)\")):\n        print(f\"\\n{title}\")\n        rows = [d for d in devices if d.kind == kind]\n        if not rows:\n            print(\"  (none found)\")\n        for d in rows:\n            star = \"*\" if d.is_default else \" \"\n            print(f\" {star}[{d.index:>3}] {d.name}  ({d.channels} ch, {d.rate} Hz)\")\n    print(\"\\n * = current Windows default. Pick the loopback that matches the output \"\n          \"device your call app plays to (e.g. your headphones).\")\n\n\ndef resolve(devices: list[Device], index: int, kind: str) -> Device:\n    \"\"\"Return the device with this index, checking it is the expected kind.\"\"\"\n    for d in devices:\n        if d.index == index:\n            if d.kind != kind:\n                raise ValueError(\n                    f\"Device [{index}] '{d.name}' is a {d.kind} device, not a {kind} device. \"\n                    \"Run with --list-devices to see the right indices.\")\n            return d\n    raise ValueError(f\"No WASAPI {kind} device with index {index}. Run with --list-devices.\")\nEOF\nmd5sum .gitignore requirements.txt livetrans/audio/devices.py"

      "input": {
        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && cat > livetrans/audio/capture.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Capture one audio device and keep its samples aligned to a shared wall clock.\n\nTwo pieces:\n- CaptureStream: opens a PyAudio callback stream. The callback only time-stamps\n  the buffer and puts it on a queue (never blocks, never does work).\n- ChunkAligner: consumes those buffers in another thread and turns them into a\n  continuous signal that starts at the session's t0. When buffers stop arriving\n  (a dropout, or -- normal for WASAPI loopback -- nothing is playing), the time\n  is filled with zeros and logged as a gap. Because both sources are aligned to\n  the same t0, sample n of the mic and sample n of the loopback refer to the\n  same moment (to within the devices' own latency, typically tens of ms).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport queue\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n# Buffers can arrive late and then in a burst; only treat a hole longer than\n# this as a gap. Shorter jitter is absorbed.\nGAP_TOLERANCE_S = 0.2\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Gap:\n    start_s: float        # seconds since session t0\n    duration_s: float\n    db_before: float      # level just before / after the gap; lets us tell an\n    db_after: float       # idle loopback (silence both sides) from a glitch\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StreamStats:\n    callbacks: int = 0\n    frames: int = 0\n    overflows: int = 0\n    underflows: int = 0\n    first_buffer_s: float | None = None   # when the first buffer arrived, since t0\n    gaps: list[Gap] = field(default_factory=list)\n    filled_s: float = 0.0                  # total zeros inserted inside the recording\n    max_queue: int = 0\n\n\ndef to_db(mean_square: float) -> float:\n    return 10.0 * np.log10(mean_square + 1e-12)\n\n\nclass ChunkAligner:\n    \"\"\"Turns time-stamped int16 buffers into an aligned stream. Pure Python + numpy,\n    so it can be tested without audio hardware.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, rate: int, channels: int, t0: float, sink):\n        self.rate = rate\n        self.channels = channels\n        self.t0 = t0\n        self.sink = sink              # callable(np.ndarray int16, shape (n, channels))\n        self.written = 0              # frames handed to sink, including filled zeros\n        self.stats = StreamStats()\n        self._recent: deque[tuple[float, float, int]] = deque()   # (t, mean_sq, n)\n        self._last_db = -120.0\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    # -- level meter (read from the main thread) --------------------------------\n    def level_db(self, window_s: float = 0.3) -> float:\n        now = time.perf_counter()\n        with self._lock:\n            while self._recent and now - self._recent[0][0] > window_s:\n                self._recent.popleft()\n            if not self._recent:\n                return -120.0\n            num = sum(ms * n for _, ms, n in self._recent)\n            den = sum(n for _, _, n in self._recent)\n        return to_db(num / den)\n\n    def _fill(self, seconds: float) -> None:\n        n = int(round(seconds * self.rate))\n        if n > 0:\n            self.sink(np.zeros((n, self.channels), dtype=np.int16))\n            self.written += n\n\n    def push(self, t_arrival: float, data: bytes, status: int = 0,\n             overflow_flag: int = 2, underflow_flag: int = 1) -> None:\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(data, dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, self.channels)\n        n = pcm.shape[0]\n        st = self.stats\n        st.callbacks += 1\n        st.frames += n\n        if status & overflow_flag:\n            st.overflows += 1\n        if status & underflow_flag:\n            st.underflows += 1\n\n        chunk_start = t_arrival - n / self.rate          # buffer is full when callback fires\n        expected = self.t0 + self.written / self.rate\n        hole = chunk_start - expected\n        ms = float(np.mean((pcm.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0) ** 2)) if n else 0.0\n\n        if st.first_buffer_s is None:\n            st.first_buffer_s = t_arrival - self.t0\n            self._fill(max(hole, 0.0))                   # lead-in: device started late\n        elif hole > GAP_TOLERANCE_S:\n            st.gaps.append(Gap(round(expected - self.t0, 3), round(hole, 3),\n                               round(self._last_db, 1), round(to_db(ms), 1)))\n            st.filled_s += hole\n            self._fill(hole)\n\n        self.sink(pcm)\n        self.written += n\n        self._last_db = to_db(ms)\n        with self._lock:\n            self._recent.append((t_arrival, ms, n))\n\n    def pad_to(self, t_end: float) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pad with zeros up to t_end so all sources end at the same time.\"\"\"\n        self._fill(max(t_end - (self.t0 + self.written / self.rate), 0.0))\n\n\nclass CaptureStream:\n    \"\"\"One PyAudio input stream feeding a ChunkAligner via a worker thread.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, pa, device, t0: float, sink, buffer_s: float = 0.02):\n        import pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio   # imported here so ChunkAligner works without it\n        self._pyaudio = pyaudio\n        self.pa = pa\n        self.device = device\n        self.aligner = ChunkAligner(device.rate, device.channels, t0, sink)\n        self._q: queue.Queue = queue.Queue()\n        self._stop = threading.Event()\n        self._worker = threading.Thread(target=self._drain, daemon=True,\n                                         name=f\"drain-{device.kind}\")\n        self.last_callback = None\n        self.stream = None\n        self.error: str | None = None\n        self._fpb = max(int(device.rate * buffer_s), 64)\n\n    def _callback(self, in_data, frame_count, time_info, status):\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        self.last_callback = t\n        self._q.put((t, in_data, status))\n        return (None, self._pyaudio.paContinue)\n\n    def _drain(self) -> None:\n        pa = self._pyaudio\n        while not (self._stop.is_set() and self._q.empty()):\n            try:\n                t, data, status = self._q.get(timeout=0.1)\n            except queue.Empty:\n                continue\n            self.aligner.stats.max_queue = max(self.aligner.stats.max_queue, self._q.qsize() + 1)\n            try:\n                self.aligner.push(t, data, status, pa.paInputOverflow, pa.paInputUnderflow)\n            except Exception as e:  # never let a bad buffer kill the thread silently\n                self.error = f\"{type(e).__name__}: {e}\"\n\n    def start(self) -> None:\n        self.stream = self.pa.open(\n            format=self._pyaudio.paInt16,\n            channels=self.device.channels,\n            rate=self.device.rate,\n            input=True,\n            input_device_index=self.device.index,\n            frames_per_buffer=self._fpb,\n            stream_callback=self._callback,\n        )\n        self._worker.start()\n\n    def is_active(self) -> bool:\n        try:\n            return bool(self.stream and self.stream.is_active())\n        except OSError:\n            return False\n\n    def stop(self) -> None:\n        if self.stream is not None:\n            try:\n                self.stream.stop_stream()\n                self.stream.close()\n            except OSError as e:          # e.g. device unplugged mid-session\n                self.error = self.error or f\"close failed: {e}\"\n        self._stop.set()\n        if self._worker.is_alive():\n            self._worker.join(timeout=5)\nEOF\nmd5sum livetrans/audio/capture.py"

        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && cat > tools/m0_record.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"M0: record the microphone and the system audio (WASAPI loopback) at the same time.\n\n  python tools/m0_record.py --list-devices\n  python tools/m0_record.py --mic <N> --loopback <M> --guided      # 60 s scripted test\n  python tools/m0_record.py --mic <N> --loopback <M> --seconds 30  # free recording\n\nBoth devices must be chosen explicitly; nothing is picked silently.\nWrites recordings/<timestamp>/{mic.wav, loopback.wav, session.json}.\nAudio recordings stay local: recordings/ is git-ignored.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport time\nimport wave\nfrom dataclasses import asdict\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\n\nimport pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio  # noqa: E402\n\nfrom livetrans.audio.capture import CaptureStream  # noqa: E402\nfrom livetrans.audio.devices import list_devices, print_devices, resolve  # noqa: E402\n\n# Guided test script: (start_s, end_s, phase_id, instruction)\nPHASES = [\n    (0, 5, \"ready\", \"SILENCE - nobody speaks (measuring background noise)\"),\n    (5, 20, \"me\", \"ME only - you talk, remote person stays silent\"),\n    (20, 35, \"remote\", \"REMOTE only - signal them to start; you stay silent\"),\n    (35, 50, \"both\", \"BOTH at once - you start talking too, they keep talking\"),\n    (50, 60, \"silence\", \"SILENCE - signal them to stop; nobody speaks\"),\n]\nMIC_STALL_S = \"#\" * filled + \".\" * (width - filled)\n\n\ndef open_wav(path: Path, dev) -> wave.Wave_write:\n    w = wave.open(str(path), \"wb\")\n    w.setnchannels(dev.channels)\n    w.setsampwidth(2)\n Prints the report\nand saves it as m0_report.txt next to the recording (text only, no audio).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport wave\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nFRAME_S = 0.05          # level is measured in 50 ms frames\nEDGE_S = 1.5            # ignore the first/last 1.5 s of each phase (people react late)\nACTIVE_ABOVE_FLOOR = 15  # dB above the noise floor counts as \"active\"\nACTIVE_MIN_DB = -60.0   # ...and never below this absolute level\nSPEECH_MIN = 0.30       # a talking phase needs >= 30 % active frames (speech has pauses)\nQUIET_MAX = 0.10        # a quiet phase allows <= 10 % active frames\nIDLE_EDGE_DB = -50.0    # loopback gap with quiet edges = nothing was playing\n\n\ndef load(path: Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"rb\") as w:\n        rate, ch = w.getframerate(), w.getnchannels()\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, ch)\n    return pcm, rate\n\n\ndef frame_db(pcm: np.ndarray, rate: int) -> np.ndarray:\n    mono = pcm.astype(np.float32).mean(axis=1) / 32768.0\n    n = int(rate * FRAME_S)\n    usable = len(mono) // n * n\n    ms = (mono[:usable].reshape(-1, n) ** 2).mean(axis=1)\n    return 10 * np.log10(ms + 1e-12)\n\n\ndef phase_slice(db: np.ndarray, start: float, end: float) -> np.ndarray:\n    a, b = int((start + EDGE_S) / FRAME_S), int((end - EDGE_S) / FRAME_S)\n    return db[a:max(a, b)]\n\n\ndef check(session_dir: Path) -> tuple[str, bool]:\n    meta = json.loads((session_dir / \"session.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    ok = True\n\n    def verdict(passed: bool, warn_only: bool = False) -> str:\n        nonlocal ok\n        if passed:\n            return \"PASS\"\n        if not warn_only:\n            ok = False\n        return \"WARN\" if warn_only else \"FAIL\"\n\n    lines.append(f\"M0 capture check - {session_dir}\")\n    lines.append(f\"Recorded {meta['created']}, wall time {meta['wall_seconds']:.1f} s\")\n    if meta[\"errors\"]:\n        ok = False\n        lines.append(\"Runtime errors: \" + \"; \".join(meta[\"errors\"]))\n\n    db, raw = {}, {}\n    lines.append(\"\\n== Streams ==\")\n    for name in (\"mic\", \"loopback\"):\n        st = meta[\"streams\"][name]\n        pcm, rate = load(session_dir / f\"{name}.wav\")\n        raw[name] = pcm\n        db[name] = frame_db(pcm, rate)\n        dur = len(pcm) / rate\n        clip = float(np.mean(np.abs(pcm.astype(np.int32)) >= 32767)) * 100\n        dev = st[\"device\"]\n        lines.append(f\"{name.upper():9} [{dev['index']}] {dev['name']} ({dev['channels']} ch, {dev['rate']} Hz)\")\n        lines.append(f\"  length {dur:.2f} s vs wall {meta['wall_seconds']:.2f} s  \"\n                     f\"[{verdict(abs(dur - meta['wall_seconds']) < 0.1)}]\")\n        lines.append(f\"  first buffer after {st['first_buffer_s']:.3f} s; \"\n                     f\"{st['callbacks']} buffers; max queue {st['max_queue']}\")\n        lines.append(f\"  input overflows {st['overflows']}  [{verdict(st['overflows'] == 0)}]\")\n        lines.append(f\"  clipped samples {clip:.3f} %  [{verdict(clip < 0.1, warn_only=True)}]\")\n        gaps = st[\"gaps\"]\n        if name == \"mic\":\n            lines.append(f\"  dropouts {len(gaps)} totalling {st['filled_s']:.2f} s  [{verdict(not gaps)}]\")\n            for g in gaps:\n                lines.append(f\"    gap at {g['start_s']:.2f} s for {g['duration_s']:.2f} s\")\n        else:\n            idle = [g for g in gaps if g[\"db_before\"] < IDLE_EDGE_DB and g[\"db_after\"] < IDLE_EDGE_DB]\n            odd = [g for g in gaps if g not in idle]\n            lines.append(f\"  gaps {len(gaps)}: {len(idle)} idle (nothing playing - expected for WASAPI loopback), \"\n                         f\"{len(odd)} during sound  [{verdict(not odd)}]\")\n            for g in odd:\n                lines.append(f\"    gap at {g['start_s']:.2f} s for {g['duration_s']:.2f} s \"\n                             f\"(level before {g['db_before']} dB, after {g['db_after']} dB)\")\n\n    if not meta[\"phases\"]:\n        lines.append(\"\\n(free recording: no phase checks)\")\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines), ok\n\n    quiet_ids = {\"ready\", \"silence\"}\n    floor = {}\n    for name in db:\n        quiet = np.concatenate([phase_slice(db[name], p[\"start\"], p[\"end\"])\n                                for p in meta[\"phases\"] if p[\"id\"] in quiet_ids])\n        floor[name] = float(np.percentile(quiet, 50)) if quiet.size else -90.0\n    thr = {n: max(floor[n] + ACTIVE_ABOVE_FLOOR, ACTIVE_MIN_DB) for n in db}\n\n    expect = {  # phase -> (mic should talk?, loopback should talk?)\n        \"ready\": (False, False), \"me\": (True, False), \"remote\": (False, True),\n        \"both\": (True, True), \"silence\": (False, False),\n    }\n    lines.append(\"\\n== Guided phases ==\")\n    lines.append(f\"noise floor: mic {floor['mic']:.1f} dB, loopback {floor['loopback']:.1f} dB \"\n                 f\"(active = above {thr['mic']:.1f} / {thr['loopback']:.1f} dB)\")\n    lines.append(f\"{'phase':8} {'mic active':>10} {'mic med':>8} {'sys active':>11} {'sys med':>8}  result\")\n    notes = []\n    for p in meta[\"phases\"]:\n        want_mic, want_sys = expect[p[\"id\"]]\n        cells, results = [], []\n        for name, want in ((\"mic\", want_mic), (\"loopback\", want_sys)):\n            seg = phase_slice(db[name], p[\"start\"], p[\"end\"])\n            frac = float(np.mean(seg > thr[name])) if seg.size else 0.0\n            med = float(np.median(seg)) if seg.size else -120.0\n            cells += [f\"{frac * 100:9.0f}%\", f\"{med:8.1f}\"]\n            results.append(frac >= SPEECH_MIN if want else frac <= QUIET_MAX)\n            if not (frac >= SPEECH_MIN if want else frac <= QUIET_MAX):\n                label = \"mic\" if name == \"mic\" else \"system audio\"\n                if want:\n                    notes.append(f\"'{p['id']}': expected speech on {label}, found {frac:.0%} active frames.\")\n                else:\n                    hint = (\" Remote voice may be leaking into the mic (speakers or loud headphones).\"\n                            if name == \"mic\" and p[\"id\"] == \"remote\" else \"\")\n                    notes.append(f\"'{p['id']}': expected quiet {label}, found {frac:.0%} active frames.{hint}\")\n        lines.append(f\"{p['id']:8} {cells[0]:>10} {cells[1]} {cells[2]:>11} {cells[3]}  \"\n                     f\"[{verdict(all(results))}]\")\n    lines += [f\"  - {n}\" for n in notes]\n\n    lines.append(f\"\\nOVERALL: {'PASS' if ok else 'NEEDS ATTENTION'}\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines), ok\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    if len(sys.argv) != 2:\n        print(__doc__)\n        return 2\n    d = Path(sys.argv[1])\n    report, ok = check(d)\n    print(report)\n    (d / \"m0_report.txt\").write_text(report + \"\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return 0 if ok else 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\nEOF\nmd5sum tools/m0_check.py; find . -type f | sort"

      "text": "The M0 code is in a new folder on your laptop, `GitHub\\live-armenian-translation`, and I checked every file against the version I tested. I haven't installed or run anything on your machine. I can't run it for you either, because my shell there can't reach Windows audio devices, so the steps below are for you.\n\n## What was built\n- `tools\\m0_record.py` lists your devices and records the mic and system audio to two WAV files.\n  - It refuses to start unless you pass both `--mic` and `--loopback`.\n  - In `--guided` mode it runs a 60-second test script with live level meters for both streams.\n- `tools\\m0_check.py` analyses a recording and writes `m0_report.txt` with PASS or FAIL for each check:\n  - whether speech landed in the right stream in each phase, including the overlap phase;\n  - mic dropouts, buffer overflows, clipping, file length against the clock;\n  - remote voice leaking into the mic.\n- Both streams are aligned to one shared clock, so second 30 in one file is second 30 in the other.\n- I tested the logic here with simulated audio. A clean run passes. Injected faults are caught: a 0.6 s mic dropout and remote voice leaking into the mic.\n\n**One Windows behaviour to know about:** the loopback stream sends nothing while no sound is playing. The recorder fills those stretches with silence and the checker labels them \"idle\", so they don't count as dropouts. A hole while sound is playing does count, and gets flagged.\n\n## Installations (please read before running)\nEverything goes into a `.venv` folder inside the project. It doesn't touch Anaconda or system Python, and deleting `.venv` undoes it. No admin rights, drivers or virtual cable are needed, because Windows' built-in WASAPI loopback does the job BlackHole does on a Mac.\n- **PyAudioWPatch**: a version of the standard audio library (PortAudio) that can record from output devices. It's a small prebuilt Windows package under the MIT licence.\n- **numpy**: for the level meters and the analysis.\n\nIn PowerShell:\n```\ncd $HOME\\GitHub\\live-armenian-translation\npython --version\npython -m venv .venv\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1\npython -m pip install -r requirements.txt\npython tools\\m0_record.py --list-devices\n```\nYou need Python 3.10–3.13. If `Activate.ps1` is blocked, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass` first; it only applies to that window. Send me the device list if you'd like a second opinion on which indices to pick.\n\n## Google Meet test with headphones\n1. **Setup.**\n   - In Windows sound settings and in Meet's audio settings, set the output to your headphones and the microphone to the one you'll pass with `--mic`.\n   - Wired headphones are best. With Bluetooth, using the headset's own mic switches it into a low-quality \"Hands-Free\" mode, and the loopback then has to be that \"Headset\" device.\n   - The remote person must be on another device **in another room**, or their voice reaches your mic through the air.\n2. **Agree on a signal beforehand.** When you wave, they start talking and keep going for about 30 seconds until you wave again. Reading any text aloud works.\n3. **Run:** `python tools\\m0_record.py --mic N --loopback M --guided` and follow the cues on screen:\n   - 0–5 s: silence\n   - 5–20 s: you talk\n   - at 20 s: you wave; they talk and you stay silent\n   - 35–50 s: you start talking too, so both of you talk at once\n   - at 50 s: you wave; they stop\n   - 50–60 s: silence\n\n   While it runs, the MIC bar should move only for your voice and the SYS bar only for theirs.\n4. **Check:** `python tools\\m0_check.py recordings\\<folder it printed>`\n\nThen tell me it's done.
