## Message 8 — assistant — 10/30/2026 15:20:14


```
This block is not supported on your current device yet.
```

Mostly yes. The device detection works and your `.venv` is intact: I checked inside it and both packages are there. Two things need fixing before the Meet test, and the second one matters.

**1. One package also went outside the venv.** Activation was blocked, so the second `pip install` used your global Python. That put a copy of PyAudioWPatch (100 kB) in your user folder. It's harmless, but it isn't the isolated setup I described. To remove it, run `python -m pip uninstall PyAudioWPatch` and leave numpy alone, since it was already there. From now on, skip activation and call the venv's Python directly, as you did in your first two commands. Better still, select `.venv` as the interpreter in VS Code (Ctrl+Shift+P, then "Python: Select Interpreter").

**2. Don't use the Buds as the microphone.** Device `[15] Headset (Buds3 Pro), 1 ch, 16000 Hz` is Bluetooth's hands-free mode. When any app opens that mic, Windows switches the Buds out of the normal "Headphones" mode. Meet's audio then plays through a different "Headset" device, and loopback `[16]` would likely record silence. That's exactly the "remote voice missing" failure you want to catch, so avoid it by design. Use:

- **mic `[14]`**, the laptop's built-in Microphone Array;
- **loopback `[16]`**, the Buds in "Headphones" mode.

In-ear Buds should leak very little sound into the laptop mic, and the overlap phase of the test will confirm that.

**In Meet** (Settings → Audio), set:
- Microphone: Microphone Array (Intel Smart Sound…)
- Speakers: Headphones (Sarkis's Buds3 Pro)

Your Windows default mic is currently the Buds, so Meet may pick it automatically. Check this setting.

**Then run step 3:**
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\m0_record.py --list-devices
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\m0_record.py --mic 14 --loopback 16 --guided
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\m0_check.py recordings\<folder it prints>
```
Re-list the devices right before recording. Indices can change when the Buds reconnect.

If the live SYS meter stays flat while the other person is talking, stop with Ctrl+C and tell me. That would mean the Buds switched modes anyway. Otherwise, tell me when the check finishes and I'll read the report from the folder.

**What passed**
- **Separation:** your voice is only in the mic stream, and the remote voice is only in the system-audio stream.
- **No leakage from the Buds:** while the remote person talked alone (21–30 s), the mic stayed at its background level of about −75 dB.
- **Overlap:** you really talked over each other from about 33 to 43 s. Both streams stayed at full speech level (−16 to −22 dB), and Meet didn't turn the remote voice down while you spoke. During that stretch, when your mic was active the remote stream was active 56% of the time. That matches normal pauses in speech, not suppression.
- **No capture errors:** no mic dropouts, no buffer overflows, no clipping, and no runtime errors. The queue never held more than one buffer, so the recorder kept up easily.
- **Loopback never went idle:** Meet keeps the output open with a near-silent signal (about −99 dB), so the "no data while silent" case never came up.

**One item flagged: the loopback file is about 0.1 s too long**
The system-audio stream delivered about 0.1 s more audio than the time that actually passed (60.11 s against 60.01 s). That's far too much for normal clock drift. My guess is a burst of already-buffered audio when the stream starts, which would put the remote side about 100 ms late relative to your mic. For this project that's harmless: each stream is transcribed separately, and 100 ms is invisible on a 5-second budget. I haven't proven the cause, though. Next step: log each buffer's arrival time so one short recording shows whether this is a one-off startup burst or steady drift, and fix the alignment to match.

**A note on the test itself**
The real timeline drifted from the on-screen script. Overlap was 33–43 s rather than 35–50 s, and the remote person stopped early. The phase checks still passed, but only with some luck. The checker should detect when each stream is actually active instead of trusting the script's timing, and I'll make that change alongside the logging fix.

**Not tested yet:** playing through laptop speakers instead of headphones, and unplugging or switching a device mid-recording. Both are in the M0 plan. The speaker test is quick and tells us how much call audio leaks into your mic if you don't wear the Buds at the interview.

That's far too much for normal clock drift. My guess is a burst of already-buffered audio when the stream starts, which would put the remote side about 100 ms late relative to your mic. For this project that's harmless: each stream is transcribed separately, and 100 ms is invisible on a 5-second budget. I haven't proven the cause, though. Next step: log each buffer's arrival time so one short recording shows whether this is a one-off startup burst or steady drift, and fix the alignment to match.\n\n**A note on the test itself**\nThe real timeline drifted from the on-screen script. Overlap was 33–43 s rather than 35–50 s, and the remote person stopped early. The phase checks still passed, but only with some luck. The checker should detect when each stream is actually active instead of trusting the script's timing, and I'll make that change alongside the logging fix.\n\n**Not tested yet:** playing through laptop speakers instead of headphones, and unplugging or switching a device mid-recording. Both are in the M0 plan. The speaker test is quick and tells us how much call audio leaks into your mic if you don't wear the Buds at the interview.\n\nShould I make the two small fixes (buffer timing log, overlap detection from the actual audio) and then run the speaker and unplug tests, or move on to M1?",

The M1 files are on your laptop, and I checked each one against what I tested here. I couldn't run anything with the real models, because neither my workspace nor the shell on your laptop can reach Hugging Face. To catch my own mistakes, I dry-ran every script here with stand-in models and fake FLEURS files. That found and fixed one real bug: the way I stripped punctuation split words like «ինչպե՞ս» in two, which would have inflated the error rates.

**What M1 measures, all on your laptop**
- **Speech recognition:** word and character error rates, processing time per clip and peak memory, on 100 FLEURS sentences read by Eastern Armenian speakers.
- **Your own voice:** you read 15 of the **same** sentences, so your Western-influenced pronunciation is compared with the FLEURS speakers on identical text.
- **Translation:** quality (chrF and BLEU scores) and time per sentence, from two kinds of input:
  - the correct Armenian text;
  - the speech recogniser's output, which is the realistic case.

  Each runs with beam search at sizes 1 and 4. Beam size trades speed for quality.

**Installations (into `.venv` only, no PyTorch)**
- `onnx-asr`: runs the speech model. It also brings ONNX Runtime (Microsoft's CPU inference engine) and `huggingface_hub` for downloads.
- `ctranslate2` and `sentencepiece`: run the translation model and its tokenizer.
- `soxr`: converts your mic's 48 kHz audio to the 16 kHz the model needs.
- Evaluation only: `jiwer` (error rates), `sacrebleu` (translation scores), `psutil` (memory).

**Downloads (about 1.3 GB plus the FLEURS archive)** go into `models\` and `data\`, which git ignores:
- the speech model (~460 MB);
- the translation model, int8 NLLB-600M (~620 MB).

One caveat about the translation model: it's a third-party int8 conversion. The tokenizer comes from Meta's official repo, and the quality score will show whether the conversion is sound.

If a download gets interrupted, delete the half-filled model folder before rerunning. onnx-asr treats an existing folder as complete.

**Run in this order** (plugged in, Windows power mode on "Best performance", since timings depend on it):
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\m1_fetch.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\m1_bench_asr.py --set fleurs
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\m1_bench_mt.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\m1_record_reading.py --mic 14 --n 15
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\m1_bench_asr.py --set own
```
For the reading step, read the way you normally speak and don't adjust your accent. That's the whole point of the test. It takes about 10 minutes.

You can stop after any step and tell me. I'll read the result files in `results\` directly. If something errors, paste the last few lines of output.

      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Armenian speech -> Armenian text.\n\nModel: NVIDIA FastConformer-Hybrid Large (hy), 115M params, exported to ONNX\n(CTC head) by OpenVoiceOS and run with onnx-asr + ONNX Runtime on CPU.\nNo NeMo / PyTorch needed. The model is non-streaming: we call it once per\nspeech segment (one VAD segment = one call).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nASR_REPO = \"OpenVoiceOS/stt_hy_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc_onnx\"\nSAMPLE_RATE = 16_000\n\n\nclass Transcriber:\n    def __init__(self, model_dir: str | Path = \"models/asr-hy-fastconformer\", threads: int | None = None):\n        import onnx_asr\n        import onnxruntime as rt\n\n        opts = None\n        if threads:\n            opts = rt.SessionOptions()\n            opts.intra_op_num_threads = threads\n        # onnx-asr reads the model from model_dir, downloading it there first if missing\n        self.model = onnx_asr.load_model(ASR_REPO, path=Path(model_dir), sess_options=opts,\n                                         providers=[\"CPUExecutionProvider\"])\n\n    def transcribe(self, audio: np.ndarray) -> str:\n        \"\"\"audio: mono float32 in [-1, 1] at 16 kHz.\"\"\"\n        if audio.dtype != np.float32:\n            audio = audio.astype(np.float32)\n        return self.model.recognize(audio, sample_rate=SAMPLE_RATE).strip()\n",
        "file_path": "/home/claude/repo/livetrans/asr.py"
      },

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Armenian text -> English text.\n\nModel: NLLB-200 distilled 600M (Meta), int8 CTranslate2 conversion, on CPU.\nTokenisation uses NLLB's own SentencePiece model directly (no `transformers`).\nLicence note: NLLB-200 weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nNLLB_CT2_REPO = \"JustFrederik/nllb-200-distilled-600M-ct2-int8\"   # third-party int8 conversion\nNLLB_SPM_REPO = \"facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M\"                # official tokenizer file\nSPM_FILE = \"sentencepiece.bpe.model\"\nSRC, TGT = \"hye_Armn\", \"eng_Latn\"\n\n\nclass Translator:\n    def __init__(self, model_dir: str | Path = \"models/mt-nllb-600m-int8\", threads: int = 4,\n                 beam_size: int = 4):\n        import ctranslate2\n        import sentencepiece as spm\n\n        model_dir = Path(model_dir)\n        self.translator = ctranslate2.Translator(str(model_dir), device=\"cpu\", compute_type=\"int8\",\n                                                 intra_threads=threads)\n        self.sp = spm.SentencePieceProcessor(model_file=str(model_dir / SPM_FILE))\n        self.beam_size = beam_size\n\n    def translate_batch(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n        sources = [[SRC] + self.sp.encode(t, out_type=str) + [\"</s>\"] for t in texts]\n        results = self.translator.translate_batch(\n            sources, target_prefix=[[TGT]] * len(texts), beam_size=self.beam_size,\n            max_decoding_length=256, repetition_penalty=1.1)\n        out = []\n        for r in results:\n            tokens = r.hypotheses[0]\n            if tokens and tokens[0] == TGT:\n                tokens = tokens[1:]\n            out.append(self.sp.decode(tokens).strip())\n        return out\n\n    def translate(self, text: str) -> str:\n        if not text.strip():\n            return \"\"\n        return self.translate_batch([text])[0]\n\n\ndef download(model_dir: str | Path = \"models/mt-nllb-600m-int8\") -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Fetch the CT2 model and the official SentencePiece model into model_dir.\"\"\"\n    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download, snapshot_download\n\n    model_dir = Path(model_dir)\n    snapshot_download(NLLB_CT2_REPO, local_dir=model_dir)\n    hf_hub_download(NLLB_SPM_REPO, SPM_FILE, local_dir=model_dir)\n    return model_dir\n",
        "file_path": "/home/claude/repo/livetrans/translate.py"
      },

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Shared helpers for the M1 benchmarks (evaluation only, not used at runtime).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nimport wave\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nDATA = ROOT / \"data\"\nRESULTS = ROOT / \"results\"\n\n\ndef normalize_hy(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalisation for WER/CER: case, punctuation and the եւ/և spelling variant\n    are not counted as errors (the model emits punctuation; FLEURS raw text has it).\"\"\"\n    t = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFC\", text).lower()\n    t = t.replace(\"եւ\", \"և\")\n    t = \"\".join(\" \" if unicodedata.category(c).startswith(\"P\") else c for c in t)\n    return re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", t).strip()\n\n\ndef read_wav_16k_mono(path: Path) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Read a 16-bit PCM WAV, downmix to mono, resample to 16 kHz if needed.\"\"\"\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"rb\") as w:\n        rate, ch = w.getframerate(), w.getnchannels()\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, ch)\n    audio = pcm.astype(np.float32).mean(axis=1) / 32768.0\n    if rate != 16_000:\n        import soxr\n        audio = soxr.resample(audio, rate, 16_000).astype(np.float32)\n    return audio\n\n\ndef write_wav_16k_mono(path: Path, audio: np.ndarray) -> None:\n    pcm = np.clip(audio * 32767, -32768, 32767).astype(np.int16)\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"wb\") as w:\n        w.setnchannels(1)\n        w.setsampwidth(2)\n        w.setframerate(16_000)\n        w.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())\n\n\ndef read_jsonl(path: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines() if line.strip()]\n\n\ndef write_jsonl(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> None:\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    path.write_text(\"\".join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\" for r in rows), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef peak_ram_mb() -> float:\n    \"\"\"Peak working set on Windows; current RSS elsewhere.\"\"\"\n    import psutil\n    mi = psutil.Process().memory_info()\n    return round(getattr(mi, \"peak_wset\", mi.rss) / 2**20, 1)\n\n\ndef machine_info() -> dict:\n    import os\n    import platform\n    import psutil\n    return {\"cpu\": platform.processor(), \"logical_cores\": os.cpu_count(),\n            \"physical_cores\": psutil.cpu_count(logical=False),\n            \"ram_gb\": round(psutil.virtual_memory().total / 2**30, 1), \"os\": platform.platform()}\n",

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"M1 step 1: download the models and a FLEURS test subset (one-time, ~1.3 GB).\n\n  python tools/m1_fetch.py            # models + 100 FLEURS hy_am test clips\n  python tools/m1_fetch.py --n 50\n\nEverything lands in models/ and data/, both git-ignored.\nFLEURS (CC-BY-4.0) sentences are FLORES sentences, so the same IDs in the\nen_us split give English reference translations for the MT benchmark.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport random\nimport sys\nimport tarfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))\n\nfrom m1_common import DATA, ROOT, write_jsonl  # noqa: E402\n\nFLEURS = \"google/fleurs\"\n\n\ndef find(files: list[str], lang: str, suffix: str) -> str:\n    hits = [f for f in files if f\"/{lang}/\" in f and f.endswith(suffix)]\n    if not hits:\n        raise SystemExit(f\"Could not find '{suffix}' for {lang} in {FLEURS}; repo layout changed?\")\n    return hits[0]\n\n\ndef parse_tsv(path: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    rows = []\n    with open(path, encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as f:\n        for parts in csv.reader(f, delimiter=\"\\t\", quoting=csv.QUOTE_NONE):\n            wav = next((p for p in parts if p.endswith(\".wav\")), None)\n            if not wav:\n                continue\n            i = parts.index(wav)\n            rows.append({\"id\": parts[0], \"file\": wav, \"raw\": parts[i + 1], \"gender\": parts[-1]})\n    return rows\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--n\", type=int, default=100, help=\"number of FLEURS clips (unique sentences)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--seed\", type=int, default=0)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--skip-models\", action=\"store_true\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    from huggingface_hub import HfApi, hf_hub_download\n\n    if not args.skip_models:\n        print(\"1/3 ASR model (FastConformer hy, ONNX, ~460 MB)...\")\n        from livetrans.asr import Transcriber\n        Transcriber(ROOT / \"models/asr-hy-fastconformer\")       # downloads on first load\n        print(\"2/3 MT model (NLLB-200 600M int8, ~620 MB)...\")\n        from livetrans.translate import download\n        download(ROOT / \"models/mt-nllb-600m-int8\")\n\n    print(\"3/3 FLEURS test split (hy_am audio + text, en_us text)...\")\n    raw_dir = DATA / \"fleurs_raw\"\n    files = HfApi().list_repo_files(FLEURS, repo_type=\"dataset\")\n    hy_tsv = Path(hf_hub_download(FLEURS, find(files, \"hy_am\", \"test.tsv\"), repo_type=\"dataset\", local_dir=raw_dir))\n    en_tsv = Path(hf_hub_download(FLEURS, find(files, \"en_us\", \"test.tsv\"), repo_type=\"dataset\", local_dir=raw_dir))\n    hy, en = parse_tsv(hy_tsv), parse_tsv(en_tsv)\n    en_by_id = {r[\"id\"]: r[\"raw\"] for r in en}\n\n    # one clip per sentence id, only ids that also have an English reference\n    seen, candidates = set(), []\n    for r in hy:\n        if r[\"id\"] in en_by_id and r[\"id\"] not in seen:\n            seen.add(r[\"id\"])\n            candidates.append(r)\n    random.Random(args.seed).shuffle(candidates)\n    chosen = {r[\"file\"]: r for r in candidates[: args.n]}\n    print(f\"   {len(hy)} hy_am test clips, {len(candidates)} usable sentences, taking {len(chosen)}\")\n\n    tar_path = Path(hf_hub_download(FLEURS, find(files, \"hy_am\", \"test.tar.gz\"), repo_type=\"dataset\",\n                                    local_dir=raw_dir))\n    out_dir = DATA / \"fleurs_hy\"\n    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    found = 0\n    with tarfile.open(tar_path, \"r:gz\") as tar:\n        for member in tar:\n            name = Path(member.name).name\n            if member.isfile() and name in chosen:\n                (out_dir / name).write_bytes(tar.extractfile(member).read())\n                found += 1\n    rows = [{\"id\": r[\"id\"], \"wav\": f\"fleurs_hy/{r['file']}\", \"ref_hy\": r[\"raw\"],\n             \"ref_en\": en_by_id[r[\"id\"]], \"gender\": r[\"gender\"]}\n            for r in chosen.values() if (out_dir / r[\"file\"]).exists()]\n    write_jsonl(DATA / \"fleurs_hy.jsonl\", rows)\n    print(f\"   extracted {found} clips -> {out_dir}; manifest data/fleurs_hy.jsonl ({len(rows)} rows)\")\n    print(\"Done. Next: python tools/m1_bench_asr.py --set fleurs\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"M1 step 2: ASR accuracy, speed and memory on this machine.\n\n  python tools/m1_bench_asr.py --set fleurs          # FLEURS Eastern Armenian read speech\n  python tools/m1_bench_asr.py --set own             # your own read sentences (m1_record_reading.py)\n  python tools/m1_bench_asr.py --set fleurs --threads 2\n\nWrites results/m1_asr_<set>.jsonl (per clip) and results/m1_asr_<set>_summary.json.\nWER/CER use normalised text (no case/punctuation); see m1_common.normalize_hy.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))\n\nfrom m1_common import DATA, RESULTS, ROOT, machine_info, normalize_hy, peak_ram_mb, read_jsonl, \\\n    read_wav_16k_mono, write_jsonl  # noqa: E402\n\nMANIFESTS = {\"fleurs\": DATA / \"fleurs_hy.jsonl\", \"own\": DATA / \"own_reading.jsonl\"}\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--set\", choices=sorted(MANIFESTS), default=\"fleurs\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--threads\", type=int, default=None, help=\"ONNX Runtime threads (default: runtime decides)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--limit\", type=int, default=None)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    import jiwer\n    from livetrans.asr import Transcriber\n\n    rows = read_jsonl(MANIFESTS[args.set])[: args.limit]\n    ram_before = peak_ram_mb()\n    t = time.perf_counter()\n    asr = Transcriber(ROOT / \"models/asr-hy-fastconformer\", threads=args.threads)\n    load_s = time.perf_counter() - t\n    asr.transcribe(np.zeros(16_000, dtype=np.float32))  # warm-up, not timed\n\n    out = []\n    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):\n        audio = read_wav_16k_mono(DATA / r[\"wav\"])\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        hyp = asr.transcribe(audio)\n        dt = time.perf_counter() - t\n        dur = len(audio) / 16_000\n        ref_n, hyp_n = normalize_hy(r[\"ref_hy\"]), normalize_hy(hyp)\n        out.append({**r, \"hyp_hy\": hyp, \"audio_s\": round(dur, 2), \"asr_s\": round(dt, 3),\n                    \"rtf\": round(dt / dur, 3),\n                    \"wer\": round(jiwer.wer(ref_n, hyp_n), 3) if ref_n else None,\n                    \"cer\": round(jiwer.cer(ref_n, hyp_n), 3) if ref_n else None})\n        print(f\"[{i:3}/{len(rows)}] {dur:5.1f}s audio  {dt:5.2f}s asr  WER {out[-1]['wer']}\")\n\n    refs = [normalize_hy(r[\"ref_hy\"]) for r in out]\n    hyps = [normalize_hy(r[\"hyp_hy\"]) for r in out]\n    lat = np.array([r[\"asr_s\"] for r in out])\n    durs = np.array([r[\"audio_s\"] for r in out])\n    summary = {\n        \"set\": args.set, \"clips\": len(out), \"audio_minutes\": round(durs.sum() / 60, 2),\n        \"corpus_wer\": round(jiwer.wer(refs, hyps), 4), \"corpus_cer\": round(jiwer.cer(refs, hyps), 4),\n        \"rtf_mean\": round(lat.sum() / durs.sum(), 3),\n        \"asr_s_p50\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 50)), 3),\n        \"asr_s_p95\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 95)), 3),\n        \"asr_s_max\": round(float(lat.max()), 3),\n        \"longest_clip_s\": round(float(durs.max()), 2),\n        \"model_load_s\": round(load_s, 2),\n        \"peak_ram_mb\": peak_ram_mb(), \"ram_before_load_mb\": ram_before,\n        \"threads\": args.threads or \"default\", \"machine\": machine_info(),\n    }\n    RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n    write_jsonl(RESULTS / f\"m1_asr_{args.set}.jsonl\", out)\n    (RESULTS / f\"m1_asr_{args.set}_summary.json\").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),\n                                                             encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in summary.items() if k != \"machine\"}, indent=2))\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",

        "content": "\"\"\"M1 step 3: translation quality, speed and memory on this machine.\n\n  python tools/m1_bench_mt.py             # needs data/fleurs_hy.jsonl (+ results/m1_asr_fleurs.jsonl)\n\nTranslates the FLEURS Armenian sentences one at a time (as in live use), from\n  - the clean reference text, and\n  - the ASR output from m1_bench_asr.py (the realistic, chained case),\nwith beam sizes 1 and 4, against the FLEURS/FLORES English references.\nWrites results/m1_mt.jsonl and results/m1_mt_summary.json.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))\n\nfrom m1_common import DATA, RESULTS, ROOT, machine_info, peak_ram_mb, read_jsonl, write_jsonl  # noqa: E402\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--threads\", type=int, default=4)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--beams\", type=int, nargs=\"+\", default=[1, 4])\n    ap.add_argument(\"--limit\", type=int, default=None)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    import sacrebleu\n    from livetrans.translate import Translator\n\n    rows = read_jsonl(DATA / \"fleurs_hy.jsonl\")[: args.limit]\n    asr_path = RESULTS / \"m1_asr_fleurs.jsonl\"\n    asr_hyp = {r[\"id\"]: r[\"hyp_hy\"] for r in read_jsonl(asr_path)} if asr_path.exists() else {}\n    inputs = {\"clean\": [r[\"ref_hy\"] for r in rows]}\n    if asr_hyp:\n        rows = [r for r in rows if r[\"id\"] in asr_hyp]\n        inputs = {\"clean\": [r[\"ref_hy\"] for r in rows], \"asr\": [asr_hyp[r[\"id\"]] for r in rows]}\n    else:\n        print(\"note: results/m1_asr_fleurs.jsonl not found; only clean-input MT is measured\")\n    refs = [r[\"ref_en\"] for r in rows]\n\n    t = time.perf_counter()\n    tr = Translator(ROOT / \"models/mt-nllb-600m-int8\", threads=args.threads)\n    load_s = time.perf_counter() - t\n    tr.translate(\"Բարև։\")  # warm-up\n\n    summary = {\"sentences\": len(rows), \"model_load_s\": round(load_s, 2), \"threads\": args.threads,\n               \"runs\": {}, \"machine\": machine_info()}\n    per_sentence = [{\"id\": r[\"id\"], \"ref_hy\": r[\"ref_hy\"], \"ref_en\": r[\"ref_en\"],\n                     \"asr_hy\": asr_hyp.get(r[\"id\"])} for r in rows]\n    for beam in args.beams:\n        tr.beam_size = beam\n        for cond, texts in inputs.items():\n            hyps, lat = [], []\n            for i, text in enumerate(texts):\n                t = time.perf_counter()\n                hyps.append(tr.translate(text))\n                lat.append(time.perf_counter() - t)\n                per_sentence[i][f\"en_{cond}_b{beam}\"] = hyps[-1]\n            lat = np.array(lat)\n            key = f\"{cond}_beam{beam}\"\n            summary[\"runs\"][key] = {\n                \"chrf\": round(sacrebleu.corpus_chrf(hyps, [refs]).score, 2),\n                \"bleu\": round(sacrebleu.corpus_bleu(hyps, [refs]).score, 2),\n                \"ms_p50\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 50)) * 1000),\n                \"ms_p95\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 95)) * 1000),\n                \"ms_max\": round(float(lat.max()) * 1000),\n            }\n            print(key, summary[\"runs\"][key])\n    summary[\"peak_ram_mb\"] = peak_ram_mb()\n\n    RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n    write_jsonl(RESULTS / \"m1_mt.jsonl\", per_sentence)\n    (RESULTS / \"m1_mt_summary.json\").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),\n                                                encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    print(f\"peak RAM {summary['peak_ram_mb']} MB, load {summary['model_load_s']} s\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",

      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"M1 (optional but important): record yourself reading FLEURS sentences.\n\n  python tools/m1_record_reading.py --mic 14 --n 15\n\nShows Armenian sentences from the same FLEURS subset used in m1_bench_asr.py.\nRead each one naturally, the way you normally speak (don't imitate a standard\naccent): press Enter to start, Enter to stop; 's' + Enter skips, 'r' + Enter redoes.\nBecause the sentences are the same, your WER can be compared directly with the\nFLEURS speakers on identical text. Audio stays in data/own/ (git-ignored).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))\n\nfrom m1_common import DATA, read_jsonl, write_jsonl, write_wav_16k_mono  # noqa: E402\n\n\ndef record_until_enter(pa, pyaudio, dev) -> np.ndarray:\n    chunks: list[bytes] = []\n\n    def cb(in_data, frame_count, time_info, status):\n        chunks.append(in_data)\n        return (None, pyaudio.paContinue)\n\n    stream = pa.open(format=pyaudio.paInt16, channels=dev.channels, rate=dev.rate, input=True,\n                     input_device_index=dev.index, frames_per_buffer=int(dev.rate * 0.02), stream_callback=cb)\n    input(\"   recording... press Enter when done \")\n    time.sleep(0.3)                      # keep the tail of the last word\n    stream.stop_stream()\n    stream.close()\n    pcm = np.frombuffer(b\"\".join(chunks), dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, dev.channels)\n    audio = pcm.astype(np.float32).mean(axis=1) / 32768.0\n    if dev.rate != 16_000:\n        import soxr\n        audio = soxr.resample(audio, dev.rate, 16_000).astype(np.float32)\n    return audio\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--mic\", type=int, required=True, help=\"mic index from m0_record.py --list-devices\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--n\", type=int, default=15)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    import pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio\n    from livetrans.audio.devices import list_devices, resolve\n\n    sentences = read_jsonl(DATA / \"fleurs_hy.jsonl\")[: args.n]\n    out_dir = DATA / \"own\"\n    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    rows = []\n    with pyaudio.PyAudio() as pa:\n        dev = resolve(list_devices(pa), args.mic, \"mic\")\n        print(f\"Mic: [{dev.index}] {dev.name}\\n\")\n        for i, s in enumerate(sentences, 1):\n            while True:\n                print(f\"\\n({i}/{len(sentences)})  {s['ref_hy']}\")\n                cmd = input(\"   Enter = start, s = skip > \").strip().lower()\n                if cmd == \"s\":\n                    break\n                audio = record_until_enter(pa, pyaudio, dev)\n                peak = float(np.abs(audio).max()) if audio.size else 0.0\n                print(f\"   {len(audio) / 16000:.1f} s, peak {20 * np.log10(peak + 1e-9):.0f} dBFS\")\n                if input(\"   keep? Enter = yes, r = redo > \").strip().lower() == \"r\":\n                    continue\n                name = f\"own_{i:02d}.wav\"\n                write_wav_16k_mono(out_dir / name, audio)\n                rows.append({\"id\": s[\"id\"], \"wav\": f\"own/{name}\", \"ref_hy\": s[\"ref_hy\"], \"ref_en\": s[\"ref_en\"],\n                             \"gender\": \"own\"})\n                break\n    write_jsonl(DATA / \"own_reading.jsonl\", rows)\n    print(f\"\\nSaved {len(rows)} recordings. Next: python tools/m1_bench_asr.py --set own\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",

noqa: E402\n\nFLEURS = \"google/fleurs\"\n\n\ndef find(files: list[str], lang: str, suffix: str) -> str:\n    hits = [f for f in files if f\"/{lang}/\" in f and f.endswith(suffix)]\n    if not hits:\n        raise SystemExit(f\"Could not find '{suffix}' for {lang} in {FLEURS}; repo layout changed?\")\n    return hits[0]\n\n\ndef parse_tsv(path: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    rows = []\n    with open(path, encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as f:\n        for parts in csv.reader(f, delimiter=\"\\t\", quoting=csv.QUOTE_NONE):\n            wav = next((p for p in parts if p.endswith(\".wav\")), None)\n            if not wav:\n                continue\n            i = parts.index(wav)\n            rows.append({\"id\": parts[0], \"file\": wav, \"raw\": parts[i + 1], \"gender\": parts[-1]})\n    return rows\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--n\", type=int, default=100, help=\"number of FLEURS clips (unique sentences)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--seed\", type=int, default=0)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--skip-models\", action=\"store_true\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    from huggingface_hub import HfApi, hf_hub_download\n\n    if not args.skip_models:\n        print(\"1/3 ASR model (FastConformer hy, ONNX, ~460 MB)...\")\n        from livetrans.asr import Transcriber\n        Transcriber(ROOT / \"models/asr-hy-fastconformer\")       # one clip per sentence id, only ids that also have an English reference\n    seen, candidates = set(), []\n    for r in hy:\n        if r[\"id\"] in en_by_id and r[\"id\"] not in seen:\n            seen.add(r[\"id\"])\n            candidates.append(r)\n    random.Random(args.seed).shuffle(candidates)\n    chosen = {r[\"file\"]: r for r in candidates[: args.n]}\n    print(f\"   {len(hy)} hy_am test clips, {len(candidates)} usable sentences, taking {len(chosen)}\")\n\n    tar_path = Path(hf_hub_download(FLEURS, find(files, \"hy_am\", \"test.tar.gz\"), repo_type=\"dataset\",\n                                    local_dir=raw_dir))\n    out_dir = DATA / \"fleurs_hy\"\n    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    found = 0\n    with tarfile.open(tar_path, \"r:gz\") as tar:\n        for member in tar:\n            name = Path(member.name).name\n            if member.isfile() and name in chosen:\n                (out_dir / name).write_bytes(tar.extractfile(member).read())\n                found += 1\n    rows = [{\"id\": r[\"id\"], \"wav\": f\"fleurs_hy/{r['file']}\", \"ref_hy\": r[\"raw\"],\n             \"ref_en\": en_by_id[r[\"id\"]], \"gender\": r[\"gender\"]}\n            for r in chosen.values() if (out_dir / r[\"file\"]).exists()]\n    write_jsonl(DATA / \"fleurs_hy.jsonl\", rows)\n    print(f\"   extracted {found} clips -> {out_dir}; manifest data/fleurs_hy.jsonl ({len(rows)} rows)\")\n    print(\"Done. t\n        dur = len(audio) / 16_000\n        ref_n, hyp_n = normalize_hy(r[\"ref_hy\"]), normalize_hy(hyp)\n        out.append({**r, \"hyp_hy\": hyp, \"audio_s\": round(dur, 2), \"asr_s\": round(dt, 3),\n                    \"rtf\": round(dt / dur, 3),\n                    \"wer\": round(jiwer.wer(ref_n, hyp_n), 3) if ref_n else None,\n                    \"cer\": round(jiwer.cer(ref_n, hyp_n), 3) if ref_n else None})\n        print(f\"[{i:3}/{len(rows)}] {dur:5.1f}s audio  {dt:5.2f}s asr  WER {out[-1]['wer']}\")\n\n    refs = [normalize_hy(r[\"ref_hy\"]) for r in out]\n    hyps = [normalize_hy(r[\"hyp_hy\"]) for r in out]\n    lat = np.array([r[\"asr_s\"] for r in out])\n    durs = np.array([r[\"audio_s\"] for r in out])\n    summary = {\n        \"set\": args.set, \"clips\": len(out), \"audio_minutes\": round(durs.sum() / 60, 2),\n        \"corpus_wer\": round(jiwer.wer(refs, hyps), 4), \"corpus_cer\": round(jiwer.cer(refs, hyps), 4),\n        \"rtf_mean\": round(lat.sum() / durs.sum(), 3),\n        \"asr_s_p50\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 50)), 3),\n        \"asr_s_p95\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 95)), 3),\n        \"asr_s_max\": round(float(lat.max()), 3),\n        \"longest_clip_s\": round(float(durs.max()), 2),\n        \"model_load_s\": round(load_s, 2),\n        \"peak_ram_mb\": peak_ram_mb(), \"ram_before_load_mb\": ram_before,\n        \"threads\": args.threads or \"default\", \"machine\": machine_info(),\n    }\n    RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n    write_jsonl(RESULTS / f\"m1_asr_{args.set}.jsonl\", out)\n    (RESULTS / f\"m1_asr_{args.set}_summary.json\").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),\n                                                             encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in summary.items() if k != \"machine\"}, indent=2))\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\nEOF\nmd5sum tools/m1_fetch.py tools/m1_bench_asr.py"

noqa: E402\n\n\ndef record_until_enter(pa, pyaudio, dev) -> np.ndarray:\n    chunks: list[bytes] = []\n\n    def cb(in_data, frame_count, time_info, status):\n        chunks.append(in_data)\n        return (None, pyaudio.paContinue)\n\n    stream = pa.open(format=pyaudio.paInt16, channels=dev.channels, rate=dev.rate, input=True,\n                     input_device_index=dev.index, frames_per_buffer=int(dev.rate * 0.02), stream_callback=cb)\n    input(\"   recording... press Enter when done \")\n    time.sleep(0.3)                      # keep the tail of the last word\n    stream.stop_stream()\n    stream.close()\n    pcm = np.frombuffer(b\"\".join(chunks), dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, dev.channels)\n    audio = pcm.astype(np.float32).mean(axis=1) / 32768.0\n    if dev.rate != 16_000:\n        import soxr\n        audio = soxr.resample(audio, dev.rate, 16_000).astype(np.float32)\n    return audio\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--mic\", type=int, required=True, help=\"mic index from m0_record.py --list-devices\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--n\", type=int, default=15)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    import pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio\n    from livetrans.audio.devices import list_devices, resolve\n\n    sentences = read_jsonl(DATA / \"fleurs_hy.jsonl\")[: args.n]\n    out_dir = DATA / \"own\"\n    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    rows = []\n    with pyaudio.PyAudio() as pa:\n        dev = resolve(list_devices(pa), args.mic, \"mic\")\n        print(f\"Mic: [{dev.index}] {dev.name}\\n\")\n        for i, s in enumerate(sentences, 1):\n            while True:\n                print(f\"\\n({i}/{len(sentences)})  {s['ref_hy']}\")\n                cmd = input(\"   Enter = start, s = skip > \").strip().lower()\n                if cmd == \"s\":\n                    break\n                audio = record_until_enter(pa, pyaudio, dev)\n                peak = float(np.abs(audio).max()) if audio.size else 0.0\n                print(f\"   {len(audio) / 16000:.1f} s, peak {20 * np.log10(peak + 1e-9):.0f} dBFS\")\n                if input(\"   keep? Enter = yes, r = redo > \").strip().lower() == \"r\":\n                    continue\n                name = f\"own_{i:02d}.wav\"\n                write_wav_16k_mono(out_dir / name, audio)\n                rows.append({\"id\": s[\"id\"], \"wav\": f\"own/{name}\", \"ref_hy\": s[\"ref_hy\"], \"ref_en\": s[\"ref_en\"],\n                             \"gender\": \"own\"})\n                break\n    write_jsonl(DATA / \"own_reading.jsonl\", rows)\n    print(f\"\\nSaved {len(rows)} recordings. Next: python tools/m1_bench_asr.py --set own\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\nEOF\nmd5sum tools/m1_bench_mt.py tools/m1_record_reading.py; ls tools livetrans"

That found and fixed one real bug: the way I stripped punctuation split words like «ինչպե՞ս» in two, which would have inflated the error rates.\n\n**What M1 measures, all on your laptop**\n- **Speech recognition:** word and character error rates, processing time per clip and peak memory, on 100 FLEURS sentences read by Eastern Armenian speakers.\n- **Your own voice:** you read 15 of the **same** sentences, so your Western-influenced pronunciation is compared with the FLEURS speakers on identical text.\n- **Translation:** quality (chrF and BLEU scores) and time per sentence, from two kinds of input:\n  - the correct Armenian text;\n  - the speech recogniser's output, which is the realistic case.\n\n  Each runs with beam search at sizes 1 and 4. It also brings ONNX Runtime (Microsoft's CPU inference engine) and `huggingface_hub` for downloads.\n- `ctranslate2` and `sentencepiece`: run the translation model and its tokenizer.\n- `soxr`: converts your mic's 48 kHz audio to the 16 kHz the model needs.\n- Evaluation only: `jiwer` (error rates), `sacrebleu` (translation scores), `psutil` (memory).\n\n**Downloads (about 1.3 GB plus the FLEURS archive)** go into `models\\` and `data\\`, which git ignores:\n- the speech model (~460 MB);\n- the translation model, int8 NLLB-600M (~620 MB).\n\nOne caveat about the translation model: it's a third-party int8 conversion. The walking skeleton is built and on your laptop, and I checked every file against the tested version. Segmentation is verified on your real audio. The speech and translation models still need your Windows machine, because neither of my shells can download them.

**What happens to each phrase**
1. **Capture:** mic and loopback are recorded side by side, kept on one shared clock.
2. **Format:** each stream is converted from 48 kHz stereo to the 16 kHz mono the models expect.
3. **Phrase cutting (Silero VAD):** a phrase ends after 0.5 s of silence, and anything longer than 10 s is cut.
4. **One worker thread:** recognition (FastConformer) runs first, then translation (NLLB).
5. **Terminal:** each phrase prints with its label, `Me` or `Remote`, then `HY:` and `EN:` lines and a latency breakdown:

```
[00:00:21] Remote
  HY: ...
  EN: ...
  .. latency 2.3s = vad 0.5 + queue 0.0 + asr 0.9 + mt 0.6  (3.9s audio)
```
Latency counts from the moment the speaker stops. Anything over 5 s is marked `!! OVER 5 s`. Capture problems and processing errors print as `!!` lines as they happen. Ctrl+C prints a summary per source: median, 95th-percentile and worst latency, how many phrases went over 5 s, and how the time split between stages. The full session log is saved to `logs\` (git-ignored).

**Verified so far**
- **Phrase cutting on your M0 recording:** your mic gave 9 phrases and the loopback gave 6. They sit exactly in the stretches where each of you spoke, including the 33–45 s overlap. No phrases appeared in silence, and your voice never showed up in the loopback.
- **A timing bug fixed:** a stub test revealed that a late first buffer shifted a whole stream about 0.3 s late. That was also the cause of the "loopback 0.1 s too long" finding in M0. While fixing it I closed a worse risk: under heavy CPU load, late buffers would have been padded with silence mid-speech. Stream start is now estimated from the first half second, and silence is inserted only when the loopback was already idle.
- **Latency accounting:** with stand-in models, the reported phrase ends are within 20 ms of the true ends. When both sides talk at once, the second phrase's wait in the queue shows up correctly.

**New installations (into `.venv`, no PyTorch)**
- `onnx-asr`: runs the speech model and downloads Silero. It also brings ONNX Runtime and `huggingface_hub`.
- `ctranslate2` and `sentencepiece`: run the translation model.
- `soxr`: converts 48 kHz to 16 kHz.

The models total about 1.1 GB, downloaded into `models\`. The translation model is a third-party int8 conversion of Meta's NLLB-600M.

**Run in order**
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans.models
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\try_file.py recordings\20261030-201834\mic.wav --source mic
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\try_file.py recordings\20261030-201834\loopback.wav --source loopback
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --save-audio
```
- **Steps 3–4 are the one-sample check.** They run the same conversion, phrase-cutting and model code as the live program, on your M0 recording. If that recording wasn't Armenian speech, the text will be nonsense, but the step still proves the models load and run.
- **Step 5 is the live test.** Use Meet with the Buds, both of you speaking Armenian for 3–5 minutes. Include short replies, some talking over each other, and one monologue longer than 10 s. `--save-audio` keeps each phrase as a WAV file inside `logs\` on your laptop, so we can tell whether a bad line came from recognition or from translation.

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Audio format bridge: device format (int16, N channels, 44.1/48 kHz) -> model format\n(float32 mono 16 kHz). Streaming, so one converter instance per source keeps\nresampler state across chunks and the total sample count stays exact.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nTARGET_RATE = 16_000\n\n\nclass To16kMono:\n    def __init__(self, in_rate: int):\n        self.in_rate = in_rate\n        self._rs = None\n        if in_rate != TARGET_RATE:\n            import soxr\n            self._rs = soxr.ResampleStream(in_rate, TARGET_RATE, 1, dtype=\"float32\", quality=\"HQ\")\n\n    def __call__(self, pcm: np.ndarray, last: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"pcm: int16 array shaped (frames, channels). Returns float32 1-D at 16 kHz.\"\"\"\n        mono = pcm.astype(np.float32).mean(axis=1) / 32768.0\n        if self._rs is None:\n            return mono\n        return self._rs.resample_chunk(mono, last=last)\n",
        "file_path": "/home/claude/repo/livetrans/audio/convert.py"
      },

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Cut a continuous 16 kHz stream into spoken phrases with Silero VAD (ONNX).\n\nSilero is run frame by frame (512 samples = 32 ms) with its recurrent state\ncarried between frames, so it works on a live stream. Times are measured on\nthe sample clock: sample n of a source is n / 16000 s after the session t0,\nbecause capture.ChunkAligner keeps every source aligned to t0.\n\nA phrase ends after `min_silence_s` of non-speech; `end_s` is the end of the\nlast speech frame (the moment the speaker stopped), which is what the 5 s\nlatency budget is measured from. Phrases longer than `max_speech_s` are cut\nso one long monologue cannot block the pipeline.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nRATE = 16_000\nFRAME = 512          # Silero frame at 16 kHz\nCONTEXT = 64         # Silero expects the last 64 samples of the previous frame prepended\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Segment:\n    source: str          # \"mic\" | \"loopback\"\n    start_s: float       # since session t0 (sample clock)\n    end_s: float         # end of the last speech frame\n    emitted_s: float     # sample-clock time when the segment was closed (end_s + silence wait)\n    audio: np.ndarray    # float32 16 kHz mono, with a little padding\n    forced: bool = False  # True if cut because it hit max_speech_s\n\n\nclass SileroVad:\n    \"\"\"Stateless wrapper around the ONNX session; each stream keeps its own state.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, model_path: str | Path):\n        import onnxruntime as rt\n        opts = rt.SessionOptions()\n        opts.intra_op_num_threads = 1\n        opts.inter_op_num_threads = 1\n        self.session = rt.InferenceSession(str(model_path), opts, providers=[\"CPUExecutionProvider\"])\n        self._sr = np.array(RATE, dtype=np.int64)\n\n    def prob(self, frame_with_context: np.ndarray, state: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]:\n        out, new_state = self.session.run([\"output\", \"stateN\"],\n                                          {\"input\": frame_with_context[None, :], \"state\": state, \"sr\": self._sr})\n        return float(out[0, 0]), new_state\n\n\nclass Segmenter:\n    def __init__(self, source: str, vad: SileroVad, on_segment, *, start_th: float = 0.5,\n                 end_th: float = 0.35, min_silence_s: float = 0.5, min_speech_s: float = 0.25,\n                 max_speech_s: float = 10.0, pad_s: float = 0.2):\n        self.source, self.vad, self.on_segment = source, vad, on_segment\n        self.start_th, self.end_th = start_th, end_th\n        self.min_silence = int(min_silence_s * RATE)\n        self.min_speech = int(min_speech_s * RATE)\n        self.max_speech = int(max_speech_s * RATE)\n        self.pad = int(pad_s * RATE)\n        self._state = np.zeros((2, 1, 128), dtype=np.float32)\n        self._context = np.zeros(CONTEXT, dtype=np.float32)\n        self._pending = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float32)\n        self._n = 0                                       # samples consumed by the VAD so far\n        self._preroll: deque[np.ndarray] = deque(maxlen=max(1, self.pad // FRAME + 1))\n        self._active = False\n        self._frames: list[np.ndarray] = []\n        self._seg_start = 0\n        self._last_speech_end = 0\n        self._silence = 0\n        self.frames_seen = 0\n        self.dropped_short = 0\n\n    def push(self, audio: np.ndarray) -> None:\n        self._pending = np.concatenate([self._pending, audio.astype(np.float32, copy=False)])\n        while len(self._pending) >= FRAME:\n            frame, self._pending = self._pending[:FRAME], self._pending[FRAME:]\n            p, self._state = self.vad.prob(np.concatenate([self._context, frame]), self._state)\n            self._context = frame[-CONTEXT:]\n            self._step(frame, p)\n\n    def _step(self, frame: np.ndarray, p: float) -> None:\n        start, end = self._n, self._n + FRAME\n        self._n = end\n        self.frames_seen += 1\n        if not self._active:\n            if p >= self.start_th:\n                self._active = True\n                self._frames = list(self._preroll) + [frame]\n                self._seg_start = start - FRAME * len(self._preroll)\n                self._last_speech_end = end\n                self._silence = 0\n                self._preroll.clear()\n            else:\n                self._preroll.append(frame)\n            return\n\n        self._frames.append(frame)\n        if p >= self.end_th:\n            self._last_speech_end = end\n            self._silence = 0\n        else:\n            self._silence += FRAME\n        if self._silence >= self.min_silence:\n            self._close(forced=False)\n        elif end - self._seg_start >= self.max_speech:\n            self._close(forced=True)\n\n    def _close(self, forced: bool) -> None:\n        audio = np.concatenate(self._frames)\n        if forced:\n            end = self._n\n        else:\n            end = self._last_speech_end\n            audio = audio[: min(len(audio), end - self._seg_start + self.pad)]\n        speech_len = end - (self._seg_start + FRAME * 0)\n        seg = Segment(self.source, max(self._seg_start, 0) / RATE, end / RATE, self._n / RATE, audio, forced)\n        if forced:\n            # keep going: the speaker has not stopped, the next segment starts here\n            self._frames, self._seg_start, self._silence = [], self._n, 0\n        else:\n            self._active, self._frames = False, []\n        if speech_len >= self.min_speech:\n            self.on_segment(seg)\n        else:\n            self.dropped_short += 1\n\n    def flush(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Close an open phrase (end of session or end of file).\"\"\"\n        if self._active and self._frames:\n            self._close(forced=False)\n",
        "file_path": "/home/claude/repo/livetrans/segmenter.py"
      },

      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Segment queue -> ASR -> translation -> terminal, with per-segment latency.\n\nLatency of a line = time it is printed - moment the speaker stopped (segment.end_s\non the shared sample clock). It is split into:\n  vad   - waiting for the end-of-phrase silence (min_silence) + capture delivery\n  queue - waiting behind other segments (the single worker is busy)\n  asr   - speech recognition\n  mt    - translation\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport queue\nimport sys\nimport threading\nimport time\nimport traceback\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom livetrans.segmenter import Segment\n\nLABELS = {\"mic\": \"Me\", \"loopback\": \"Remote\"}\nBUDGET_S = 5.0\n\n\ndef hms(seconds: float) -> str:\n    s = int(seconds)\n    return f\"{s // 3600:02d}:{s % 3600 // 60:02d}:{s % 60:02d}\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Stats:\n    rows: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)\n    failures: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n    empty_asr: int = 0\n    max_queue: int = 0\n\n\nclass Worker(threading.Thread):\n    \"\"\"Single consumer: models run one segment at a time so they never fight for CPU.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, asr, mt, t0: float, log_dir: Path | None = None, save_audio: bool = False):\n        super().__init__(daemon=True, name=\"worker\")\n        self.asr, self.mt, self.t0 = asr, mt, t0\n        self.q: queue.Queue[Segment | None] = queue.Queue()\n        self.stats = Stats()\n        self.log_dir, self.save_audio = log_dir, save_audio\n        self._print_lock = threading.Lock()\n        self._log = open(log_dir / \"segments.jsonl\", \"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") if log_dir else None\n\n    # called from capture threads\n    def submit(self, seg: Segment) -> None:\n        seg_t_queued = time.perf_counter()\n        self.q.put((seg, seg_t_queued))\n        depth = self.q.qsize()\n        self.stats.max_queue = max(self.stats.max_queue, depth)\n        if depth >= 3:\n            self.say(f\"!! backlog: {depth} segments waiting - latency will exceed the budget\")\n\n    def stop(self) -> None:\n        self.q.put(None)\n\n    def say(self, text: str) -> None:\n        with self._print_lock:\n            print(text, flush=True)\n\n    def run(self) -> None:\n        while (item := self.q.get()) is not None:\n            seg, t_queued = item\n            try:\n                self._process(seg, t_queued)\n            except Exception as e:  # report and keep going\n                msg = f\"{LABELS[seg.source]} @ {hms(seg.start_s)}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}\"\n                self.stats.failures.append(msg)\n                self.say(f\"!! processing failed - {msg}\")\n                traceback.print_exc()\n\n    def _process(self, seg: Segment, t_queued: float) -> None:\n        t_start = time.perf_counter()\n        hy = self.asr.transcribe(seg.audio)\n        t_asr = time.perf_counter()\n        en = self.mt.translate(hy) if hy else \"\"\n        t_mt = time.perf_counter()\n\n        speech_end_wall = self.t0 + seg.end_s\n        total = t_mt - speech_end_wall\n        parts = {\"vad\": t_queued - speech_end_wall, \"queue\": t_start - t_queued,\n                 \"asr\": t_asr - t_start, \"mt\": t_mt - t_asr}\n        label = LABELS[seg.source]\n        dur = len(seg.audio) / 16_000\n        flag = \"  !! OVER 5 s\" if total > BUDGET_S else \"\"\n        timing = (f\"latency {total:.1f}s = vad {parts['vad']:.1f} + queue {parts['queue']:.1f} \"\n                  f\"+ asr {parts['asr']:.1f} + mt {parts['mt']:.1f}  ({dur:.1f}s audio\"\n                  f\"{', cut at max length' if seg.forced else ''}){flag}\")\n        if not hy:\n            self.stats.empty_asr += 1\n            self.say(f\"[{hms(seg.start_s)}] {label}   (no words recognised; {timing})\")\n        else:\n            self.say(f\"[{hms(seg.start_s)}] {label}\\n  HY: {hy}\\n  EN: {en}\\n  .. {timing}\")\n\n        row = {\"source\": seg.source, \"label\": label, \"start_s\": round(seg.start_s, 2),\n               \"end_s\": round(seg.end_s, 2), \"audio_s\": round(dur, 2), \"forced\": seg.forced,\n               \"hy\": hy, \"en\": en, \"latency_s\": round(total, 3),\n               **{f\"{k}_s\": round(v, 3) for k, v in parts.items()}}\n        self.stats.rows.append(row)\n        if self._log:\n            self._log.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n            self._log.flush()\n        if self.save_audio and self.log_dir:\n            from livetrans.audio.wavio import write_wav16k\n            write_wav16k(self.log_dir / f\"{seg.start_s:08.2f}_{label}.wav\", seg.audio)\n\n\ndef summarize(stats: Stats) -> dict:\n    out: dict = {\"segments\": len(stats.rows), \"empty_asr\": stats.empty_asr,\n                 \"failures\": stats.failures, \"max_queue_depth\": stats.max_queue, \"by_source\": {}}\n    for src, label in LABELS.items():\n        lat = np.array([r[\"latency_s\"] for r in stats.rows if r[\"source\"] == src])\n        if lat.size == 0:\n            out[\"by_source\"][label] = {\"segments\": 0}\n            continue\n        rows = [r for r in stats.rows if r[\"source\"] == src]\n        out[\"by_source\"][label] = {\n            \"segments\": int(lat.size),\n            \"latency_p50_s\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 50)), 2),\n            \"latency_p95_s\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 95)), 2),\n            \"latency_max_s\": round(float(lat.max()), 2),\n            \"over_budget\": int((lat > BUDGET_S).sum()),\n            \"mean_parts_s\": {k: round(float(np.mean([r[f\"{k}_s\"] for r in rows])), 2)\n                             for k in (\"vad\", \"queue\", \"asr\", \"mt\")},\n        }\n    return out\n\n\ndef print_summary(summary: dict, capture_problems: list[str]) -> None:\n    print(\"\\n=========== session summary ===========\")\n    print(f\"segments: {summary['segments']}  (no words recognised: {summary['empty_asr']}), \"\n          f\"max queue depth: {summary['max_queue_depth']}\")\n    for label, s in summary[\"by_source\"].items():\n        if not s[\"segments\"]:\n            print(f\"{label:6}: no segments\")\n            continue\n        p = s[\"mean_parts_s\"]\n        print(f\"{label:6}: {s['segments']} segments, latency p50 {s['latency_p50_s']}s, \"\n              f\"p95 {s['latency_p95_s']}s, max {s['latency_max_s']}s, over 5 s: {s['over_budget']}  \"\n              f\"[mean vad {p['vad']} / queue {p['queue']} / asr {p['asr']} / mt {p['mt']}]\")\n    problems = capture_problems + [f\"processing: {f}\" for f in summary[\"failures\"]]\n    print(\"failures: \" + (\"none\" if not problems else \"\"))\n    for p in problems:\n        print(f\"  - {p}\")\n    sys.stdout.flush()\n",

        "content": "\"\"\"Minimal WAV helpers (16-bit PCM) using only the standard library + numpy.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport wave\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\ndef read_wav(path: str | Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:\n    \"\"\"Returns (int16 array shaped (frames, channels), sample_rate).\"\"\"\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"rb\") as w:\n        if w.getsampwidth() != 2:\n            raise ValueError(f\"{path}: only 16-bit PCM WAV is supported\")\n        rate, ch = w.getframerate(), w.getnchannels()\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, ch)\n    return pcm, rate\n\n\ndef write_wav16k(path: str | Path, audio: np.ndarray) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write float32 mono 16 kHz audio.\"\"\"\n    pcm = np.clip(audio * 32767, -32768, 32767).astype(np.int16)\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"wb\") as w:\n        w.setnchannels(1)\n        w.setsampwidth(2)\n        w.setframerate(16_000)\n        w.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())\n",

        "content": "\"\"\"Model locations and one-time download (all CPU, all local after download).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nASR_DIR = ROOT / \"models\" / \"asr-hy-fastconformer\"\nMT_DIR = ROOT / \"models\" / \"mt-nllb-600m-int8\"\nVAD_DIR = ROOT / \"models\" / \"vad-silero\"\n\n\ndef vad_model_path() -> Path:\n    hits = sorted(VAD_DIR.glob(\"*.onnx\"))\n    if not hits:\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"No Silero VAD model in {VAD_DIR}. Run: python -m livetrans.models\")\n    return hits[0]\n\n\ndef fetch_all() -> None:\n    import onnx_asr\n\n    from livetrans.asr import Transcriber\n    from livetrans.translate import download\n\n    print(\"1/3 VAD: Silero (ONNX, ~2 MB)\")\n    onnx_asr.load_vad(\"silero\", path=VAD_DIR)\n    print(\"    ->\", vad_model_path())\n    print(\"2/3 ASR: FastConformer-Hybrid Large hy (ONNX CTC, ~460 MB)\")\n    Transcriber(ASR_DIR)\n    print(\"3/3 MT: NLLB-200 distilled 600M int8 (CTranslate2, ~620 MB)\")\n    download(MT_DIR)\n    print(\"Done. If a download was interrupted, delete that folder under models/ and rerun.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    fetch_all()\n",

      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Live Armenian -> English transcription of a call (walking skeleton).\n\n  python -m livetrans --list-devices\n  python -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16\n  python -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --save-audio     # also keep each segment as WAV\n\nSources are labelled \"Me\" (microphone) and \"Remote\" (system audio). Each line\nshows the Armenian recognition AND the English translation, plus where the\nlatency went. Ctrl+C prints a summary. A log of the session (text + timings)\ngoes to logs/<timestamp>/ (git-ignored).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    for s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):        # Armenian text on any Windows console\n        try:\n            s.reconfigure(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (AttributeError, ValueError):\n            pass\n\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--list-devices\", action=\"store_true\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--mic\", type=int)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--loopback\", type=int)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--asr-threads\", type=int, default=None)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--mt-threads\", type=int, default=4)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--beam\", type=int, default=4, help=\"translation beam size (1 = fastest)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--min-silence\", type=float, default=0.5, help=\"seconds of silence that end a phrase\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--max-speech\", type=float, default=10.0, help=\"force a cut after this many seconds\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--save-audio\", action=\"store_true\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    import pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio\n\n    from livetrans import models\n    from livetrans.audio.capture import CaptureStream\n    from livetrans.audio.convert import To16kMono\n    from livetrans.audio.devices import list_devices, print_devices, resolve\n    from livetrans.pipeline import Worker, print_summary, summarize\n    from livetrans.segmenter import Segmenter, SileroVad\n\n    with pyaudio.PyAudio() as pa:\n        devices = list_devices(pa)\n        if args.list_devices:\n            print_devices(devices)\n            return 0\n        if args.mic is None or args.loopback is None:\n            ap.error(\"choose both devices: --mic N --loopback M (see --list-devices)\")\n        try:\n            mic, lb = resolve(devices, args.mic, \"mic\"), resolve(devices, args.loopback, \"loopback\")\n        except ValueError as e:\n            print(f\"ERROR: {e}\")\n            return 2\n\n        print(\"Loading models...\", flush=True)\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        from livetrans.asr import Transcriber\n        from livetrans.translate import Translator\n        asr = Transcriber(models.ASR_DIR, threads=args.asr_threads)\n        mt = Translator(models.MT_DIR, threads=args.mt_threads, beam_size=args.beam)\n        vad = SileroVad(models.vad_model_path())\n        # warm-up so the first real phrase is not slowed by lazy initialisation\n        import numpy as np\n        mt.translate(asr.transcribe(np.zeros(16_000, dtype=np.float32)) or \"Բարև։\")\n        print(f\"Models ready in {time.perf_counter() - t:.1f} s\")\n\n        log_dir = Path(\"logs\") / datetime.now().strftime(\"%Y%m%d-%H%M%S\")\n        log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        print(f\"Me     = [{mic.index}] {mic.name}\\nRemote = [{lb.index}] {lb.name}\")\n        print(f\"Log: {log_dir}   Listening... (Ctrl+C to stop)\\n\", flush=True)\n\n        t0 = time.perf_counter()\n        worker = Worker(asr, mt, t0, log_dir, save_audio=args.save_audio)\n        worker.start()\n        seg_kw = dict(min_silence_s=args.min_silence, max_speech_s=args.max_speech)\n        pipes = {}\n        for name, dev in ((\"mic\", mic), (\"loopback\", lb)):\n            seg = Segmenter(name, vad, worker.submit, **seg_kw)\n            conv = To16kMono(dev.rate)\n            pipes[name] = (seg, conv, CaptureStream(pa, dev, t0, lambda pcm, s=seg, c=conv: s.push(c(pcm))))\n\n        problems: list[str] = []\n        try:\n            for name, (_, _, cap) in pipes.items():\n                cap.start()\n            stall_reported = False\n            while True:\n                time.sleep(0.25)\n                for name, (_, _, cap) in pipes.items():\n                    label = \"Me\" if name == \"mic\" else \"Remote\"\n                    if not cap.is_active() and f\"{label}: capture stopped\" not in problems:\n                        problems.append(f\"{label}: capture stopped (device unplugged or switched?)\")\n                        worker.say(f\"!! {label}: capture stopped (device unplugged or switched?)\")\n                    if cap.error and f\"{label}: {cap.error}\" not in problems:\n                        problems.append(f\"{label}: {cap.error}\")\n                        worker.say(f\"!! {label}: {cap.error}\")\n                last = pipes[\"mic\"][2].last_callback\n                if not stall_reported and last and time.perf_counter() - last > 2.0:\n                    stall_reported = True\n                    problems.append(\"Me: microphone stopped delivering audio for >2 s\")\n                    worker.say(\"!! Me: microphone stopped delivering audio\")\n        except KeyboardInterrupt:\n            print(\"\\nStopping...\", flush=True)\n        except OSError as e:\n            problems.append(f\"could not open a device: {e}\")\n            print(f\"!! could not open a device: {e}\", flush=True)\n        finally:\n            for name, (seg, conv, cap) in pipes.items():\n                cap.stop()\n                seg.flush()\n            worker.stop()\n            worker.join(timeout=30)\n\n        for name, (seg, _, cap) in pipes.items():\n            label = \"Me\" if name == \"mic\" else \"Remote\"\n            st = cap.aligner.stats\n            if st.overflows:\n                problems.append(f\"{label}: {st.overflows} input buffer overflows (audio lost)\")\n            real_gaps = [g for g in st.gaps if g.db_before > -50 or g.db_after > -50]\n            if name == \"mic\" and st.gaps:\n                problems.append(f\"{label}: {len(st.gaps)} dropouts, {st.filled_s:.2f} s of audio missing\")\n            elif real_gaps:\n                problems.append(f\"{label}: {len(real_gaps)} gaps while sound was playing\")\n        summary = summarize(worker.stats)\n        summary[\"capture_problems\"] = problems\n        summary[\"settings\"] = vars(args)\n        (log_dir / \"summary.json\").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        print_summary(summary, problems)\n        print(f\"Log saved to {log_dir}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",

      "name": "Write",
      "input": {
        "content": "\"\"\"Run the full chain on a recorded WAV: format conversion -> VAD -> ASR -> MT.\n\n  python tools/try_file.py recordings/20261030-201834/mic.wav --source mic\n  python tools/try_file.py recordings/20261030-201834/loopback.wav --source loopback --start 20 --end 35\n\nUses exactly the same conversion, segmentation and model code as the live\nprogram, so a problem seen here is a problem in the pipeline, not in capture.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\n\nfrom livetrans import models  # noqa: E402\nfrom livetrans.audio.convert import To16kMono  # noqa: E402\nfrom livetrans.audio.wavio import read_wav  # noqa: E402\nfrom livetrans.pipeline import LABELS, hms  # noqa: E402\nfrom livetrans.segmenter import Segmenter, SileroVad  # noqa: E402\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    for s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):\n        try:\n            s.reconfigure(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (AttributeError, ValueError):\n            pass\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"wav\", type=Path)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--source\", choices=[\"mic\", \"loopback\"], default=\"mic\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--start\", type=float, default=0.0)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--end\", type=float, default=None)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--vad-only\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"only show the segments, skip the models\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--beam\", type=int, default=4)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    pcm, rate = read_wav(args.wav)\n    a = int(args.start * rate)\n    b = int(args.end * rate) if args.end else len(pcm)\n    pcm = pcm[a:b]\n    print(f\"{args.wav}: {pcm.shape[1]} ch, {rate} Hz, using {args.start:.1f}-{args.start + len(pcm) / rate:.1f} s\")\n\n    segments = []\n    seg = Segmenter(args.source, SileroVad(models.vad_model_path()), segments.append)\n    conv = To16kMono(rate)\n    step = int(rate * 0.02)                       # feed 20 ms chunks, like live capture\n    for i in range(0, len(pcm), step):\n        seg.push(conv(pcm[i:i + step], last=i + step >= len(pcm)))\n    seg.flush()\n    print(f\"VAD: {len(segments)} phrases ({seg.dropped_short} too-short blips dropped)\\n\")\n\n    asr = mt = None\n    if not args.vad_only:\n        from livetrans.asr import Transcriber\n        from livetrans.translate import Translator\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        asr = Transcriber(models.ASR_DIR)\n        mt = Translator(models.MT_DIR, beam_size=args.beam)\n        print(f\"models loaded in {time.perf_counter() - t:.1f} s\\n\")\n\n    for s in segments:\n        start = args.start + s.start_s\n        head = (f\"[{hms(start)}] {LABELS[s.source]}  {start:.2f}-{args.start + s.end_s:.2f} s \"\n                f\"({len(s.audio) / 16000:.1f} s audio{', cut at max length' if s.forced else ''})\")\n        if asr is None:\n            print(head)\n            continue\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        hy = asr.transcribe(s.audio)\n        t_asr = time.perf_counter() - t\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        en = mt.translate(hy) if hy else \"\"\n        t_mt = time.perf_counter() - t\n        print(f\"{head}\\n  HY: {hy or '(nothing recognised)'}\\n  EN: {en}\\n  .. asr {t_asr:.2f}s, mt {t_mt:.2f}s\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",
        "file_path": "/home/claude/repo/tools/try_file.py"

        "command": ". /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/c25c5839-b672-5827-867b-45b4f360c659/scratchpad/venv/bin/activate && python - <<'EOF'\nimport sys, time, threading, numpy as np\nsys.path.insert(0, \".\")\nfrom livetrans.audio.capture import ChunkAligner\nfrom livetrans.audio.convert import To16kMono\nfrom livetrans.segmenter import Segmenter\nfrom livetrans.pipeline import Worker, summarize, print_summary\n\nclass FakeVad:\n    def prob(self, x, state):\n        return (0.9 if np.sqrt(np.mean(x[64:]**2)) > 0.01 else 0.05), state\nclass FakeASR:\n    def transcribe(self, a): time.sleep(0.3); return \"Բարև, ինչպե՞ս ես։\"\nclass FakeMT:\n    def translate(self, t): time.sleep(0.2); return \"Hello, how are you?\"\n\nt0 = time.perf_counter()\nw = Worker(FakeASR(), FakeMT(), t0); w.start()\ndef make(name):\n    seg = Segmenter(name, FakeVad(), w.submit); conv = To16kMono(48000)\n    return ChunkAligner(48000, 2, t0, lambda pcm: seg.push(conv(pcm))), seg\npipes = {n: make(n) for n in (\"mic\", \"loopback\")}\n# real-time feed: mic speaks 0.5-2.0 s, loopback speaks 1.0-3.0 s (overlap), then silence to 4.5 s\ndef feed(name, a, b):\n    al, _ = pipes[name]; n = 960; k = 0\n    while True:\n        t = k * n / 48000\n        if t >= 4.5: break\n        target = t0 + t + n/48000\n        while time.perf_counter() < target: time.sleep(0.002)\n        ts = t + np.arange(n)/48000\n        x = (0.2*np.sin(2*np.pi*200*ts)) if a <= t < b else np.zeros(n)\n        al.push(time.perf_counter(), (np.tile(x[:,None],(1,2))*32767).astype(np.int16).tobytes())\n        k += 1\nth = [threading.Thread(target=feed, args=a) for a in ((\"mic\",0.5,2.0),(\"loopback\",1.0,3.0))]\n[t.start() for t in th]; [t.join() for t in th]\nfor _, s in pipes.values(): s.flush()\nw.stop(); w.join()\ns = summarize(w.stats); print_summary(s, [])\nfor r in w.stats.rows: print({k: r[k] for k in (\"label\",\"start_s\",\"end_s\",\"latency_s\",\"vad_s\",\"queue_s\",\"asr_s\",\"mt_s\")})\nEOF",

The callback only time-stamps\n  the buffer and puts it on a queue (never blocks, never does work).\n- ChunkAligner: consumes those buffers in another thread and turns them into a\n  continuous signal that starts at the session's t0, so sample n of the mic and\n  sample n of the loopback refer to the same moment.\n\nTiming rules (learned from M0 and from load tests):\n- Buffers can only arrive *late*, never early. A stream's start time is therefore\n  estimated from the earliest-arriving buffer of a short warm-up window, not\n  from the first buffer alone (a late first buffer followed by a catch-up burst\n  would otherwise shift the whole stream late for the rest of the session).\n- Late delivery is not lost audio. Under CPU load (ASR running) callbacks can be\n  late by hundreds of ms and then arrive in a burst; inserting zeros there would\n  corrupt speech. So zeros are only inserted when `fill_gaps` is on (loopback)\n  AND the stream was quiet before the hole: WASAPI loopback simply stops\n  delivering while nothing is playing. Other late deliveries are only logged.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport queue\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nGAP_TOLERANCE_S = 0.3     # lateness below this is normal jitter\nWARMUP_S = 0.5            # audio collected before the start time is fixed\nIDLE_DB = -50.0           # \"quiet\" level for deciding that a loopback hole is idle time\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Gap:\n    start_s: float        # seconds since session t0\n    duration_s: float\n    db_before: float      # level just before / after the gap; lets us tell an\n    db_after: float       # idle loopback (silence both sides) from a glitch\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StreamStats:\n    callbacks: int = 0\n    frames: int = 0\n    overflows: int = 0\n    underflows: int = 0\n    first_buffer_s: float | None = None   # when the first buffer arrived, since t0\n    start_offset_s: float | None = None   # estimated time of the stream's first sample, since t0\n    gaps: list[Gap] = field(default_factory=list)       # holes filled with zeros (idle loopback)\n    filled_s: float = 0.0                  # total zeros inserted inside the recording\n    late: list[Gap] = field(default_factory=list)       # late deliveries NOT filled (audio intact)\n    max_lateness_s: float = 0.0\n    max_queue: int = 0\n\n\ndef to_db(mean_square: float) -> float:\n    return float(10.0 * np.log10(mean_square + 1e-12))\n\n\nclass ChunkAligner:\n    \"\"\"Turns time-stamped int16 buffers into an aligned stream. Pure Python + numpy,\n    so it can be tested without audio hardware.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, rate: int, channels: int, t0: float, sink, fill_gaps: bool = False):\n        self.rate = rate\n        self.channels = channels\n        self.t0 = t0\n        self.sink = sink              # callable(np.ndarray int16, shape (n, channels))\n        self.fill_gaps = fill_gaps\n        self.written = 0              # frames handed to sink, including filled zeros\n        self.stats = StreamStats()\n        self._warm: list[tuple[float, np.ndarray, float]] | None = []\n        self._recent: deque[tuple[float, float, int]] = deque()   # (t, mean_sq, n)\n        self._last_db = -120.0\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    # -- level meter (read from the main thread) --------------------------------\n    def level_db(self, window_s: float = 0.3) -> float:\n        now = time.perf_counter()\n        with self._lock:\n            while self._recent and now - self._recent[0][0] > window_s:\n                self._recent.popleft()\n            if not self._recent:\n                return -120.0\n            num = sum(ms * n for _, ms, n in self._recent)\n            den = sum(n for _, _, n in self._recent)\n        return to_db(num / den)\n\n    def _fill(self, seconds: float) -> None:\n        n = int(round(seconds * self.rate))\n        if n > 0:\n            self.sink(np.zeros((n, self.channels), dtype=np.int16))\n            self.written += n\n\n    def _emit(self, pcm: np.ndarray, ms: float) -> None:\n        self.sink(pcm)\n        self.written += pcm.shape[0]\n        self._last_db = to_db(ms)\n\n    def push(self, t_arrival: float, data: bytes, status: int = 0,\n             overflow_flag: int = 2, underflow_flag: int = 1) -> None:\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(data, dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, self.channels)\n        n = pcm.shape[0]\n        st = self.stats\n        st.callbacks += 1\n        st.frames += n\n        if status & overflow_flag:\n            st.overflows += 1\n        if status & underflow_flag:\n            st.underflows += 1\n        ms = float(np.mean((pcm.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0) ** 2)) if n else 0.0\n        with self._lock:\n            self._recent.append((t_arrival, ms, n))\n        if st.first_buffer_s is None:\n            st.first_buffer_s = t_arrival - self.t0\n\n        if self._warm is not None:                         # still collecting the warm-up window\n            self._warm.append((t_arrival, pcm, ms))\n            if sum(p.shape[0] for _, p, _ in self._warm) >= WARMUP_S * self.rate:\n                self._finish_warmup()\n            return\n        self._place(t_arrival, pcm, ms)\n\n    def _finish_warmup(self) -> None:\n        cum, starts = 0, []\n        for t_arr, p, _ in self._warm:\n            cum += p.shape[0]\n            starts.append(t_arr - cum / self.rate)          # implied time of the stream's first sample\n        start = min(starts)\n        self.stats.start_offset_s = round(start - self.t0, 4)\n        self._fill(max(start - self.t0, 0.0))              # lead-in: device started after t0\n        for _, p, ms in self._warm:\n            self._emit(p, ms)\n        self._warm = None\n\n    def _place(self, t_arrival: float, pcm: np.ndarray, ms: float) -> None:\n        st = self.stats\n        n = pcm.shape[0]\n        lateness = t_arrival - (self.t0 + (self.written + n) / self.rate)\n        st.max_lateness_s = max(st.max_lateness_s, round(lateness, 3))\n        if lateness > GAP_TOLERANCE_S:\n            gap = Gap(round(self.written / self.rate, 3), round(lateness, 3),\n                      round(self._last_db, 1), round(to_db(ms), 1))\n            if self.fill_gaps and self._last_db < IDLE_DB:\n                st.gaps.append(gap)\n                st.filled_s += lateness\n                self._fill(lateness)\n            else:\n                st.late.append(gap)\n        self._emit(pcm, ms)\n\n    def flush(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Release warm-up audio if the stream ended before warm-up completed.\"\"\"\n        if self._warm:\n            self._finish_warmup()\n\n    def pad_to(self, t_end: float) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pad with zeros up to t_end so all sources end at the same time.\"\"\"\n        self.flush()\n        self._fill(max(t_end - (self.t0 + self.written / self.rate), 0.0))\n\n\n'''\ns = s[:start] + new_top + s[end:]\ns = s.replace(\"self.aligner = ChunkAligner(device.rate, device.channels, t0, sink)\",\n              \"self.aligner = ChunkAligner(device.rate, device.channels, t0, sink,\\n                                    fill_gaps=device.kind == \\\"loopback\\\")\")\nopen(p, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\").write(s)\nEOF\ngrep -n \"fill_gaps\" livetrans/audio/capture.py; . /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/c25c5839-b672-5827-867b-45b4f360c659/scratchpad/venv/bin/activate && python -m py_compile livetrans/audio/capture.py && echo ok",
