The callback only time-stamps\n  the buffer and puts it on a queue (never blocks, never does work).\n- ChunkAligner: consumes those buffers in another thread and turns them into a\n  continuous signal that starts at the session's t0, so sample n of the mic and\n  sample n of the loopback refer to the same moment.\n\nTiming rules (learned from M0 and from load tests):\n- Buffers can only arrive *late*, never early. A stream's start time is therefore\n  estimated from the earliest-arriving buffer of a short warm-up window, not\n  from the first buffer alone (a late first buffer followed by a catch-up burst\n  would otherwise shift the whole stream late for the rest of the session).\n- Late delivery is not lost audio. Under CPU load (ASR running) callbacks can be\n  late by hundreds of ms and then arrive in a burst; inserting zeros there would\n  corrupt speech. So zeros are only inserted when `fill_gaps` is on (loopback)\n  AND the stream was quiet before the hole: WASAPI loopback simply stops\n  delivering while nothing is playing. Other late deliveries are only logged.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport queue\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nGAP_TOLERANCE_S = 0.3     # lateness below this is normal jitter\nWARMUP_S = 0.5            # audio collected before the start time is fixed\nIDLE_DB = -50.0           # \"quiet\" level for deciding that a loopback hole is idle time\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Gap:\n    start_s: float        # seconds since session t0\n    duration_s: float\n    db_before: float      # level just before / after the gap; lets us tell an\n    db_after: float       # idle loopback (silence both sides) from a glitch\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StreamStats:\n    callbacks: int = 0\n    frames: int = 0\n    overflows: int = 0\n    underflows: int = 0\n    first_buffer_s: float | None = None   # when the first buffer arrived, since t0\n    start_offset_s: float | None = None   # estimated time of the stream's first sample, since t0\n    gaps: list[Gap] = field(default_factory=list)       # holes filled with zeros (idle loopback)\n    filled_s: float = 0.0                  # total zeros inserted inside the recording\n    late: list[Gap] = field(default_factory=list)       # late deliveries NOT filled (audio intact)\n    max_lateness_s: float = 0.0\n    max_queue: int = 0\n\n\ndef to_db(mean_square: float) -> float:\n    return float(10.0 * np.log10(mean_square + 1e-12))\n\n\nclass ChunkAligner:\n    \"\"\"Turns time-stamped int16 buffers into an aligned stream. Pure Python + numpy,\n    so it can be tested without audio hardware.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, rate: int, channels: int, t0: float, sink, fill_gaps: bool = False):\n        self.rate = rate\n        self.channels = channels\n        self.t0 = t0\n        self.sink = sink              # callable(np.ndarray int16, shape (n, channels))\n        self.fill_gaps = fill_gaps\n        self.written = 0              # frames handed to sink, including filled zeros\n        self.stats = StreamStats()\n        self._warm: list[tuple[float, np.ndarray, float]] | None = []\n        self._recent: deque[tuple[float, float, int]] = deque()   # (t, mean_sq, n)\n        self._last_db = -120.0\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    # -- level meter (read from the main thread) --------------------------------\n    def level_db(self, window_s: float = 0.3) -> float:\n        now = time.perf_counter()\n        with self._lock:\n            while self._recent and now - self._recent[0][0] > window_s:\n                self._recent.popleft()\n            if not self._recent:\n                return -120.0\n            num = sum(ms * n for _, ms, n in self._recent)\n            den = sum(n for _, _, n in self._recent)\n        return to_db(num / den)\n\n    def _fill(self, seconds: float) -> None:\n        n = int(round(seconds * self.rate))\n        if n > 0:\n            self.sink(np.zeros((n, self.channels), dtype=np.int16))\n            self.written += n\n\n    def _emit(self, pcm: np.ndarray, ms: float) -> None:\n        self.sink(pcm)\n        self.written += pcm.shape[0]\n        self._last_db = to_db(ms)\n\n    def push(self, t_arrival: float, data: bytes, status: int = 0,\n             overflow_flag: int = 2, underflow_flag: int = 1) -> None:\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(data, dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, self.channels)\n        n = pcm.shape[0]\n        st = self.stats\n        st.callbacks += 1\n        st.frames += n\n        if status & overflow_flag:\n            st.overflows += 1\n        if status & underflow_flag:\n            st.underflows += 1\n        ms = float(np.mean((pcm.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0) ** 2)) if n else 0.0\n        with self._lock:\n            self._recent.append((t_arrival, ms, n))\n        if st.first_buffer_s is None:\n            st.first_buffer_s = t_arrival - self.t0\n\n        if self._warm is not None:                         # still collecting the warm-up window\n            self._warm.append((t_arrival, pcm, ms))\n            if sum(p.shape[0] for _, p, _ in self._warm) >= WARMUP_S * self.rate:\n                self._finish_warmup()\n            return\n        self._place(t_arrival, pcm, ms)\n\n    def _finish_warmup(self) -> None:\n        cum, starts = 0, []\n        for t_arr, p, _ in self._warm:\n            cum += p.shape[0]\n            starts.append(t_arr - cum / self.rate)          # implied time of the stream's first sample\n        start = min(starts)\n        self.stats.start_offset_s = round(start - self.t0, 4)\n        self._fill(max(start - self.t0, 0.0))              # lead-in: device started after t0\n        for _, p, ms in self._warm:\n            self._emit(p, ms)\n        self._warm = None\n\n    def _place(self, t_arrival: float, pcm: np.ndarray, ms: float) -> None:\n        st = self.stats\n        n = pcm.shape[0]\n        lateness = t_arrival - (self.t0 + (self.written + n) / self.rate)\n        st.max_lateness_s = max(st.max_lateness_s, round(lateness, 3))\n        if lateness > GAP_TOLERANCE_S:\n            gap = Gap(round(self.written / self.rate, 3), round(lateness, 3),\n                      round(self._last_db, 1), round(to_db(ms), 1))\n            if self.fill_gaps and self._last_db < IDLE_DB:\n                st.gaps.append(gap)\n                st.filled_s += lateness\n                self._fill(lateness)\n            else:\n                st.late.append(gap)\n        self._emit(pcm, ms)\n\n    def flush(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Release warm-up audio if the stream ended before warm-up completed.\"\"\"\n        if self._warm:\n            self._finish_warmup()\n\n    def pad_to(self, t_end: float) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pad with zeros up to t_end so all sources end at the same time.\"\"\"\n        self.flush()\n        self._fill(max(t_end - (self.t0 + self.written / self.rate), 0.0))\n\n\nclass CaptureStream:\n    \"\"\"One PyAudio input stream feeding a ChunkAligner via a worker thread.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, pa, device, t0: float, sink, buffer_s: float = 0.02):\n        import pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio   # imported here so ChunkAligner works without it\n        self._pyaudio = pyaudio\n        self.pa = pa\n        self.device = device\n        self.aligner = ChunkAligner(device.rate, device.channels, t0, sink,\n                                    fill_gaps=device.kind == \"loopback\")\n        self._q: queue.Queue = queue.Queue()\n        self._stop = threading.Event()\n        self._worker = threading.Thread(target=self._drain, daemon=True,\n                                         name=f\"drain-{device.kind}\")\n        self.last_callback = None\n        self.stream = None\n        self.error: str | None = None\n        self._fpb = max(int(device.rate * buffer_s), 64)\n\n    def _callback(self, in_data, frame_count, time_info, status):\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        self.last_callback = t\n        self._q.put((t, in_data, status))\n        return (None, self._pyaudio.paContinue)\n\n    def _drain(self) -> None:\n        pa = self._pyaudio\n        while not (self._stop.is_set() and self._q.empty()):\n            try:\n                t, data, status = self._q.get(timeout=0.1)\n            except queue.Empty:\n                continue\n            self.aligner.stats.max_queue = max(self.aligner.stats.max_queue, self._q.qsize() + 1)\n            try:\n                self.aligner.push(t, data, status, pa.paInputOverflow, pa.paInputUnderflow)\n            except Exception as e:  # never let a bad buffer kill the thread silently\n                self.error = f\"{type(e).__name__}: {e}\"\n\n    def start(self) -> None:\n        self.stream = self.pa.open(\n            format=self._pyaudio.paInt16,\n            channels=self.device.channels,\n            rate=self.device.rate,\n            input=True,\n            input_device_index=self.device.index,\n            frames_per_buffer=self._fpb,\n            stream_callback=self._callback,\n        )\n        self._worker.start()\n\n    def is_active(self) -> bool:\n        try:\n            return bool(self.stream and self.stream.is_active())\n        except OSError:\n            return False\n\n    def stop(self) -> None:\n        if self.stream is not None:\n            try:\n                self.stream.stop_stream()\n                self.stream.close()\n            except OSError as e:          # e.g. device unplugged mid-session\n                self.error = self.error or f\"close failed: {e}\"\n        self._stop.set()\n        if self._worker.is_alive():\n            self._worker.join(timeout=5)\nEOF\ncat > livetrans/audio/convert.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Audio format bridge: device format (int16, N channels, 44.1/48 kHz) -> model format\n(float32 mono 16 kHz). Streaming, so one converter instance per source keeps\nresampler state across chunks and the total sample count stays exact.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nTARGET_RATE = 16_000\n\n\nclass To16kMono:\n    def __init__(self, in_rate: int):\n        self.in_rate = in_rate\n        self._rs = None\n        if in_rate != TARGET_RATE:\n            import soxr\n            self._rs = soxr.ResampleStream(in_rate, TARGET_RATE, 1, dtype=\"float32\", quality=\"HQ\")\n\n    def __call__(self, pcm: np.ndarray, last: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"pcm: int16 array shaped (frames, channels). Returns float32 1-D at 16 kHz.\"\"\"\n        mono = pcm.astype(np.float32).mean(axis=1) / 32768.0\n        if self._rs is None:\n            return mono\n        return self._rs.resample_chunk(mono, last=last)\nEOF\ncat > livetrans/audio/wavio.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Minimal WAV helpers (16-bit PCM) using only the standard library + numpy.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport wave\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\ndef read_wav(path: str | Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:\n    \"\"\"Returns (int16 array shaped (frames, channels), sample_rate).\"\"\"\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"rb\") as w:\n        if w.getsampwidth() != 2:\n            raise ValueError(f\"{path}: only 16-bit PCM WAV is supported\")\n        rate, ch = w.getframerate(), w.getnchannels()\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, ch)\n    return pcm, rate\n\n\ndef write_wav16k(path: str | Path, audio: np.ndarray) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write float32 mono 16 kHz audio.\"\"\"\n    pcm = np.clip(audio * 32767, -32768, 32767).astype(np.int16)\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"wb\") as w:\n        w.setnchannels(1)\n        w.setsampwidth(2)\n        w.setframerate(16_000)\n        w.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())\nEOF\ncat > requirements.txt <<'EOF'\n# Live pipeline (CPU only; no PyTorch)\nPyAudioWPatch>=0.2.12.6   # PortAudio fork with WASAPI loopback (Windows system-audio capture)\nnumpy>=1.24\nsoxr>=0.5                 # resampling 48 kHz device audio -> 16 kHz model audio\nonnx-asr[cpu,hub]>=0.12   # FastConformer ASR + Silero VAD download (pulls onnxruntime, huggingface_hub)\nctranslate2>=4.5          # int8 NLLB translation\nsentencepiece>=0.2        # NLLB tokenizer\n# Optional, only for tools/m1_bench_*.py: jiwer sacrebleu psutil\nEOF\nsed -i 's|^recordings/$|recordings/\\nlogs/|' .gitignore\nmd5sum livetrans/audio/capture.py livetrans/audio/convert.py livetrans/audio/wavio.py requirements.txt .gitignore"

Times are measured on\nthe sample clock: sample n of a source is n / 16000 s after the session t0,\nbecause capture.ChunkAligner keeps every source aligned to t0.\n\nA phrase ends after `min_silence_s` of non-speech; `end_s` is the end of the\nlast speech frame (the moment the speaker stopped), which is what the 5 s\nlatency budget is measured from. Phrases longer than `max_speech_s` are cut\nso one long monologue cannot block the pipeline.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections import deque\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nRATE = 16_000\nFRAME = 512          # Silero frame at 16 kHz\nCONTEXT = 64         # Silero expects the last 64 samples of the previous frame prepended\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Segment:\n    source: str          # \"mic\" | \"loopback\"\n    start_s: float       # since session t0 (sample clock)\n    end_s: float         # end of the last speech frame\n    emitted_s: float     # sample-clock time when the segment was closed (end_s + silence wait)\n    audio: np.ndarray    # float32 16 kHz mono, with a little padding\n    forced: bool = False  # True if cut because it hit max_speech_s\n\n\nclass SileroVad:\n    \"\"\"Stateless wrapper around the ONNX session; each stream keeps its own state.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, model_path: str | Path):\n        import onnxruntime as rt\n        opts = rt.SessionOptions()\n        opts.intra_op_num_threads = 1\n        opts.inter_op_num_threads = 1\n        self.session = rt.InferenceSession(str(model_path), opts, providers=[\"CPUExecutionProvider\"])\n        self._sr = np.array(RATE, dtype=np.int64)\n\n    def prob(self, frame_with_context: np.ndarray, state: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]:\n        out, new_state = self.session.run([\"output\", \"stateN\"],\n                                          {\"input\": frame_with_context[None, :], \"state\": state, \"sr\": self._sr})\n        return float(out[0, 0]), new_state\n\n\nclass Segmenter:\n    def __init__(self, source: str, vad: SileroVad, on_segment, *, start_th: float = 0.5,\n                 end_th: float = 0.35, min_silence_s: float = 0.5, min_speech_s: float = 0.25,\n                 max_speech_s: float = 10.0, pad_s: float = 0.2):\n        self.source, self.vad, self.on_segment = source, vad, on_segment\n        self.start_th, self.end_th = start_th, end_th\n        self.min_silence = int(min_silence_s * RATE)\n        self.min_speech = int(min_speech_s * RATE)\n        self.max_speech = int(max_speech_s * RATE)\n        self.pad = int(pad_s * RATE)\n        self._state = np.zeros((2, 1, 128), dtype=np.float32)\n        self._context = np.zeros(CONTEXT, dtype=np.float32)\n        self._pending = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float32)\n        self._n = 0                                       # samples consumed by the VAD so far\n        self._preroll: deque[np.ndarray] = deque(maxlen=max(1, self.pad // FRAME + 1))\n        self._active = False\n        self._frames: list[np.ndarray] = []\n        self._seg_start = 0\n        self._last_speech_end = 0\n        self._silence = 0\n        self.frames_seen = 0\n        self.dropped_short = 0\n\n    def push(self, audio: np.ndarray) -> None:\n        self._pending = np.concatenate([self._pending, audio.astype(np.float32, copy=False)])\n        while len(self._pending) >= FRAME:\n            frame, self._pending = self._pending[:FRAME], self._pending[FRAME:]\n            p, self._state = self.vad.prob(np.concatenate([self._context, frame]), self._state)\n            self._context = frame[-CONTEXT:]\n            self._step(frame, p)\n\n    def _step(self, frame: np.ndarray, p: float) -> None:\n        start, end = self._n, self._n + FRAME\n        self._n = end\n        self.frames_seen += 1\n        if not self._active:\n            if p >= self.start_th:\n                self._active = True\n                self._frames = list(self._preroll) + [frame]\n                self._seg_start = start - FRAME * len(self._preroll)\n                self._last_speech_end = end\n                self._silence = 0\n                self._preroll.clear()\n            else:\n                self._preroll.append(frame)\n            return\n\n        self._frames.append(frame)\n        if p >= self.end_th:\n            self._last_speech_end = end\n            self._silence = 0\n        else:\n            self._silence += FRAME\n        if self._silence >= self.min_silence:\n            self._close(forced=False)\n        elif end - self._seg_start >= self.max_speech:\n            self._close(forced=True)\n\n    def _close(self, forced: bool) -> None:\n        audio = np.concatenate(self._frames)\n        if forced:\n            end = self._n\n        else:\n            end = self._last_speech_end\n            audio = audio[: min(len(audio), end - self._seg_start + self.pad)]\n        speech_len = end - self._seg_start\n        seg = Segment(self.source, max(self._seg_start, 0) / RATE, end / RATE, self._n / RATE, audio, forced)\n        if forced:\n            # keep going: the speaker has not stopped, the next segment starts here\n            self._frames, self._seg_start, self._silence = [], self._n, 0\n        else:\n            self._active, self._frames = False, []\n        if speech_len >= self.min_speech:\n            self.on_segment(seg)\n        else:\n            self.dropped_short += 1\n\n    def flush(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Close an open phrase (end of session or end of file).\"\"\"\n        if self._active and self._frames:\n            self._close(forced=False)\nEOF\ncat > If a download was interrupted, delete that folder under models/ and rerun.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    fetch_all()\nEOF\nmd5sum livetrans/segmenter.py livetrans/models.py"

~~~~~~~~~~~~json
        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && cat > livetrans/pipeline.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Segment queue -> ASR -> translation -> terminal, with per-segment latency.\n\nLatency of a line = time it is printed - moment the speaker stopped (segment.end_s\non the shared sample clock). It is split into:\n  vad   - waiting for the end-of-phrase silence (min_silence) + capture delivery\n  queue - waiting behind other segments (the single worker is busy)\n  asr   - speech recognition\n  mt    - translation\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport queue\nimport sys\nimport threading\nimport time\nimport traceback\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom livetrans.segmenter import Segment\n\nLABELS = {\"mic\": \"Me\", \"loopback\": \"Remote\"}\nBUDGET_S = 5.0\n\n\ndef hms(seconds: float) -> str:\n    s = int(seconds)\n    return f\"{s // 3600:02d}:{s % 3600 // 60:02d}:{s % 60:02d}\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Stats:\n    rows: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)\n    failures: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n    empty_asr: int = 0\n    max_queue: int = 0\n\n\nclass Worker(threading.Thread):\n    \"\"\"Single consumer: models run one segment at a time so they never fight for CPU.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, asr, mt, t0: float, log_dir: Path | None = None, save_audio: bool = False):\n        super().__init__(daemon=True, name=\"worker\")\n        self.asr, self.mt, self.t0 = asr, mt, t0\n        self.q: queue.Queue[Segment | None] = queue.Queue()\n        self.stats = Stats()\n        self.log_dir, self.save_audio = log_dir, save_audio\n        self._print_lock = threading.Lock()\n        self._log = open(log_dir / \"segments.jsonl\", \"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") if log_dir else None\n\n    # called from capture threads\n    def submit(self, seg: Segment) -> None:\n        seg_t_queued = time.perf_counter()\n        self.q.put((seg, seg_t_queued))\n        depth = self.q.qsize()\n        self.stats.max_queue = max(self.stats.max_queue, depth)\n        if depth >= 3:\n            self.say(f\"!! backlog: {depth} segments waiting - latency will exceed the budget\")\n\n    def stop(self) -> None:\n        self.q.put(None)\n\n    def say(self, text: str) -> None:\n        with self._print_lock:\n            print(text, flush=True)\n\n    def run(self) -> None:\n        while (item := self.q.get()) is not None:\n            seg, t_queued = item\n            try:\n                self._process(seg, t_queued)\n            except Exception as e:  # report and keep going\n                msg = f\"{LABELS[seg.source]} @ {hms(seg.start_s)}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}\"\n                self.stats.failures.append(msg)\n                self.say(f\"!! processing failed - {msg}\")\n                traceback.print_exc()\n\n    def _process(self, seg: Segment, t_queued: float) -> None:\n        t_start = time.perf_counter()\n        hy = self.asr.transcribe(seg.audio)\n        t_asr = time.perf_counter()\n        en = self.mt.translate(hy) if hy else \"\"\n        t_mt = time.perf_counter()\n\n        speech_end_wall = self.t0 + seg.end_s\n        total = t_mt - speech_end_wall\n        parts = {\"vad\": t_queued - speech_end_wall, \"queue\": t_start - t_queued,\n                 \"asr\": t_asr - t_start, \"mt\": t_mt - t_asr}\n        label = LABELS[seg.source]\n        dur = len(seg.audio) / 16_000\n        flag = \"  !! OVER 5 s\" if total > BUDGET_S else \"\"\n        timing = (f\"latency {total:.1f}s = vad {parts['vad']:.1f} + queue {parts['queue']:.1f} \"\n                  f\"+ asr {parts['asr']:.1f} + mt {parts['mt']:.1f}  ({dur:.1f}s audio\"\n                  f\"{', cut at max length' if seg.forced else ''}){flag}\")\n        if not hy:\n            self.stats.empty_asr += 1\n            self.say(f\"[{hms(seg.start_s)}] {label}   (no words recognised; {timing})\")\n        else:\n            self.say(f\"[{hms(seg.start_s)}] {label}\\n  HY: {hy}\\n  EN: {en}\\n  .. {timing}\")\n\n        row = {\"source\": seg.source, \"label\": label, \"start_s\": round(seg.start_s, 2),\n               \"end_s\": round(seg.end_s, 2), \"audio_s\": round(dur, 2), \"forced\": seg.forced,\n               \"hy\": hy, \"en\": en, \"latency_s\": round(total, 3),\n               **{f\"{k}_s\": round(v, 3) for k, v in parts.items()}}\n        self.stats.rows.append(row)\n        if self._log:\n            self._log.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n            self._log.flush()\n        if self.save_audio and self.log_dir:\n            from livetrans.audio.wavio import write_wav16k\n            write_wav16k(self.log_dir / f\"{seg.start_s:08.2f}_{label}.wav\", seg.audio)\n\n\ndef summarize(stats: Stats) -> dict:\n    out: dict = {\"segments\": len(stats.rows), \"empty_asr\": stats.empty_asr,\n                 \"failures\": stats.failures, \"max_queue_depth\": stats.max_queue, \"by_source\": {}}\n    for src, label in LABELS.items():\n        lat = np.array([r[\"latency_s\"] for r in stats.rows if r[\"source\"] == src])\n        if lat.size == 0:\n            out[\"by_source\"][label] = {\"segments\": 0}\n            continue\n        rows = [r for r in stats.rows if r[\"source\"] == src]\n        out[\"by_source\"][label] = {\n            \"segments\": int(lat.size),\n            \"latency_p50_s\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 50)), 2),\n            \"latency_p95_s\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 95)), 2),\n            \"latency_max_s\": round(float(lat.max()), 2),\n            \"over_budget\": int((lat > BUDGET_S).sum()),\n            \"mean_parts_s\": {k: round(float(np.mean([r[f\"{k}_s\"] for r in rows])), 2)\n                             for k in (\"vad\", \"queue\", \"asr\", \"mt\")},\n        }\n    return out\n\n\ndef print_summary(summary: dict, capture_problems: list[str]) -> None:\n    print(\"\\n=========== session summary ===========\")\n    print(f\"segments: {summary['segments']}  (no words recognised: {summary['empty_asr']}), \"\n          f\"max queue depth: {summary['max_queue_depth']}\")\n    for label, s in summary[\"by_source\"].items():\n        if not s[\"segments\"]:\n            print(f\"{label:6}: no segments\")\n            continue\n        p = s[\"mean_parts_s\"]\n        print(f\"{label:6}: {s['segments']} segments, latency p50 {s['latency_p50_s']}s, \"\n              f\"p95 {s['latency_p95_s']}s, max {s['latency_max_s']}s, over 5 s: {s['over_budget']}  \"\n              f\"[mean vad {p['vad']} / queue {p['queue']} / asr {p['asr']} / mt {p['mt']}]\")\n    problems = capture_problems + [f\"processing: {f}\" for f in summary[\"failures\"]]\n    print(\"failures: \" + (\"none\" if not problems else \"\"))\n    for p in problems:\n        print(f\"  - {p}\")\n    sys.stdout.flush()\nEOF\nmd5sum livetrans/pipeline.py"
~~~~~~~~~~~~

You were right that words were missed, but processing time wasn't the reason. Your microphone stream lost about 7% of its audio, roughly 7 s over 90 s, while the remote side lost nothing. I've added detection for this and two likely fixes. The fixes are a hypothesis until you run the two short tests below.

**What the log shows**

| | Me (mic) | Remote (loopback) |
|---|---|---|
| Phrases | 14 | 11 |
| Latency, typical / worst | 4.6 s / 8.3 s | 1.9 s / 2.1 s |
| Over 5 s | 6 | 0 |
| Time between end of speech and phrase handed off | 0.5 s at the start, growing to 7.1 s | steady 0.5 s |

- **Processing was fast on both sides.** Recognition averaged 0.44 s per phrase and translation 0.77 s, and no phrase ever had to wait behind another.
- **The mic fell behind steadily.** Its delay grew at a constant ~0.07 s per second, about 7% of its audio never arriving. Missing samples cause both your missed words and your high latency.
- **The timestamps agree.** Your lines were stamped too early. «Շատ հաճելի ա, Կարում ջան» shows 74.0 s but was really spoken around 79.8 s, after the remote sentence it answers.
- **My earlier check missed it.** It labelled this "late delivery, audio kept". That was wrong; it was lost audio.

**Recognition or translation?** When the Armenian was right, the English was right too:
- «Լսո՞ւմ ես։» → "Do you hear me?"
- «Իմ անունը Սարգիս ա։» → "My name is Sarkis."
- «Որտե՞ղ եք ապրում։» → "Where do you live?"
- «Բայց ծնվել մեծացել է սիրիա...» → "But I was born and raised in Syria."

The bad lines started with bad Armenian:
- «Հեռեւ ձեզ, ո՞նցեքք» instead of «Բարև ձեզ, ո՞նց եք», which became "Away from you".
- A lone «֊։», which the translator turned into an invented "What is it?".

So recognition is the weaker link. Translation also stumbles on colloquial forms like «Քոնը ո՞նց ա».

**What I changed**
- **Lost audio is now reported, not hidden.** If a stream's delay doesn't recover within 1 s, the program prints `!! Me: 0.38 s of audio LOST around 45 s` during the run. It also realigns the clock, so later timestamps and latencies stay true.
- **A new end-of-session line shows how much of the expected audio each stream delivered**, for example `capture Me: delivered 92.9% of expected audio`. I tested this on a simulation of your session and it reported the same 92.9%.
- **The probable cause, CPU starvation of the mic's audio thread**, gets three mitigations:
  - recognition is capped at 4 threads, with its busy-waiting between runs turned off;
  - translation's busy-waiting is turned off;
  - the capture buffer grows from 20 to 50 ms, so short stalls don't overflow it.
- **Wordless recognitions such as «֊։» are no longer translated.** That removes the invented English lines.

**Please run two short tests in Meet** (same setup, both of you talking):
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --no-models
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --save-audio
```
1. **About 60 s with models off.** This only captures and cuts phrases. If the mic still loses audio here, the models aren't the cause; it's the Intel mic driver or Meet sharing the mic, and that needs a different fix.
2. **2–3 minutes with everything on.** Watch for `!! … LOST` lines and the `delivered …%` line at the end.

Tell me when both are done and I'll read the two logs.

loopback after quiet audio: WASAPI idle time -> fill with zeros now;\n          - it recovers within LOSS_CONFIRM_S: buffers were only late (CPU load) -> keep;\n          - it does not recover: the device dropped samples -> report as LOST and\n            re-anchor the timeline with zeros so timestamps and latency stay true.\"\"\"\n        st = self.stats\n        n = pcm.shape[0]\n        lateness = t_arrival - (self.t0 + (self.written + n) / self.rate)\n        st.max_lateness_s = max(st.max_lateness_s, round(lateness, 3))\n        if lateness <= GAP_TOLERANCE_S:\n            self._late_since = None\n        else:\n            gap = Gap(round(self.written / self.rate, 3), round(lateness, 3),\n                      round(self._last_db, 1), round(to_db(ms), 1))\n            if self.fill_gaps and self._last_db < IDLE_DB:\n                st.gaps.append(gap)\n                st.filled_s += lateness\n                self._fill(lateness)\n                self._late_since = None\n            elif self._late_since is None:\n                self._late_since = t_arrival\n                st.late.append(gap)\n            elif t_arrival - self._late_since >= LOSS_CONFIRM_S:\n                st.lost.append(gap)\n                st.lost_s += lateness\n                self._fill(lateness)\n                self._late_since = None\n                if self.on_loss:\n                    self.on_loss(gap)\n        self._emit(pcm, ms)\n\n    def delivered_ratio(self, t_now: float) -> float | None:\n        \"\"\"Samples actually delivered / samples expected since the stream started.\"\"\"\n        if self.stats.start_offset_s is None:\n            return None\n        expected = (t_now - <<'EOF'\nimport sys, numpy as np\nsys.path.insert(0, \"/home/claude/repo\")\nfrom livetrans.audio.capture import ChunkAligner\nR, N = 48000, 960; dt = N/R\ndef run(fill, arr, levels, total):\n    out=[]; events=[]\n    al = ChunkAligner(R, 1, 0.0, out.append, fill_gaps=fill, on_loss=events.append)\n    for t, a in zip(arr, levels):\n        al.push(t, np.full((N,1), a*32767).astype(np.int16).tobytes())\n    al.pad_to(total)\n    return al, np.concatenate(out)[:,0], events\n# A) mic loses 7% of buffers continuously (what the live log shows): every 14th buffer never arrives\ntrue_end = [(k+1)*dt for k in range(4700)]          # ~94 s\nkeep = [k for k in range(4700) if k % 14 != 13]\narr = [true_end[k] for k in keep]\nal, sig, ev = run(False, arr, [0.3]*len(arr), 94.0)\nprint(\"A lost events\", len(ev), \"lost_s\", round(al.stats.lost_s,2), \"(true\", round(4700/14*dt,2), \") final lateness ok:\",\n      round(al.written/R,2), \"delivered ratio\", al.delivered_ratio(94.0))\n# B) transient stall: 0.6 s late then burst -> must NOT be called loss\narr = [e if not (100<=k<=130) else max(e, 2.0+0.62) for k, e in enumerate(true_end[:400])]\nal, sig, ev = run(False, arr, [0.3]*400, 8.0)\nprint(\"B lost\", len(ev), \"late\", len(al.stats.late), \"zeros in speech\", int((sig[:int(7.9*R)]==0).sum()))\n# C) loopback idle still filled immediately\narr = [e if k < 50 else e+1.5 for k, e in enumerate(true_end[:200])]\nal, sig, ev = run(True, arr, [0.0]*50+[0.3]*150, 7.0)\nprint(\"C idle filled\", [(g.start_s, g.duration_s) for g in al.stats.gaps], \"lost\", len(ev))\nEOF",

~~~~~~~~~~~~json
      "text": "You were right that words were missed, but processing time wasn't the reason. Your microphone stream lost about 7% of its audio, roughly 7 s over 90 s, while the remote side lost nothing. I've added detection for this and two likely fixes. The fixes are a hypothesis until you run the two short tests below.\n\n**What the log shows**\n\n| | Me (mic) | Remote (loopback) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Phrases | 14 | 11 |\n| Latency, typical / worst | 4.6 s / 8.3 s | 1.9 s / 2.1 s |\n| Over 5 s | 6 | 0 |\n| Time between end of speech and phrase handed off | 0.5 s at the start, growing to 7.1 s | steady 0.5 s |\n\n- **Processing was fast on both sides.** Recognition averaged 0.44 s per phrase and translation 0.77 s, and no phrase ever had to wait behind another.\n- **The mic fell behind steadily.** Its delay grew at a constant ~0.07 s per second, about 7% of its audio never arriving. Missing samples cause both your missed words and your high latency.\n- **The timestamps agree.** Your lines were stamped too early. «Շատ հաճելի ա, Կարում ջան» shows 74.0 s but was really spoken around 79.8 s, after the remote sentence it answers.\n- **My earlier check missed it.** It labelled this \"late delivery, audio kept\". That was wrong; it was lost audio.\n\n**Recognition or translation?** When the Armenian was right, the English was right too:\n- «Լսո՞ւմ ես։» → \"Do you hear me?\"\n- «Իմ անունը Սարգիս ա։» → \"My name is Sarkis.\"\n- «Որտե՞ղ եք ապրում։» → \"Where do you live?\"\n- «Բայց ծնվել մեծացել է սիրիա...» → \"But I was born and raised in Syria.\"\n\nThe bad lines started with bad Armenian:\n- «Հեռեւ ձեզ, ո՞նցեքք» instead of «Բարև ձեզ, ո՞նց եք», which became \"Away from you\".\n- A lone «֊։», which the translator turned into an invented \"What is it?\".\n\nSo recognition is the weaker link. Translation also stumbles on colloquial forms like «Քոնը ո՞նց ա».\n\n**What I changed**\n- **Lost audio is now reported, not hidden.** If a stream's delay doesn't recover within 1 s, the program prints `!! Me: 0.38 s of audio LOST around 45 s` during the run. It also realigns the clock, so later timestamps and latencies stay true.\n- **A new end-of-session line shows how much of the expected audio each stream delivered**, for example `capture Me: delivered 92.9% of expected audio`. I tested this on a simulation of your session and it reported the same 92.9%.\n- **The probable cause, CPU starvation of the mic's audio thread**, gets three mitigations:\n  - recognition is capped at 4 threads, with its busy-waiting between runs turned off;\n  - translation's busy-waiting is turned off;\n  - the capture buffer grows from 20 to 50 ms, so short stalls don't overflow it.\n- **Wordless recognitions such as «֊։» are no longer translated.** That removes the invented English lines.\n\n**Please run two short tests in Meet** (same setup, both of you talking):\n```\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --no-models\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --save-audio\n```\n1. **About 60 s with models off.** This only captures and cuts phrases. If the mic still loses audio here, the models aren't the cause; it's the Intel mic driver or Meet sharing the mic, and that needs a different fix.\n2. **2–3 minutes with everything on.** Watch for `!! … LOST` lines and the `delivered …%` line at the end.\n\nTell me when both are done and I'll read the two logs.",
      "citations": []
    }
~~~~~~~~~~~~

**What's tracked and what isn't**
- `git check-ignore` confirmed that `recordings\`, `logs\`, `models\`, `data\`, `.venv\` and `__pycache__` are all ignored.
- No audio, model or environment file was staged; only source, docs and text results are tracked.

**How TESTS.md records the microphone problem**
- **Measured:** for each of your phrases, the gap between when the phrase was handed off and when its sample count said it ended. That gap grew from 0.55 s to 7.07 s (fit: 0.0769 s per second). The remote side stayed flat at 0.50–0.55 s, and there were zero overflow flags.
- **Derived, not counted:** the mic's sample clock ran at 92.9% of real time. Test 1 never logged raw sample counts; the new version does.
- **Inferred:** the samples were never delivered. Two alternatives are listed alongside: the device running at a lower true rate under some condition, and samples being lost inside the audio library without an overflow flag.
- **Hypotheses, all unconfirmed:** CPU starvation, Python's single-thread lock (the GIL) delaying the audio callback, and the Intel mic driver while Meet shares the mic.

The CPU hypothesis has some evidence each way. The run at 21:04, with only 4 phrases to process, didn't drift; test 1, with 25, did. Against it, the remote stream didn't drift under the same load.

## Test 2: models off

1. Same setup as test 1: Meet call in the browser, the Buds, the same other person, laptop plugged in, the same apps open.
2. Run:
   ```
   .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --no-models
   ```
   The first line should read `config: asr_threads=default asr_spin=on omp_passive=off capture_buffer=20 ms models=off beam=4`.
3. Talk for about **2 minutes** at the pace of test 1, with quick back-and-forth and both of you talking. The lines will say `(models off)`; that's expected.
4. Watch for any `!! Me: … LOST` lines while it runs.
5. Press Ctrl+C. Note the two lines starting `capture Me:` and `capture Remote:`.

**How to read it**
- **Both streams at 99.5% or higher, no LOST lines:** the mic is fine without models, which points at the models' CPU load. Next is test 3: models on with test 1's settings, to confirm the failure reproduces.
- **Mic clearly below that, or LOST lines appearing:** the models aren't the cause, and the three CPU mitigations are the wrong lever. Next we'd look at the audio thread and the driver.

Tell me when it's done. I'll read the log, record the result in TESTS.md, commit it, and then walk you through test 3.

Audio, logs and models are not in\nthe repo; the log folder names are given so results can be re-checked locally.\n\nMachine: Windows 11, Intel i5-13500H (12 physical / 16 logical cores), 7.6 GB\nusable RAM, no GPU. Python 3.13 in `.venv`. Devices: mic `[14]` Intel Smart\nSound microphone array (2 ch, 48 kHz); loopback `[16]` Galaxy Buds3 Pro\n\"Headphones\" endpoint (2 ch, 48 kHz). Call app: Google Meet in a browser.\n\n---\n\n## T-M0-1 - Capture both sources (2026-10-30 20:18)\n`recordings/20261030-201834`, `tools/m0_record.py --guided`, `tools/m0_check.py`\n\nMeasured:\n- No mic dropouts, 0 input overflows, max queue 1, no clipping (both streams).\n- Mic: 2,854,080 frames, file length 60.01 s = wall time 60.01 s.\n- Loopback: 2,857,920 frames, file 60.11 s vs wall 60.01 s (+0.10 s).\n- Separation: during remote-only speech (21-30 s) the mic stayed at its noise\n  floor (about -75 dB); during overlap (33-43 s) both streams carried speech at\n  -16 to -22 dB; the loopback was never idle (Meet keeps playing ~-99 dB).\n\nInferred: capture of both sources works; no leakage with the Buds.\nThe +0.10 s was later traced to the aligner anchoring a stream to its first\nbuffer (see D7); fixed in code, not yet re-measured on the device.\n\n## T-VAD-1 - Phrase segmentation on the M0 recording (offline)\n`tools/try_file.py --vad-only` with Silero 6.2.3 (PyPI copy), run in a Linux\nsandbox on the same laptop.\n\nMeasured: mic -> 9 phrases, all inside the stretches where the user spoke\n(5-17 s, 33-45 s); loopback -> 6 phrases inside 21-30 s and 33-43 s; no\nphrases in silence; none of the remote voice in the mic stream.\n\n## T-STUB - Logic tests without hardware (cloud workspace)\nSynthetic buffers through aligner -> converter -> segmenter -> worker with\nstub models. Verified: phrase end times within 20 ms; queue wait accounted\nwhen sources overlap; late first buffer + burst no longer shifts a stream;\nno zeros inserted into speech for late buffers; idle loopback gap filled;\na 7 % buffer loss is reported as lost (6.4 of 6.7 s) with delivered ratio\n0.929. These are logic tests only, not evidence about the real device.\n\n## T-MT-1 - Translation benchmark (2026-10-30 ~20:44, partial M1)\n`results/m1_mt_summary.json` - 100 FLEURS hy_am test sentences, **clean**\n(reference) Armenian input, NLLB-200-distilled-600M int8, 4 threads.\n\n| beam | chrF | BLEU | ms p50 | ms p95 | ms max |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | 61.08 | 35.38 | 1307 | 2486 | 3637 |\n| 4 | 61.74 | 36.29 | 1674 | 3543 | 5937 |\n\nPeak RAM 996 MB. Inferred: beam 1 costs ~0.7 chrF and is ~25-40 % faster;\nlong FLEURS sentences make MT the slowest stage. The ASR benchmark and the\nown-voice reading test were **not run** (skipped, see D9).\n\n## T-LIVE-0 - First live run (2026-10-30 21:04)\n`logs/20261030-210400`, default settings (beam 4, ASR threads = runtime default,\n20 ms capture buffer). Only the mic produced speech (4 phrases, 4.7 s audio).\n\nMeasured: mic VAD-wait component 0.56-0.60 s across 27-85 s (no growth;\nlinear fit slope 0.0007 s/s, i.e. sample clock at 99.9 % of wall time).\nLatency 2.2-3.2 s, all under 5 s. ASR mean 1.18 s, MT mean 1.10 s.\n\n## T-LIVE-1 - Two-person Meet call (2026-10-30 21:13) - FAILED (mic timing)\n`logs/20261030-211345`, same code and settings as T-LIVE-0. User report:\n\"when we talked a bit faster it did not catch all the words\".\n\nMeasured (per-phrase log, 14 mic + 11 remote phrases, 48.5 s of speech):\n- For each phrase the log has `vad_s` = (wall time the phrase was queued) -\n  (t0 + phrase end computed from the **sample count**). For a healthy stream\n  this is the 0.5 s end-of-phrase silence wait.\n- Remote: `vad_s` 0.50-0.55 s throughout (fit slope -0.0002 s/s).\n- Me: `vad_s` grew from 0.55 s (phrase ending at 4.0 s) to 7.07 s (phrase\n  ending at 91.5 s); linear fit `vad_s = -0.07 + 0.0769 t`.\n- The capture code logged 4315 buffers arriving > 0.3 s later than their\n  sample position predicted; max lateness 6.93 s. 0 input-overflow flags.\n- Latency: Me p50 4.62 s, p95 8.18 s, 6 of 14 over 5 s; Remote p50 1.85 s,\n  max 2.08 s, 0 over 5 s. ASR mean 0.44 s, MT mean 0.77 s, queue wait 0.\n- Raw sample counts per stream were **not** logged in this version, so the\n  ratio below is derived from timing, not counted.\n\nDerived: the mic's sample clock advanced at 1/(1+0.0769) = 92.9 % of wall\ntime, i.e. ~7 s of samples missing after ~90 s. Phrase timestamps for \"Me\"\nwere early by that amount (e.g. a reply stamped 74.0 s, before the remote\nsentence it answers, was really spoken around 79.8 s).\n\nInferred (not proven): the missing samples were never delivered (audio loss),\nwhich matches the user's missed words. Alternatives not yet excluded: the\ndevice running at a lower real sample rate under some condition, or samples\nlost inside PortAudio without an overflow flag. T-LIVE-0 and T-M0-1 show the\nsame mic delivering ~100 % of samples, so a fixed rate mismatch is unlikely.\n\nHypotheses (all **unconfirmed**):\n- H1 CPU starvation: ONNX Runtime (all cores, busy-waiting) and CTranslate2\n  (OpenMP) delay the mic's audio thread until WASAPI data is lost. Weak\n  support: T-LIVE-0 (4.7 s of speech processed) did not drift, T-LIVE-1\n  (48.5 s processed) did. Against: the loopback, under the same load, did\n  not drift.\n- H2 Python GIL contention delaying the PyAudio callback.\n- H3 Intel Smart Sound mic driver behaviour while Meet uses the same mic.\n\nAccuracy notes (same log): when the Armenian was right the English was right\n(\"Լսո՞ւմ ես։\" -> \"Do you hear me?\"; \"Որտե՞ղ եք ապրում։\" -> \"Where do you\nlive?\"). Bad lines started with bad recognition (\"Հեռեւ ձեզ, ո՞նցեքք\" for\n\"Բարև ձեզ, ո՞նց եք\" -> \"Away from you\"; a lone \"֊։\" -> invented \"What is it?\").\n\n## Pending\n- T-LIVE-2: models off (`--no-models`), test-1 settings. Separates H1 from H2/H3.\n- T-LIVE-3: models on, test-1 settings. Checks that the failure reproduces.\n- Then one mitigation at a time (see D10).\nEOF\necho written; wc -l TESTS.md"

~~~~~~~~~~~~json
        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && cat > DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'\n# Decisions\n\nEach entry: what was decided, why, and its status. \"Unverified\" means it has\nnot yet been confirmed on the target laptop.\n\n**D1 - System audio via WASAPI loopback (PyAudioWPatch).** Windows exposes a\nloopback twin of every output device, so no virtual cable (BlackHole\nequivalent) is needed and the user still hears the call. Verified in T-M0-1.\n\n**D2 - Microphone = laptop array `[14]`, not the Buds' mic.** Opening the\nBuds' \"Headset\" mic switches them to the Bluetooth hands-free profile; call\naudio then moves to a different endpoint and loopback `[16]` would go\nsilent. In-ear Buds also leak little sound into the laptop mic (T-M0-1).\n\n**D3 - ASR: NVIDIA FastConformer-Hybrid Large (hy), ONNX CTC export via\nonnx-asr.** Best open model on ArmBench-ASR v1.0 (combined WER 19.9 vs\nWhisper-large-v3 65.1), 115M params, runs without NeMo/PyTorch. Known risks:\n~61 % WER on conversational movie audio in that benchmark; trained on read\nEastern Armenian; CTC head (published numbers are RNN-T). Not benchmarked\nlocally (D9).\n\n**D4 - MT: NLLB-200 distilled 600M, int8 CTranslate2 (third-party\nconversion), Meta's own SentencePiece model.** Fits in ~1 GB RAM; T-MT-1:\nchrF 61-62 on clean FLEURS input. Licence CC-BY-NC (fine for this\nchallenge). Beam 4 is the current default; beam 1 is nearly as good and\nfaster (T-MT-1) - not changed yet.\n\n**D5 - Phrase segmentation: Silero VAD run frame by frame (32 ms) with its\nstate carried**, 0.5 s silence ends a phrase, 10 s maximum. Latency is\nmeasured from the end of the last speech frame. Verified offline (T-VAD-1).\n\n**D6 - One worker thread, FIFO across both sources.** Models never compete\nwith each other for CPU; overlapping speech shows up as measurable queue\nwait instead of hidden slowdowns. Labels are \"Me\" / \"Remote\" for now;\nper-speaker labels come later.\n\n**D7 - Sample-clock timing with a shared t0.** A stream's start time is the\nearliest arrival in a 0.5 s warm-up window (a late first buffer used to shift\nthe whole stream: T-M0-1's +0.10 s). Late buffers are never padded with\nzeros; zeros are inserted only for idle loopback, or when lateness has not\nrecovered for 1 s (confirmed loss), which is then reported as LOST.\nVerified with stub tests only.\n\n**D8 - Errors are reported, not hidden.** Lines over 5 s are flagged; lost\naudio, overflows, stalled devices and processing exceptions print `!!` lines\nlive and are listed in the session summary. Wordless ASR output is not sent\nto MT (NLLB invents sentences for it).\n\n**D9 - Skip the 100-clip ASR benchmark and own-voice reading test** (user\ndecision, 2026-10-30): prioritise an end-to-end walking skeleton. Cost: no\nlocal WER number; accent risk unmeasured.\n\n**D10 - Debug the microphone loss one variable at a time.** The baseline\ncommit already contains three mitigations applied together (ASR thread cap\n+ no spinning, `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE`, capture buffer 20 -> 50 ms). An\nimprovement with all three on would not show which one helped, so they are\nmade switchable, the default returns to the T-LIVE-1 configuration, and each\nis tested on its own after the failure is reproduced. Status: open.\nEOF\necho ok"

        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && cat > PLAN.md <<'EOF'\n# PLAN — Live Armenian → English transcription with speaker labels\n\n> Status (2026-10-30 evening): original plan, kept as written. Changes since:\n> M1 benchmarks were cut back to the translation benchmark only (D9), work\n> moved to an end-to-end walking skeleton, and speaker-embedding tests move to\n> M5. See DECISIONS.md and TESTS.md for what actually happened.\n\nStatus: planning only. Nothing installed or implemented yet.\nTarget machine: Windows 11, i5-13500H, 8 GB RAM, Intel Iris Xe (no CUDA). Everything runs on CPU.\n\n## 1. Goal\n\nBuild a Python terminal program that:\n- captures the **microphone** (labelled `Me`) and the **system audio** (the call side) at the same time;\n- cuts each stream into spoken phrases and transcribes them as Armenian text;\n- translates each phrase into English;\n- labels call-side phrases `Speaker 1`, `Speaker 2`, … and keeps each label stable for the whole session;\n- prints `[time] speaker / HY / EN`. The target is ≤ 5 s from the end of a phrase to its English line. This is **a target to measure, not a promise.**\n\nLocal models only. Keep it small. Spare time goes to reliability, not features.\n\n## 2. What the research changes\n\n| Finding | Source | Consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| NVIDIA FastConformer-Hybrid (hy), 115M params, is the **best open model** on the independent ArmBench-ASR v1.0 (combined WER 19.9; Whisper-large-v3 zero-shot 65.1). | ArmBench-ASR leaderboard; Karpov et al., Interspeech 2025 | Primary ASR candidate. It is small enough for CPU. |\n| Even that model scores **~61% WER on movie dialogue**, against 7.7% on Common Voice read speech. It was trained on read speech and its card calls it noise-sensitive. | ArmBench-ASR; model card | Conversational call audio is the **main quality risk**. The README must state this honestly. |\n| An **ONNX export** exists (CTC head, fp32) that runs with `onnx-asr` and ONNX Runtime. It needs **no NeMo or PyTorch**. There is no int8 version. | `OpenVoiceOS/stt_hy_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc_onnx` | It avoids installing NeMo on Windows. The paper's numbers are for the RNN-T head, so CTC quality must be measured. |\n| The model card says it is **non-streaming**. | model card | Run it once per VAD segment, not as a stream. |\n| Armenian fine-tunes of Whisper exist (turbo ~0.8B, large-v3) but rank **below** FastConformer on ArmBench and are 7–13× larger. | ArmBench-ASR | Fallback only, if FastConformer fails on our audio. |\n| Coria et al. (diart): rolling-buffer segmentation plus **incremental clustering**. New speaker if distance > δ_new. Update a centroid **only from long-enough segments** (ρ_update). Speaker confusion rises as latency drops. Labels improve as the conversation goes on. | Paper provided | Borrow the clustering rules and nothing else. Expect labels to be shaky in the first minute. |\n| Newer streaming diarizers exist (FASTDIAR 2026, ~10M params, 5× real-time on one CPU thread). | microsoft/fastdiar | Fallback only, if the simple approach measurably fails. |\n| sherpa-onnx ships ungated ONNX speaker-embedding models (3D-Speaker CAM++, WeSpeaker) for CPU. | sherpa-onnx docs | Gives speaker embeddings without pyannote or a Hugging Face token. |\n| Translation: NLLB-200 distilled 600M is available as CTranslate2 int8 (~0.6 GB). TranslateGemma-4B (Gemma terms) Q4 is ~2.5 GB. Gemma-3/NLLB-3.3B score well on hye→eng, but those sizes are too big here. | HF model cards; OpenWHO eval | NLLB-600M int8 is primary. TranslateGemma-4B is an optional experiment, only if RAM and latency allow. |\n| ArmBench and almost all training data are **Eastern Armenian**. | ArmBench; Chakmakjian & Wang 2022 | Your Western-influenced pronunciation on the mic is a specific risk. Test it explicitly. |\n\n**Not taken from the papers:** data collection, pseudo-labelling, fine-tuning, overlap-aware segmentation models, hyper-parameter optimisation pipelines.\n\n## 3. Architecture\n\n```\n mic (WASAPI)       ─► Capture ─► VAD/Segmenter ─┐\n loopback (WASAPI)  ─► Capture ─► VAD/Segmenter ─┤\n                                                 ▼\n                                        segment queue (FIFO)\n                                                 ▼\n                       Worker: Speaker → ASR → Translate → Printer\n```\n\n- One capture thread per source. One shared inference worker, because parallel models on 4 performance cores would fight each other. If measurement shows ASR and MT pipelining helps, that becomes a two-stage worker.\n- The pipeline is the same for live audio and for **WAV replay**, so every test can be repeated.\n- Every segment carries timestamps, logged at each stage, so latency is measured rather than guessed.\n\n## 4. Modules and their inputs/outputs\n\n| Module | Input | Output | Initial choice (to confirm in M1) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `audio/devices.py` | — | printed device list; resolved device IDs from `--mic` / `--loopback` | PyAudioWPatch (WASAPI loopback, no virtual cable) |\n| `audio/capture.py` | device ID | `(source, float32 mono 16 kHz chunk, t_capture)` | downmix + resample (soxr) |\n| `audio/segmenter.py` | chunks of one source | `Segment(source, t_start, t_end, audio)` | Silero VAD (ONNX); silence hang-over ~0.5 s; max segment length ~10 s (both tunable) |\n| `speakers.py` | `Segment` | `\"Me\"` for mic; `\"Speaker N\"` for loopback | CAM++ or ECAPA embedding + online cosine clustering with δ_new; centroid updated only for segments ≥ ~1.5 s |\n| `asr.py` | segment audio | Armenian text (punctuated) | FastConformer-hy ONNX (CTC) via onnx-asr |\n| `translate.py` | Armenian text | English text | NLLB-200-distilled-600M, CTranslate2 int8 |\n| `output.py` | labelled result + timings | terminal lines; optional `--debug-latency` column | plain print |\n| `pipeline.py` / `main.py` | CLI flags | wiring, threads, queue, shutdown | stdlib `threading` + `queue` |\n| `tools/replay.py`, `tools/bench_*.py` | WAV files | the same pipeline offline; metric tables | jiwer, sacrebleu |\n\nEach model module exposes one function so it can be swapped (`transcribe(audio) -> str`, `translate(text) -> str`, `assign(segment) -> label`). There are no plugin frameworks.\n\n## 5. Major risks\n\n1. **ASR quality on conversational and call audio.** The domain gap from read speech is large (ArmBench Movies ~61% WER). Codecs, noise, and short replies like «հա», «լավ» make it worse.\n2. **Western-accented speech on the mic.** The model is Eastern-trained and the accent effect is unmeasured.\n3. **CPU contention and latency.** Both sides plus the call app share one laptop. Backlog in the queue directly breaks the 5 s budget.\n4. **8 GB RAM.** Models (~2 GB estimated, *to measure*) plus Windows plus the call app plus a browser.\n5. **CTC vs RNN-T.** The ONNX export uses the CTC head. Quality may be below the published numbers.\n6. **Diarization on short segments.** Embeddings from segments under ~1–1.5 s are unreliable. Cold start produces label churn. A VAD segment may contain two speakers if there's no pause. Overlap is ignored. Codec audio can make voices sound alike.\n7. **Translation of noisy or fragmentary ASR output.** NLLB can hallucinate on very short or broken input. NLLB is CC-BY-NC, which is fine for this challenge but must be noted.\n8. **Windows audio quirks.** The loopback device changes when output switches between headphones, Bluetooth and speakers. Sample rates and channel counts vary.\n9. **Audio leakage without headphones.** Echo handling is out of scope, but leakage causes duplicate `Me` lines. This will be documented rather than fixed.\n\n## 6. Milestones and how each is tested\n\n| # | Milestone | Done when / test |\n|---|---|---|\n| M0 | **Audio capture.** List devices, pick them by flag, record mic and loopback together to WAV. | Record 60 s of a real call (Meet, Zoom, Telegram) with headphones and with speakers. Both WAVs are audible, there are no dropouts, and they are time-aligned. Unplugging or switching the device gives a clear error, not a hang. |\n| M1 | **Model spike (offline benchmark, decision gate).** No live code yet. | ASR: ~50 FLEURS `hy_am` + ~20 Common Voice clips + your own recordings, split into Eastern speakers and your voice. Report CER/WER, real-time factor and peak RAM for FastConformer-CTC, plus Whisper-turbo-hy as a reference. MT: ~100 FLORES hye→eng sentences, clean and with ASR output as input. Report chrF and ms per sentence for NLLB-600M, with TranslateGemma-4B only if RAM allows. Speakers: cosine-score distributions for same vs. different speaker at 1, 2 and 4 s. **Outputs: a choice of models plus written numbers for the README.** |\n| M2 | **Live segmentation.** VAD on both streams prints `[time] source segment-length`. | Replay WAVs at real-time speed and count segments against hand-marked phrases. Live: speaking short and long phrases creates no merged or chopped segments. Tune the hang-over and the maximum length here. |\n| M3 | **ASR in the loop.** Live Armenian text with latency logging. | Replay test set: CER matches M1, which shows the integration adds no errors. The latency log shows p50/p95 from end of segment to text. If p95 is already near 5 s, stop and re-plan before adding MT. |\n| M4 | **Translation in the loop.** | Same replay with EN output. Spot-check ~30 lines by hand (you're fluent in both languages). The p95 end-to-end latency is reported. |\n| M5 | **Speaker labels on loopback.** | Build a replay file of 3 known speakers taking alternating turns (from your recordings or CV clips with different `client_id`s). Report segment-level label accuracy and the number of spurious new speakers. Tune δ_new and the minimum update duration on this file only, then confirm on a second file. |\n| M6 | **Full live run and hardening.** | 30-min session with both sides active: RAM is stable, the queue doesn't grow, Ctrl+C exits cleanly. Rehearse the interview setup with ≥ 2 people on the call side, including you speaking with your accent. Record the honest results. |\n| M7 | **Deliverables.** | README: setup, devices, models with alternatives and numbers, architecture, limitations. Export every chat session to `chats/` as separate `.md` files. Confirm the repo contains no weights, audio or keys (`.gitignore` plus a final check). |\n\n**Decision gates:**\n- After M1: if FastConformer-CTC is clearly worse than expected, try exporting the RNN-T head or switching to the Whisper fallback.\n- After M3/M4: if latency is too high, shorten the maximum segment length, cut thread counts or use a smaller MT model.\n- After M5: only if label accuracy is clearly poor, consider a streaming diarizer (diart or FASTDIAR).\n\n## 7. Explicitly not doing\nGUI, packaging, echo cancellation, named or persistent speakers, saving transcripts, non-Armenian input, fine-tuning, LLM post-editing, or GPU/OpenVINO work. The last one is revisited only if M3/M4 latency forces it.\n\n## 8. References\n- Coria, Bredin, Ghannay, Rosset — *Overlap-aware low-latency online speaker diarization based on end-to-end local segmentation* (diart).\n- Karpov et al. — *From Scarcity to Sufficiency: Speech Recognition Pipeline for Zero-resource Language*, Interspeech 2025.\n- Metric AI Lab — ArmBench-ASR v1.0 leaderboard (metric-ai-armbench-asr.static.hf.space).\n- nvidia/stt_hy_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc; OpenVoiceOS ONNX export.\n- Torgashov & Köpüklü — FASTDIAR (arXiv 2610.02941), as a fallback only.\n- Chakmakjian & Wang — *Towards a Unified ASR System for the Armenian Standards*, DigitAm 2022.\nEOF\ngit add PLAN.md TESTS.md DECISIONS.md results/ && git diff --cached --stat && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nDocs: test log, decisions, original plan; record mic timing failure\n\n- TESTS.md: T-M0-1, T-VAD-1, stub tests, T-MT-1 (translation benchmark),\n  T-LIVE-0, and T-LIVE-1 (FAILED: mic sample clock at ~92.9 % of wall time,\n  derived from per-phrase timing; audio loss inferred; CPU starvation kept\n  as an unconfirmed hypothesis alongside GIL and driver hypotheses).\n- DECISIONS.md: D1-D10, including the plan to separate the three bundled\n  mitigations (D10).\n- PLAN.md: original plan with a status note on what changed.\n- results/: T-MT-1 outputs (text only).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsfqbdDUnntF4mME6PPVki\nEOF\ngit log --oneline"

Defaults = T-LIVE-1 config;\n    # change ONE per test run.\n    ap.add_argument(\"--asr-threads\", type=int, default=None, help=\"ONNX Runtime threads (default: all cores)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--asr-no-spin\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"stop ONNX Runtime busy-waiting between runs\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--omp-passive\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"set OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE for CTranslate2\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--capture-buffer-ms\", type=int, default=20, help=\"PortAudio buffer per callback\")'''),\n('''    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    import pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio''', '''    args = ap.parse_args()\n    if args.omp_passive:                          # must be set before ctranslate2 is imported\n        os.environ[\"OMP_WAIT_POLICY\"] = \"PASSIVE\"\n    print(f\"config: asr_threads={args.asr_threads or 'default'} asr_spin={'off' if args.asr_no_spin else 'on'} \"\n          f\"omp_passive={'on' if args.omp_passive else 'off'} capture_buffer={args.capture_buffer_ms} ms \"\n          f\"models={'off' if args.no_models else 'on'} beam={args.beam}\")\n\n    import pyaudiowpatch as pyaudio'''),\n('''            asr = Transcriber(models.ASR_DIR, threads=args.asr_threads)''',\n'''            asr = Transcriber(models.ASR_DIR, threads=args.asr_threads, spin=not args.asr_no_spin)'''),\n('''            pipes[name] = (seg, conv, CaptureStream(pa, dev, t0, lambda pcm, s=seg, c=conv: s.push(c(pcm)),\n                                                    on_loss=loss_warning(label)))''',\n'''            pipes[name] = (seg, conv, CaptureStream(pa, dev, t0, lambda pcm, s=seg, c=conv: s.push(c(pcm)),\n                                                    buffer_s=args.capture_buffer_ms / 1000,\n                                                    on_loss=loss_warning(label)))'''),\n])\nprint(\"patched\")\nPYEOF\ncd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && python3 $HOME/patch_flags.py . && md5sum livetrans/asr.py livetrans/audio/capture.py livetrans/__main__.py && git diff --stat"

      "stop_timestamp": null,
      "flags": null,
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Three commits are in, and none claims anything passes:\n\n| Commit | What |\n|---|---|\n| `e7817a9` | Unverified debugging baseline: the code as it stood after live test 1 |\n| `1f710b5` | TESTS.md, DECISIONS.md, the original PLAN.md, and the translation benchmark results |\n| `b72c767` | The three mitigations made switchable; with no flags the program runs test 1's configuration |\n\n**What's tracked and what isn't**\n- `git check-ignore` confirmed that `recordings\\`, `logs\\`, `models\\`, `data\\`, `.venv\\` and `__pycache__` are all ignored.\n- No audio, model or environment file was staged; only source, docs and text results are tracked.\n- Deleting in your GitHub folder was enabled, but I only let git use it inside this project.\n\n**How TESTS.md records the microphone problem**\n- **Measured:** for each of your phrases, the gap between when the phrase was handed off and when its sample count said it ended. That gap grew from 0.55 s to 7.07 s (fit: 0.0769 s per second). The remote side stayed flat at 0.50–0.55 s, and there were zero overflow flags.\n- **Derived, not counted:** the mic's sample clock ran at 92.9% of real time. Test 1 never logged raw sample counts; the new version does.\n- **Inferred:** the samples were never delivered. Two alternatives are listed alongside: the device running at a lower true rate under some condition, and samples being lost inside the audio library without an overflow flag.\n- **Hypotheses, all unconfirmed:** CPU starvation, Python's single-thread lock (the GIL) delaying the audio callback, and the Intel mic driver while Meet shares the mic.\n\nThe CPU hypothesis has some evidence each way. The run at 21:04, with only 4 phrases to process, didn't drift; test 1, with 25, did. Against it, the remote stream didn't drift under the same load.\n\n## Test 2: models off\n\nThis checks whether your mic loses audio when no recognition or translation runs. Everything else matches test 1.\n\n1. Same setup as test 1: Meet call in the browser, the Buds, the same other person, laptop plugged in, the same apps open.\n2. Fair question, and answering it precisely shows I overstated what option 1 would fix.
~~~~~~~~~~~~

**Definition.** A "real letter" means a character from the Armenian alphabet (Ա–Ֆ, ա–և). Punctuation and symbols such as `։ ՞ ֊ .` and spaces don't count. The rule: **translate only if the recognised text has at least 2 Armenian letters; otherwise print the Armenian alone.**

**What that fixes in your log: 3 lines, not 7.**

| Recognised | Letters | Now translated as | With the rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| «Հ։» (twice) | 1 | "A: What are you talking about?" | skipped |
| «Ս։» | 1 | "Q. What is this?" | skipped |
| «Հովհ.» | 4 | "John: How did you know?" | **still translated** |
| «Հահ։» | 3 | "Oh, my God." | **still translated** |
| «Հ է։» | 2 | "That's right." | still translated (reasonable here) |

«Հովհ» and «Հահ» look like words to any letter count, so this rule can't catch them; telling those apart would need a different approach. So it's a small cleanup, not the fix for the quality problem. That remains recognition.

A letter means a character from the Armenian alphabet (Ա–Ֆ, ա–և). Punctuation such as `։ ՞ ֊ .` and spaces don't count.

**Checked against your last conversation:** I ran all 36 recognised lines from the log through the new rule. **Exactly 3 lines change**: «Հ։» twice and «Ս։» once, which had been turned into "A: What are you talking about?" and "Q. What is this?". The other 33 are untouched.

**What it doesn't fix:**
- «Հովհ.» → "John: How did you know?" and «Հահ։» → "Oh, my God." have 3–4 letters, so a letter count can't catch them.
- My earlier "~7 lines" was an overstatement; this rule fixes 3. TESTS.md records that correction.
- The real quality problem is still recognition.

It hasn't been seen in a live run yet. It will show up the next time you run the same command; nothing else about running it changed.

## Steps on your laptop

Keep it plugged in and close Meet during these runs, so the timings aren't disturbed.

**E0. Check the pins**, about 1 minute; it should end with `ALL OK`:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans.models --verify
```

**E1. Warm-up**, about 5 minutes; six fresh processes:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\warmup_check.py
```

**Correct the call references** (about 10 minutes, needs you as a native speaker). Open `eval\t-live-4_refs.jsonl` in VS Code. For each line:
1. Play the WAV named in `"wav"`.
2. Replace `"ref_hy"` with what was actually said.
3. Change `"ref_status"` to `"confirmed"`.

The 5 lines marked `"beam_check": true` are required; all 14 Remote lines are better. If a clip is only laughter or a sound, set `"ref_hy": ""`.

**E2. Beam 1 vs 4**, about 1 minute. Then tell me which English lines are right:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\beam_check.py
```

**E3. Recognition: CTC vs RNN-T.** First download the RNN-T fp32 files (about 455 MB) into `models\`:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans.models --only asr-rnnt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\asr_compare.py --model ctc  --set fleurs
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\asr_compare.py --model rnnt --set fleurs
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\asr_compare.py --model ctc  --set calls
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\asr_compare.py --model rnnt --set calls
```

Every step writes its results to `results\`, where I'll read them. You can stop after any step and tell me. Once E3 is in, I'll pin the RNN-T revision that was tested and record everything.           "type": "text",
~~~~~~~~~~~~json
          "text": "**Model:** Vana-Labs/stt-fastconformer-armenian, an ONNX export of NVIDIA's Armenian ASR model.\n\n- **Base model:** nvidia/stt_hy_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc, which performs speech recognition with punctuation and capitalization.\n- **Decoder head:** The page says the export covers the \"transducer (RNNT) branch.\" The config is `nemo-conformer-rnnt`. CTC and TDT are not mentioned.\n- **Format:** ONNX, with both int8 and full-precision (fp32) files. The int8 files use onnxruntime dynamic quantization.\n- **Task and tags:** Automatic speech recognition. Tags include Armenian, fastconformer, rnnt, and onnx-asr.\n- **Purpose:** Built for Tetro, a local meeting transcriber for macOS.\n\n**How to run:**\n- **onnx-asr** is the documented route. Load with `onnx_asr.load_model(\"nemo-conformer-rnnt\", \"<folder>\", quantization=\"int8\")`, then call `recognize()` on a 16 kHz mono WAV file.\n- The page says any runtime that loads NeMo Parakeet ONNX models should also work.\n- NeMo was used for export and as the reference decoder. The page does not mention sherpa-onnx.\n\n**Files:**\n\n| File | Size | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `encoder-model.int8.onnx` | 125 MB | Dynamic int8 quantization |\n| `decoder_joint-model.int8.onnx` | 5 MB | Dynamic int8 quantization |\n| `encoder-model.onnx` | 435 MB | Full precision |\n| `decoder_joint-model.onnx` | 20 MB | Full precision |\n| `nemo80.onnx` | 87 KB | 80-band log-mel preprocessor, taken from onnx-asr |\n| `vocab.txt` | 13 KB | 1024 SentencePiece tokens plus `<blk>` (index 1024) |\n| `config.json` | not listed | onnx-asr config: 80 features, subsampling 8 |\n\nThe `scripts/` folder is referenced as containing the export and quantization code.\n\n**Training data:** Not described on the page.\n\n**WER/CER:** Not reported. The page says accuracy is inherited from the base model and points to its model card. The only check described is on three Common Voice hy-AM test clips, where NeMo's RNNT decoder and this export produced the same text at both precisions. That shows the export matches NeMo, not its accuracy. The page also notes the model sometimes writes \"եւ\" where \"և\" might be expected.\n\n**License:** CC-BY-4.0, the same as the base model. Credit goes to NVIDIA.\n\n**Last commit/revision:** Not shown. The page links to \"Files and versions\" and \"Community\" but displays no commit hash or date.\n\n**Other details:** The page lists 0 likes, 40 downloads last month, and no Inference Provider deployment. It also shows three quantized variants of the base model on the Hub."

If a download was interrupted, delete that folder under models/ and rerun.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    fetch_all()\n48:def download(model_dir: str | Path = \"models/mt-nllb-600m-int8\") -> Path:\n49-    \"\"\"Fetch the CT2 model and the official SentencePiece model into model_dir.\"\"\"\n50-    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download, snapshot_download\n51-\n52-    model_dir = Path(model_dir)\n53-    snapshot_download(NLLB_CT2_REPO, local_dir=model_dir)\n54-    hf_hub_download(NLLB_SPM_REPO, SPM_FILE, local_dir=model_dir)\n55-    return model_dir\n"

download the core models at their pinned revisions\n  python -m livetrans.models --only asr-rnnt # download one optional model\n  python -m livetrans.models --verify        # check file hashes and runtime versions\n\nRevisions are the commits that were actually tested (read from the\nhuggingface_hub download metadata of the files in use, 2026-10-30).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport hashlib\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nASR_DIR = ROOT / \"models\" / \"asr-hy-fastconformer\"\nASR_RNNT_DIR = ROOT / \"models\" / \"asr-hy-fastconformer-rnnt\"\nMT_DIR = ROOT / \"models\" / \"mt-nllb-600m-int8\"\nVAD_DIR = ROOT / \"models\" / \"vad-silero\"\n\nMODELS = {\n    \"vad\": dict(\n        repo=\"istupakov/silero-vad-onnx\", revision=\"b3e3ee3cce4c11ceb63b1a0b229d916069c1ddf6\",\n        dir=VAD_DIR, patterns=[\"silero_vad.onnx\", \"config.json\"],\n        sha256={\"silero_vad.onnx\": \"1a153a22f4509e292a94e67d6f9b85e8deb25b4988682b7e174c65279d8788e3\"}),\n    \"asr-ctc\": dict(  # NVIDIA FastConformer-Hybrid Large hy, CTC head, fp32 ONNX export\n        repo=\"OpenVoiceOS/stt_hy_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc_onnx\",\n        revision=\"f7db1fad9af6bd8a7a9e08fca02068c403b35468\",\n        dir=ASR_DIR, patterns=[\"model.onnx\", \"vocab.txt\", \"config.json\"],\n        sha256={\"model.onnx\": \"09ed4278c8536193f5324ae5b1e21be3ef1abaa92779e8c7b4577644071b131a\"}),\n    \"mt\": dict(  # NLLB-200 distilled 600M, third-party CTranslate2 int8 conversion\n        repo=\"JustFrederik/nllb-200-distilled-600M-ct2-int8\",\n        revision=\"302d78f00e6fdb50a1064059df7c392b735e9d05\",\n        dir=MT_DIR, patterns=None,\n        sha256={\"model.bin\": \"ed1beaf75134de7505315a5223162f56acff397eff6b50638a500d3936fe707b\"}),\n    \"mt-spm\": dict(  # Meta's own SentencePiece model for NLLB\n        repo=\"facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M\", revision=\"f8d333a098d19b4fd9a8b18f94170487ad3f821d\",\n        dir=MT_DIR, patterns=[\"sentencepiece.bpe.model\"],\n        sha256={\"sentencepiece.bpe.model\": \"14bb8dfb35c0ffdea7bc01e56cea38b9e3d5efcdcb9c251d6b40538e1aab555a\"}),\n    # --- optional / under evaluation (not used by the live program) ---\n    \"asr-rnnt\": dict(  # same NVIDIA weights, RNN-T (transducer) head, fp32 files only\n        repo=\"Vana-Labs/stt-fastconformer-armenian\", revision=None,   # pinned after evaluation\n        dir=ASR_RNNT_DIR,\n        patterns=[\"encoder-model.onnx\", \"decoder_joint-model.onnx\", \"vocab.txt\", \"config.json\"],\n        sha256={}, optional=True),\n}\nCORE = [k for k, m in MODELS.items() if not m.get(\"optional\")]\n\n\ndef vad_model_path() -> Path:\n    override = os.environ.get(\"LIVETRANS_VAD_MODEL\")     #   t_asr = time.perf_counter() - t\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        en = mt.translate(hy) if hy else \"\"\n        t_mt = time.perf_counter() - t\n        steps.append({\"step\": name, \"asr_s\": round(t_asr, 3), \"mt_s\": round(t_mt, 3), \"hy\": hy, \"en\": en})\n    return {\"mode\": mode, \"load_s\": round(load_s, 2), \"warmup_s\": round(warm_s, 2), \"steps\": steps}\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--runs\", type=int, default=3)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--beam\", type=int, default=4)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--clips\", nargs=3, default=DEFAULT_CLIPS)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--child\", choices=(\"minimal\", \"representative\"))\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n    if args.child:\n        print(json.dumps(child(args.child, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n            if out.returncode != 0:\n                print(out.stderr[-2000:])\n                return 1\n            r = json.loads(out.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])\n            runs.append(r)\n            s = {x[\"step\"]: x for x in r[\"steps\"]}\n            print(f\"run {i + 1} {mode:15} load {r['load_s']:.1f}s warm-up {r['warmup_s']:.1f}s | \"\n                  + \" | \".join(f\"{k}: asr {v['asr_s']:.2f} mt {v['mt_s']:.2f}\" for k, v in s.items()), flush=True)\n\n    print(\"\\nmedian over runs     rs = [r for r in runs if r[\"mode\"] == mode]\n        med = lambda f: round(statistics.median(f(r) for r in rs), 3)\n        step = lambda name, k: med(lambda r: next(x for x in r[\"steps\"] if x[\"step\"] == name)[k])\n        summary[mode] = {\"load_s\": med(lambda r: r[\"load_s\"]), \"warmup_s\": med(lambda r: r[\"warmup_s\"]),\n                         **{f\"{n}_{k}\": step(n, k) for n in (\"clip1 first\", \"clip1 again\", \"clip2\", \"clip3\")\n                            for k in (\"asr_s\", \"mt_s\")}}\n        m = summary[mode]\n        print(f\"{mode:15} {m['load_s']:5.1f}       "text": "Committed (`7373d6d`). Next, the WAV reader gets support for 32-bit float files like FLEURS. It will still return the same 16-bit format to the rest of the code, so nothing else changes.",

      "stop_timestamp": null,
      "flags": null,

      "id": "toolu_01XmzfYWxgWcBFmwE72HevL7",
      "name": "mcp__remote-devices__device_bash",
      "input": {
        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && python3 - <<'EOF'\np=\"livetrans/audio/wavio.py\"; s=open(p,encoding=\"utf-8\").read()\nold='''def read_wav(path: str | Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:\n    \"\"\"Returns (int16 array shaped (frames, channels), sample_rate).\"\"\"\n    with wave.open(str(path), \"rb\") as w:\n        if w.getsampwidth() != 2:\n            raise ValueError(f\"{path}: only 16-bit PCM WAV is supported\")\n        rate, ch = w.getframerate(), w.getnchannels()\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.int16).reshape(-1, ch)\n    return pcm, rate'''\nnew='''def read_wav(path: str | Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:\n    \"\"\"Returns (int16 array shaped (frames, channels), sample_rate).\n    Accepts 16-bit PCM and 32-bit float WAV (FLEURS ships float32); float is\n    scaled and clipped to int16 so callers see one format.\"\"\"\n    raw = Path(path).read_bytes()\n    if raw[:4] != b\"RIFF\" or raw[8:12] != b\"WAVE\":\n        raise ValueError(f\"{path}: not a RIFF/WAVE file\")\n    fmt = data = None\n    i = 12\n    while i + 8 <= len(raw):\n        cid, size = raw[i:i + 4], struct.unpack(\"<I\", raw[i + 4:i + 8])[0]\n        body = raw[i + 8:i + 8 + size]\n        if cid == b\"fmt \":\n            fmt = body\n        elif cid == b\"data\":\n            data = body\n        i += 8 + size + (size & 1)\n    if fmt is None or data is None:\n        raise ValueError(f\"{path}: missing fmt or data chunk\")\n    tag, ch, rate, _, _, bits = struct.unpack(\"<HHIIHH\", fmt[:16])\n    if tag == 0xFFFE and len(fmt) >= 26:              # WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE: real tag in SubFormat\n        tag = struct.unpack(\"<H\", fmt[24:26])[0]\n    if tag == 1 and bits == 16:\n        pcm = np.frombuffer(data, dtype=\"<i2\").reshape(-1, ch)\n    elif tag == 3 and bits == 32:\n        x = np.frombuffer(data, dtype=\"<f4\").reshape(-1, ch)\n        pcm = np.clip(np.round(x * 32767.0), -32768, 32767).astype(np.int16)\n    else:\n        raise ValueError(f\"{path}: unsupported WAV format (tag {tag}, {bits} bit)\")\n    return pcm, rate'''\nassert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new).replace(\"import wave\\n\",\"import struct\\nimport wave\\n\",1)\nopen(p,\"w\",encoding=\"utf-8\").write(s)\nEOF\n. $HOME/evalenv/bin/activate && python - <<'EOF'\nimport sys, wave, json, numpy as np\nsys.path.insert(0, \".\")\nfrom livetrans.audio.wavio import read_wav\n# 16-bit file: must match the stdlib reader exactly\np = \"logs/20261030-221541/00019.81_Remote.wav\"\nwith wave.open(p) as w: ref = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), np.int16).reshape(-1, w.getnchannels())\npcm, r = read_wav(p); print(\"int16 identical:\", np.array_equal(pcm, ref), pcm.shape, r)\np = \"recordings/20261030-201834/loopback.wav\"\nwith wave.open(p) as w: ref = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), np.int16).reshape(-1, w.getnchannels())\npcm, r = read_wav(p); print(\"int16 stereo identical:\", np.array_equal(pcm, ref), pcm.shape, r)\n# float32 FLEURS file\nrow = json.loads(open(\"data/fleurs_hy.jsonl\", encoding=\"utf-8\").readline())\npcm, r = read_wav(\"data/\" + row[\"wav\"]); print(\"FLEURS float32:\", pcm.shape, r, \"peak\", int(np.abs(pcm).max()))\nEOF",
~~~~~~~~~~~~
