Time per translation = median of 5\nrepeats after a warm-up. English quality is judged by a person (no automatic\nscore on 5 phrases). Writes results/beam_check.json.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport statistics\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom importlib.metadata import version\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nsys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    from livetrans import models\n    from livetrans.translate import Translator\n\n    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in (ROOT / \"eval\" / \"t-live-4_refs.jsonl\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines()\n            if l.strip()]\n    rows = [r for r in rows if r.get(\"beam_check\")]\n    unconfirmed = [r[\"wav\"] for r in rows if r.get(\"ref_status\") != \"confirmed\"]\n    if unconfirmed:\n        print(\"WARNING: references not confirmed yet for:\", *unconfirmed, sep=\"\\n  \")\n    tr = Translator(models.MT_DIR)\n    tr.translate(\"Բարև ձեզ, ո՞նց եք։\")                       # warm-up\n    results = []\n    for r in rows:\n        for kind in (\"ref_hy\", \"asr_hy\"):\n            entry = {\"wav\": r[\"wav\"], \"input\": kind, \"hy\": r[kind], \"ref_status\": r.get(\"ref_status\")}\n            for beam in (1, 4):\n                tr.beam_size = beam\n                times = []\n                for _ in range(5):\n                    t = time.perf_counter()\n                    en = tr.translate(r[kind])\n                    times.append(time.perf_counter() - t)\n                entry[f\"en_b{beam}\"] = en\n                entry[f\"ms_b{beam}\"] = round(statistics.median(times) * 1000)\n            results.append(entry)\n            print(f\"\\n{kind:6} HY: {entry['hy']}\\n  beam1 ({entry['ms_b1']:4d} ms): {entry['en_b1']}\"\n                  f\"\\n  beam4 ({entry['ms_b4']:4d} ms): {entry['en_b4']}\", flush=True)\n    b1 = [e[\"ms_b1\"] for e in results]\n    b4 = [e[\"ms_b4\"] for e in results]\n    summary = {\"phrases\": len(rows), \"translations_per_beam\": len(results),\n               \"ms_median_b1\": statistics.median(b1), \"ms_median_b4\": statistics.median(b4),\n               \"same_output\": sum(e[\"en_b1\"] == e[\"en_b4\"] for e in results),\n               \"ctranslate2\": version(\"ctranslate2\"), \"python\": sys.version.split()[0], \"platform\": sys.platform}\n    print(\"\\n\" + json.dumps(summary, indent=1))\n    (ROOT / \"results\").mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n    (ROOT / \"results\" / \"beam_check.json\").write_text(json.dumps({\"summary\": summary, \"results\": results},\n                                                                  indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\nEOF\n. $HOME/evalenv/bin/activate && timeout 175 python tools/beam_check.py 2>&1 | tail -30; rm -f results/beam_check.json results/asr_ctc_fleurs.json",

Fixed and committed (`b834391`).

**Cause:** the Windows console and pipes default to the cp1252 encoding, which has no Armenian letters. The live program already switched its output to UTF-8; my three new tools didn't. `warmup_check.py` failed because its child process prints the recognised Armenian into a pipe.

**Fix:** all three tools now switch to UTF-8 at start, and `warmup_check.py` also tells its child processes to do the same.

**Verified:** I reproduced your exact error in the sandbox by forcing cp1252. With the fix, `warmup_check.py`, `asr_compare.py` and `beam_check.py` all run under that same setting. The crashed run left nothing in `results\`, so nothing needs cleaning up.

Rerun from E1; nothing else changed:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\warmup_check.py
```
If you haven't run E0 yet (`python -m livetrans.models --verify`), please do; it prints only plain text, so it wasn't affected. Then continue with the reference corrections, E2 and E3 as listed before.

**About the cut, I checked the file.** At 0.69 s into the clip there are **391 ms of exact digital silence**: every sample is precisely zero. A live microphone never produces that; even your quiet room sits around −75 dB. That silence was **inserted by my own code**:
- When the mic stream falls behind and doesn't catch up, the program re-aligns the clock by inserting silence (D7).
- The silence goes in at the moment the lag is detected, which here was in the middle of your sentence.
- So the cut isn't the Buds. Your mic in these runs is the laptop's array (`[14]`); the Buds are only the output. Noise cancellation wouldn't produce exact zeros either.

The underlying shortfall is still real: those frames never arrived. But putting all of it into one 0.4 s hole mid-word is my doing, and it can break words for the recogniser. The words survived here. A better approach would correct the timestamps without touching the audio. I'll note it in TESTS.md as a found defect and not change it now, so we finish the references first.

The remote clip also has exact-zero stretches (0.1–0.17 s), but in the pauses. That's Meet sending true digital silence, which is normal.

E2 ran on your laptop (Windows, ctranslate2 4.8.4) with the corrected «Ես Երեւանում» reference. Here's my reading of the English; please correct any line you judge differently.

| Phrase (what was actually said) | Beam 1 | Beam 4 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Հաճելի է, իմ անունը գարուն է | It's nice. My name is Spring. | same | OK (name translated literally) |
| Ես Երեւանում, դո՞ւք | I'm coming, are you? | same | **wrong**: "Yerevan" dropped |
| Ես Վանաձորից եմ | I'm from Vancouver. | same | **wrong**: place name |
| Ես զբաղվում եմ կլինիկական հետազոտություններ հետ | I'm in clinical trials. | same | OK |
| Մեր մոտ ժամը տաս տասնհինգ անց | We're about 10:15 in the morning. | It's about 10:15 in the morning. | mostly OK ("morning" was added) |

On the **recognised** Armenian, all five come out wrong with both beams, because the input is wrong. Beam 4 sometimes drops the invented part ("It's a wall." disappears) but doesn't fix the meaning.

**Result:**
- **Quality:** with the corrected Armenian, beam 1 and beam 4 give the same translation in 4 of 5 phrases, and the fifth differs by one word. Across all 10 translations, 6 are identical. Neither beam fixes the two place-name errors.
- **Speed:** beam 1 is about 50 ms faster on these short phrases (median 204 vs 256 ms). On longer FLEURS sentences (T-MT-1) the saving was larger, 1.31 vs 1.67 s typical and 2.49 vs 3.54 s at the 95th percentile, at a cost of 0.7 chrF.
- **Where the errors come from:** the remaining translation errors are place names («Երեւանում», «Վանաձոր»). That's a model limitation, not a beam setting.

**My recommendation:** switch the default to beam 1. On short call phrases the saving is small, but it's 20–30% on long sentences, which is exactly where the 5 s budget is at risk, and no quality loss showed up on your phrases. I haven't changed anything yet. I'll record E2 now, and switch the default only if you agree.

## E3: recognition, CTC vs RNN-T

The recognition model's file stays the same; only the decoder head differs. The call-audio set uses the **4 confirmed intact clips** (21 words), which is only enough to illustrate. FLEURS, with 100 clips and about 2,000 words, is where a real difference can show.

Laptop plugged in, Meet closed:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans.models --only asr-rnnt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\asr_compare.py --model ctc  --set fleurs
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\asr_compare.py --model rnnt --set fleurs
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\asr_compare.py --model ctc  --set calls
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\asr_compare.py --model rnnt --set calls
```
- The first command downloads the RNN-T fp32 files, about 455 MB, into `models\asr-hy-fastconformer-rnnt\`.
- Each comparison prints one line per clip and saves a result file in `results\`. The FLEURS runs take about 1–2 minutes each.

Tell me when they're done. I'll compare the two heads, including the exact words where they differ, pin the RNN-T revision you downloaded, and record it all. RNN-T int8 is tested only if RNN-T fp32 comes out better.

E3 is recorded and committed (`cdb7cca`), and the tested RNN-T revision is now pinned with both file hashes verified. (The "SOMETHING DIFFERS" line in that check is only the sandbox's runtime versions; all model files are OK.)

## E3 result: no measurable winner, so CTC stays

On **100 FLEURS clips (1,930 words)**, same model weights, only the decoder head different:

| | CTC (current) | RNN-T |
|---|---|---|
| Word error rate (95% range) | 11.9% (9.8–14.2) | 11.4% (9.3–13.6) |
| Time per clip (11.7 s of audio) | 0.15 s | 0.77 s (~5× slower) |

- **RNN-T made 10 fewer word errors out of 1,930.** On individual clips it was better on 25, worse on 15 and equal on 60.
- **That difference could easily be chance:** the 95% range is −1.3 to +0.3 points, which includes zero, and the sign test gives p = 0.15. So Karpov et al.'s RNN-T-over-CTC result doesn't show up clearly on our data.
- **On the 4 call clips RNN-T scored worse (7 vs 5 errors)**, but 21 words can't support a conclusion, and one of its "errors" comes from a spelling quirk in the reference.
- **The live default stays CTC, and the int8 step (E4) is skipped,** because its precondition, RNN-T fp32 being better, wasn't met.

## How well the current model works (CTC)

**FLEURS read speech, 100 clips:**
- **Words:** about **88%** recognised correctly (WER 11.9%); character error rate **5.0%**, so many wrong words are near-misses (one letter or one ending).
- **Whole clips:**
  - 28% were perfect, with no wrong word.
  - **58%** had at most 1 wrong word in 10.
  - 32% had 1–3 wrong words in 10.
  - 10% had more than 3 in 10.
  - None had more than half the words wrong; the worst clip was 50%.

**Your call (T-LIVE-4), much less data:**
- **Words:** about **76%** correct on the 4 checked Remote clips (5 errors in 21 words), and none of the 4 was perfect.
- **Translation on correct Armenian (E2):** 3 of 5 acceptable; 2 wrong, both on place names.
- **Latency:** Remote lines 100% within 5 s (14 of 14). Your lines 91% (20 of 22); the two misses were the first two lines of the session.

**Read these numbers carefully.** FLEURS is clean, read, Eastern Armenian, the easiest kind of speech for this model. Conversational call audio is clearly harder (76% vs 88% here, from very few clips), and the earlier ArmBench benchmark found much worse results on film dialogue. The call-audio numbers rest on 4 clips, so treat them as indicative only.

## Options for next

1. **Beam 1:** still awaiting your yes or no. It's a one-line change, recommended for latency.
2. **More call references:** confirming the other 10 Remote clips (about 10 minutes) would make the call-audio comparison meaningful. That's the domain the interview actually tests.
3. **The silence-insertion defect:** fix the timestamps without inserting silence into your mic audio.
4. **The place-name translation errors:** try the larger NLLB-1.3B int8 (about 1.4 GB) as a one-variable experiment on the same 5 phrases plus FLEURS.

I'd do 1 and 3 next, since both are small, measurable and directly improve what you see live. Option 2 would strengthen any further model decisions.

        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && python3 - <<'EOF'\nimport json, sys, math, random\nimport numpy as np\nsys.path[:0] = [\".\", \"tools\"]\nfrom asr_compare import edits\nfrom m1_common import normalize_hy\ndef load(n): return json.load(open(f\"results/{n}.json\", encoding=\"utf-8\"))\nfor setname in (\"fleurs\", \"calls\"):\n    c, r = load(f\"asr_ctc_{setname}\")[\"clips\"], load(f\"asr_rnnt_{setname}\")[\"clips\"]\n    assert [x[\"wav\"] for x in c] == [x[\"wav\"] for x in r]\n    n = len(c)\n    print(f\"\\n===== {setname}: {n} clips =====\")\n    for name, rows in ((\"CTC\", c), (\"RNN-T\", r)):\n        we = np.array([x[\"word_errors\"] for x in rows]); rw = np.array([x[\"ref_words\"] for x in rows])\n        cwer = we / np.maximum(rw, 1)\n        # character errors per clip\n        ce = np.array([edits(list(normalize_hy(x[\"ref_hy\"])), list(normalize_hy(x[\"hyp_hy\"]))) for x in rows])\n        rc = np.array([len(normalize_hy(x[\"ref_hy\"])) for x in rows])\n        t = np.array([x[\"asr_s\"] for x in rows]); d = np.array([x[\"audio_s\"] for x in rows])\n        print(f\"{name:6} WER {we.sum()/rw.sum():.2%}  word accuracy {1-we.sum()/rw.sum():.2%}  CER {ce.sum()/rc.sum():.2%}\")\n        print(f\"       clips perfect (0 word errors): {np.mean(we==0):.0%} | per-clip WER <=10%: {np.mean(cwer<=.10):.0%} | 10-30%: {np.mean((cwer>.10)&(cwer<=.30)):.0%} | >30%: {np.mean(cwer>.30):.0%} | >50%: {np.mean(cwer>.5):.0%}\")\n        print(f\"       per-clip WER median {np.median(cwer):.1%}, worst {cwer.max():.0%} | time per clip median {np.median(t):.3f}s p95 {np.percentile(t,95):.3f}s max {t.max():.3f}s for {d.mean():.1f}s avg audio\")\n    dc = np.array([x[\"word_errors\"] for x in c]); dr = np.array([x[\"word_errors\"] for x in r]); rw = np.array([x[\"ref_words\"] for x in c])\n    better, worse, same = int((dr < dc).sum()), int((dr > dc).sum()), int((dr == dc).sum())\n    print(f\"paired: RNN-T fewer errors on {better} clips, more on {worse}, same on {same}; identical text on {sum(a['hyp_hy']==b['hyp_hy'] for a,b in zip(c,r))}\")\n    # sign test (two-sided, exact binomial on non-tied clips)\n    k, m = min(better, worse), better + worse\n    p = min(1.0, 2 * sum(math.comb(m, i) for i in range(k + 1)) / 2**m) if m else 1.0\n    print(f\"sign test p = {p:.3f}\")\n    # paired bootstrap of WER difference (RNN-T - CTC), clip resampling\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(0); B = 10000\n    idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=(B, n))\n    diff = (dr[idx].sum(1) - dc[idx].sum(1)) / rw[idx].sum(1)\n    lo, hi = np.percentile(diff, [2.5, 97.5])\n    print(f\"WER difference RNN-T - CTC = {(dr.sum()-dc.sum())/rw.sum():+.2%} (95% bootstrap CI {lo:+.2%} .. {hi:+.2%}); P(RNN-T better) = {np.mean(diff<0):.2f}\")\nEOF\nfor f in encoder-model.onnx decoder_joint-model.onnx; do echo \"$f: rev $(head -1 models/asr-hy-fastconformer-rnnt/.cache/huggingface/download/$f.metadata) etag $(sed -n 2p models/asr-hy-fastconformer-rnnt/.cache/huggingface/download/$f.metadata)\";       "text": "E3 is recorded and committed (`cdb7cca`), and the tested RNN-T revision is now pinned with both file hashes verified. Conversational call audio is clearly harder (76% vs 88% here, from very few clips), and the earlier ArmBench benchmark found much worse results on film dialogue. For a healthy stream\n  this is the 0.5 s end-of-phrase silence wait.\n- Remote: `vad_s` 0.50-0.55 s throughout (fit slope -0.0002 s/s).\n- Me: `vad_s` grew from 0.55 s (phrase ending at 4.0 s) to 7.07 s (phrase\n  ending at 91.5 s); linear fit `vad_s = -0.07 + 0.0769 t`.\n- The capture code logged 4315 buffers arriving > 0.3 s later than their\n  sample position predicted; max lateness 6.93 s. 0 input-overflow flags.\n- Latency: Me p50 4.62 s, p95 8.18 s, 6 of 14 over 5 s; Remote p50 1.85 s,\n  max 2.08 s, 0 over 5 s. ASR mean 0.44 s, MT mean 0.77 s, queue wait 0.\n- Raw sample counts per stream were **not** logged in this version, so the\n  ratio below is derived from timing, not counted.\n\nDerived: the mic's sample clock advanced at 1/(1+0.0769) = 92.9 % of wall\ntime, i.e. a shortfall of ~7 s of samples after ~90 s. Phrase timestamps for \"Me\"\nwere early by that amount (e.g. a reply stamped 74.0 s, before the remote\nsentence it answers, was really spoken around 79.8 s).\n\nHypothesis (not proven): the missing samples were never delivered,\nwhich matches the user's missed words. Alternatives not yet excluded: the\ndevice running at a lower real sample rate under some condition, or samples\nlost inside PortAudio without an overflow flag. T-LIVE-0 and T-M0-1 show the\nsame mic delivering ~100 % of samples, so a fixed rate mismatch is unlikely.\n\nHypotheses (all **unconfirmed**):\n- H1 CPU starvation: ONNX Runtime (all cores, busy-waiting) and CTranslate2\n  (OpenMP) delay the mic's audio thread until WASAPI data is lost. Weak\n  support: T-LIVE-0 (4.7 s of speech processed) did not drift, T-LIVE-1\n  (48.5 s processed) did. Against: the loopback, under the same load, did\n  not drift.\n- H2 Python GIL contention delaying the PyAudio callback.\n- H3 Intel Smart Sound mic driver behaviour while Meet uses the same mic.\n\nAccuracy notes (same log): when the Armenian was right the English was right\n(\"Լսո՞ւմ ես։\" -> \"Do you hear me?\"; \"Որտե՞ղ եք ապրում։\" -> \"Where do you\nlive?\"). Bad lines started with bad recognition (\"Հեռեւ ձեզ, ո՞նցեքք\" for\n\"Բարև ձեզ, ո՞նց եք\" -> \"Away from you\"; a lone \"֊։\" -> invented \"What is it?\").\n\n## T-LIVE-2 - Models off, T-LIVE-1 settings (2026-10-30 21:54) - mic frame shortfall REPRODUCED\n`logs/20261030-215404`, commit b72c767, `--no-models` (capture + resampling +\nSilero VAD only; no ASR/MT loaded), capture buffer 20 ms, same Meet call setup.\nPlanned 2 min; the run lasted **15.6 s** (user stopped it), so ratios are coarse.\n\nMeasured (`summary.json` -> `capture`; sample counts are now logged):\n- Me: delivered_ratio 0.840 (frames received / frames expected since the\n  stream's first sample); 3 unrecovered-lag events totalling 1.57 s (live\n  warnings at ~10 s and ~12 s, about 0.5 s each); 6 late-but-recovered events;\n  max lateness 0.556 s; 0 overflow flags.\n- Remote: delivered_ratio 0.993; 0 unrecovered-lag events; max lateness 0.003 s.\n- 4 phrases (3 Me, 1 Remote), latency 0.54-0.96 s (VAD wait only).\n\nInferred:\n- The mic shows the frame shortfall **without** any ASR/MT CPU load, so H1 (model CPU\n  starvation) cannot be the sole cause. Whether model load makes it worse is\n  unknown. The ASR/OMP mitigations from D10 are therefore not the first lever.\n- ~~The shortfall comes in ~0.5 s blocks~~ **Corrected after T-REC-2:** the ~0.5 s\n  events are an artefact of the lag detector (it confirms a deficit once\n  lateness has exceeded 0.3 s for 1 s), so a steady shortfall also shows up\n  as regular ~0.45 s events. The data do not show whether the shortfall is bursty.\n- 1.57 s of unrecovered lag in ~14.7 s explains ~11 %; the rest of the 16 % gap is\n  lateness still unconfirmed when the run stopped (lag is only logged as unrecovered\n  after 1 s without recovery).\n\nContrast with T-M0-1: same mic, same Meet setup with remote speech, 20 ms\nbuffer, same CaptureStream class -> 100 % delivered over 60 s. Difference: the\nrecorder only writes WAV per buffer; the live program also resamples (soxr)\nand runs Silero VAD per buffer in the drain thread. T-M0-1 ran with the older\naligner, but frame counts are independent of the aligner.\n\nHypotheses now (unconfirmed):\n- H2 Python-side: work in the drain threads (GIL contention) delays the\n  PyAudio callback of the mic until WASAPI drops data.\n- H3 environment: Intel Smart Sound driver / Meet sharing the mic; a\n  condition that differed from the T-M0-1 session (time-varying).\n- H1 model CPU load: may still contribute; not the sole cause.\n\n## T-REC-2 - Plain recorder in the same Meet call (2026-10-30 22:01) - mic frame shortfall REPRODUCED\n`recordings/20261030-220126`, commit 7938c53, `tools/m0_record.py --seconds 120`,\n20 ms buffer; no VAD, no resampling, no models (per buffer: write WAV only).\nBoth people talked (mic active 36 %, loopback 31 % of 50 ms frames).\nUser impression after the run: \"no problem in capturing the sounds\".\n\nMeasured (raw frame counts from PortAudio, independent of the aligner):\n- Mic: 4,985,280 frames = 103.86 s over 118.91 s since its first sample ->\n  **0.873** delivered; 32 unrecovered-lag events (14.70 s) at a regular ~3 s spacing,\n  each 0.35-0.50 s, in speech and in silence alike; 41 late-but-recovered;\n  0 overflow flags.\n- Loopback: 5,718,720 frames = 119.14 s over 118.87 s -> 1.002; no shortfall.\n\nInferred:\n- The plain recorder shows a mic frame shortfall of the same order as the\n  live program, so neither the models (H1) nor the live pipeline's per-buffer\n  work (H2) is necessary for the shortfall.\n- The regular spacing matches a steady deficit of ~13 % seen through the\n  detector (0.127 s/s reaches the 0.3 s threshold, is confirmed 1 s later at\n  ~0.43 s, then resets), see the correction under T-LIVE-2.\n- The user's listening impression and the frame counts disagree; the frame\n  counts are taken as the evidence. Not yet known: whether the shortfall is\n  dropped packets (missing audio) or the device delivering at a lower actual\n  rate (time-stretched audio) - per-buffer timing is needed to tell.\n\nMic delivery over time (same device, same 20 ms buffer):\n\n| Test | Time | Mic delivered | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| T-M0-1 | 20:18 | 1.000 | recorder, Meet call |\n| T-LIVE-0 | 21:04 | 0.999 (derived) | live, models on, mic only |\n| T-LIVE-1 | 21:13 | 0.929 (derived) | live, models on, both talking |\n| T-LIVE-2 | 21:54 | 0.840 (15 s run) | live, models off |\n| T-REC-2 | 22:01 | 0.873 | recorder, Meet call |\n\nLeading hypothesis now: **H3 environment** - a condition that started between\n21:04 and 21:13 and persisted (candidates: Meet's use of the same mic, e.g. its\naudio processing; Bluetooth activity; power/thermal state). What is this?\"; \"Հովհ.\" -> \"John: How did you know?\").\n  The existing filter only skips output with no Armenian letter at all.\n\nInferred: recognition is the largest error source; MT adds errors on short\ncolloquial phrases and names; one-letter outputs are a separate, cheap-to-fix\ndefect. \"Me\" errors may be partly caused by the mic frame shortfall.\n\n## T-OFF-1 - Minimum-letters rule replayed on T-LIVE-4 output (offline)\nChange: translate only if the recognised text has >= 2 Armenian alphabet\nletters (Ա-Ֆ, ա-և; punctuation/spaces not counted); otherwise print the\nArmenian with \"(not translated ...)\".           "type": "text",
          "text": "# Decisions\n\nEach entry: what was decided, why, and its status. \"Unverified\" means it has\nnot yet been confirmed on the target laptop.\n\n**D1 - System audio via WASAPI loopback (PyAudioWPatch).** Windows exposes a\nloopback twin of every output device, so no virtual cable (BlackHole\nequivalent) is needed and the user still hears the call. Verified in T-M0-1.\n\n**D2 - Microphone = laptop array `[14]`, not the Buds' mic.** Opening the\nBuds' \"Headset\" mic switches them to the Bluetooth hands-free profile; call\naudio then moves to a different endpoint and loopback `[16]` would go\nsilent. In-ear Buds also leak little sound into the laptop mic (T-M0-1).\n\n**D3 - ASR: NVIDIA FastConformer-Hybrid Large (hy), ONNX CTC export via\nonnx-asr.** Best open model on ArmBench-ASR v1.0 (combined WER 19.9 vs\nWhisper-large-v3 65.1), 115M params, runs without NeMo/PyTorch. Known risks:\n~61 % WER on conversational movie audio in that benchmark; trained on read\nEastern Armenian; CTC head (published numbers are RNN-T). Not benchmarked\nlocally (D9).\n\n**D4 - MT: NLLB-200 distilled 600M, int8 CTranslate2 (third-party\nconversion), Meta's own SentencePiece model.** Fits in ~1 GB RAM; T-MT-1:\nchrF 61-62 on clean FLEURS input. Licence CC-BY-NC (fine for this\nchallenge). Beam 4 is the current default; beam 1 is nearly as good and\nfaster (T-MT-1) - not changed yet.\n\n**D5 - Phrase segmentation: Silero VAD run frame by frame (32 ms) with its\nstate carried**, 0.5 s silence ends a phrase, 10 s maximum. Latency is\nmeasured from the end of the last speech frame. Verified offline (T-VAD-1).\n\n**D6 - One worker thread, FIFO across both sources.** Models never compete\nwith each other for CPU; overlapping speech shows up as measurable queue\nwait instead of hidden slowdowns. Labels are \"Me\" / \"Remote\" for now;\nper-speaker labels come later.\n\n**D7 - Sample-clock timing with a shared t0.** A stream's start time is the\nearliest arrival in a 0.5 s warm-up window (a late first buffer used to shift\nthe whole stream: T-M0-1's +0.10 s). Beam 1 holds up live: **all 34 lines came in under 5 seconds** (worst 1.46 s, typical about 1.0 s). It's recorded and committed (`1b5ed69`) and stays the default.

| | T-LIVE-4 (beam 4, yesterday) | T-LIVE-5 (beam 1, today) |
|---|---|---|
| Lines | 36 | 34 |
| Latency, typical / worst | 1.7–2.0 s / 5.32 s | **1.0 s / 1.46 s** |
| Lines over 5 s | 2 | **0** |
| Translation time per line | 0.70–0.80 s | 0.37–0.41 s |
| Recognition time per line | 0.34–0.49 s | 0.06 s |

The two runs differ in more than the beam setting. Recognition also got about 6× faster even though nothing about it changed, so part of today's speed is the laptop's state, not beam 1. The like-for-like test on identical sentences (E2) credits beam 1 with about 50 ms per short phrase. TESTS.md records it that way.

**Also seen in this run:**
- **The single-letter rule worked live:** «Հ։» showed up untranslated. «Հ հ։», «Հովհ։» and «Սովհ։» still got invented English; that's the known limit of a letter count.
- **«Այո» was translated as "I did."** It's correctly kept translatable, but NLLB's English is wrong here.
- **Your mic delivered 99.2% of its audio today**, against 87–91% yesterday, with the same settings. The cause of yesterday's shortfall is still unknown; it's recorded as varying between sessions.
- **Most wrong English still starts with wrong Armenian**, for example «Առեւ ձեզ» for «Բարեւ ձեզ», which became "Without you".

**Git housekeeping:** yesterday's permission to delete files had expired, so git left two lock files behind. I renewed the permission, removed only git's own lock and temp files, and checked the repository; it's clean.

## Next: remote speaker labels ("Speaker 1", "Speaker 2", …)

The plan, small and with no new package:
- **Voice fingerprints.** onnx-asr, already installed, can also compute a speaker embedding, a numeric fingerprint of a voice. I'll check that it really runs on your laptop before relying on it.
- **Labelling.** Each Remote phrase gets compared with the speakers seen so far. A close match reuses that label; otherwise it becomes a new speaker. Fingerprints only learn from phrases long enough to be reliable (the rule from the diart paper in the plan).
- **"Me" lines stay "Me".**

**I need one thing from you to test it:** a short recording with **at least two different people on the call side**. All recordings so far have one remote speaker (Գարուն), so they can't show whether two voices get told apart. About 2 minutes with two remote people taking turns is enough:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --save-audio
```
Note roughly who spoke when, for example "Speaker A first, then B, then A". I'll first tune and score the labelling offline on those saved phrases, then switch it on live. After that comes the final acceptance test.

Can you arrange a call with two remote people?

## Message 64 — assistant — 10/31/2026 13:33:40

Yes, two people on the same device works fine. On the call side, every remote voice arrives mixed into the one system-audio stream anyway, whether the people share a device or each have their own. The program can't tell devices apart, so it separates speakers by **voice alone**. Two people on one phone or laptop is a valid test of exactly that.

A few things make the test clean:
- **Take turns, with a short pause** (half a second or more) between speakers. A phrase containing both voices gets only one label, so overlapping speech on the remote side would muddy the result.
- **Sit at a similar distance from that device's mic.** If one person is much farther away, their voice arrives quieter and more echoey. That's realistic, but it makes the two harder to compare fairly.
- **Each person should speak several times, including a few longer sentences** of 2 seconds or more. The voice fingerprint is unreliable on very short replies like «հա».
- **Note roughly who spoke when**, for example "A, B, A, A, B…", so I can score the labels.

If the two voices are similar, say both male or both female, that makes a harder and more useful test.

You stay on your laptop as usual ("Me"). Run:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --save-audio
```
About 2 minutes is enough. Tell me when it's done, along with the speaker order you noted.

Speaker labelling is implemented, committed (`14b127d`), and switched **off by default** until it's verified on real voices. The recognition and translation pipeline is unchanged: without the new flag, the output is exactly as before.

## What the saved files show about the missed speech

The latest log is the 17:34 two-remote-speaker recording (`logs\20261031-173439`).

- **Capture:**
  - **Remote:** your laptop received 99.9% of the remote audio, and my code inserted nothing into it. But **every one of the 28 remote clips contains stretches of exact digital silence**: about 0.15–0.2 s at the start and end, and in several clips mid-sentence (one gap is 0.47 s). That silence comes from **Meet itself**: its noise suppression mutes quiet or distant speech before sending it. So part of the brother's speech never reached the laptop at all.
  - **Me:** your mic had 6 small shortfall events, but none landed inside your saved phrases this time.
- **Phrase detection:** inside the saved phrases there's no sign of trouble. Only 1 of 44 clips starts mid-sound, and none was cut at the 10 s limit. **But only detected phrases are saved.** Speech the detector never picked up, and anything between phrases, isn't on disk, so these files can't show whether speech was missed there.
- **Recognition:** errors like «Հ մազերը» for «Ձեր մազերը» occur in clips that start right after Meet's silence. Whether Meet muted the first sound or the model misheard it can't be separated from these files. Accent effects need your references.

I ran this inspection in the sandbox. It only reads the saved files, with no models and no timing, so the numbers are the same on any system. I've recorded that exception in D13; tell me if you'd rather I keep the sandbox for editing and git only.

## How speaker labels work

- **Fingerprints:** each remote phrase of 1 second or more gets a voice fingerprint from a small model, WeSpeaker ResNet34, about 26 MB. onnx-asr runs it, so no new package.
- **Labelling:** a phrase similar enough to a known speaker gets that speaker's label; otherwise it starts a new one. Only phrases of 1.5 s or more can start a new speaker or update a speaker's profile.
- **Short replies:** phrases under 1 s keep the previous remote label.
- **"Me" lines stay "Me".**

**Logic test (stub fingerprints):** A → B → A gives Speaker 1 → Speaker 2 → Speaker 1, and three voices stay apart. It also exposed a limitation: a very short reply from B right after A gets labelled as A.

        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && cat > tools/inspect_session.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Inspect a live session's log and saved phrase audio (deterministic file analysis).\n\n  python tools/inspect_session.py logs/20261031-173439\n\nSeparates what the files CAN show from what they cannot:\n- capture: delivered ratio, unrecovered-lag events (summary.json), and runs of exact\n  digital zeros inside saved phrases (mic: inserted by our aligner; loopback: usually\n  the call app's own digital silence);\n- phrase detection: phrases that start with speech already loud in the first 50 ms\n  (the 0.2 s pre-roll may have clipped the onset), and phrases cut at the 10 s maximum;\n- recognition: needs user references (eval/*.jsonl); not judged here.\nOnly detected phrases are saved (--save-audio). Speech that the VAD never detected,\nand audio between phrases, is not on disk, so this tool cannot say whether any was missed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\nfrom livetrans.audio.wavio import read_wav_float  # noqa: E402\n\nFRAME = 800                  # 50 ms at 16 kHz\nZERO_MIN = 160               # exact-zero runs >= 10 ms are reported\nONSET_HOT_DB = -6.0          # first 50 ms within 6 dB of the phrase's loud level = speech already under way\n\n\ndef zero_runs(x: np.ndarray, rate: int) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:\n    z = np.concatenate([[0], (x == 0).astype(np.int8), [0]])\n    d = np.diff(z)\n    starts, ends = np.flatnonzero(d == 1), np.flatnonzero(d == -1)\n    return [(s / rate, (e - s) / rate) for s, e in zip(starts, ends) if e - s >= ZERO_MIN]\n\n\ndef db(x: np.ndarray) -> float:\n    return float(10 *           "text": "\"\"\"Segment queue -> ASR -> translation -> terminal, with per-segment latency.\n\nLatency of a line = time it is printed - moment the speaker stopped (segment.end_s\non the shared sample clock). It is split into:\n  vad   - waiting for the end-of-phrase silence (min_silence) + capture delivery\n  queue - waiting behind other segments (the single worker is busy)\n  asr   - speech recognition\n  mt    - translation\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport queue\nimport re\nimport sys\nimport threading\nimport time\nimport traceback\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom livetrans.segmenter import Segment\n\nLABELS = {\"mic\": \"Me\", \"loopback\": \"Remote\"}\nARMENIAN_LETTER = re.compile(\"[\\u0531-\\u0556\\u0561-\\u0587]\")\n# NLLB invents whole sentences for one-letter input (\"Հ։\" -> \"A: What are you talking\n# about?\", T-LIVE-4), so text with fewer Armenian letters than this is shown untranslated.\nMIN_LETTERS_TO_TRANSLATE = 2\n\n\ndef armenian_letters(text: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Number of Armenian alphabet letters (Ա-Ֆ, ա-և); punctuation and spaces don't count.\"\"\"\n    return len(ARMENIAN_LETTER.findall(text))\nBUDGET_S = 5.0\n\n\ndef hms(seconds: float) -> str:\n    s = int(seconds)\n    return f\"{s // 3600:02d}:{s % 3600 // 60:02d}:{s % 60:02d}\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Stats:\n    rows: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)\n    failures: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)\n    empty_asr: int = 0\n    max_queue: int = 0\n\n\nclass Worker(threading.Thread):\n    \"\"\"Single consumer: models run one segment at a time so they never fight for CPU.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, asr, mt, t0: float, log_dir: Path | None = None, save_audio: bool = False):\n        super().__init__(daemon=True, name=\"worker\")\n        self.asr, self.mt, self.t0 = asr, mt, t0\n        self.q: queue.Queue[Segment | None] = queue.Queue()\n        self.stats = Stats()\n        self.log_dir, self.save_audio = log_dir, save_audio\n        self._print_lock = threading.Lock()\n        self._log = open(log_dir / \"segments.jsonl\", \"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") if log_dir else None\n\n    # called from capture threads\n    def submit(self, seg: Segment) -> None:\n        seg_t_queued = time.perf_counter()\n        self.q.put((seg, seg_t_queued))\n        depth = self.q.qsize()\n        self.stats.max_queue = max(self.stats.max_queue, depth)\n        if depth >= 3:\n            self.say(f\"!! backlog: {depth} segments waiting - latency will exceed the budget\")\n\n    def stop(self) -> None:\n        self.q.put(None)\n\n    def say(self, text: str) -> None:\n        with self._print_lock:\n            print(text, flush=True)\n\n    def run(self) -> None:\n        while (item := self.q.get()) is not None:\n            seg, t_queued = item\n            try:\n                self._process(seg, t_queued)\n            except Exception as e:  # report and keep going\n                msg = f\"{LABELS[seg.source]} @ {hms(seg.start_s)}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}\"\n                self.stats.failures.append(msg)\n                self.say(f\"!! processing failed - {msg}\")\n                traceback.print_exc()\n\n    def _process(self, seg: Segment, t_queued: float) -> None:\n        t_start = time.perf_counter()\n        if self.asr is None:                     # --no-models diagnostic mode\n            hy = \"(models off)\"\n        else:\n            hy = self.asr.transcribe(seg.audio)\n        t_asr = time.perf_counter()\n        translatable = armenian_letters(hy) >= MIN_LETTERS_TO_TRANSLATE\n        en = self.mt.translate(hy) if (translatable and self.mt is not None) else \"\"\n        t_mt = time.perf_counter()\n\n        speech_end_wall = self.t0 + seg.end_s\n        total = t_mt - speech_end_wall\n        parts = {\"vad\": t_queued - speech_end_wall, \"queue\": t_start - t_queued,\n                 \"asr\": t_asr - t_start, \"mt\": t_mt - t_asr}\n        label = LABELS[seg.source]\n        dur = len(seg.audio) / 16_000\n        flag = \"  !! OVER 5 s\" if total > BUDGET_S else \"\"\n        timing = (f\"latency {total:.1f}s = vad {parts['vad']:.1f} + queue {parts['queue']:.1f} \"\n                  f\"+ asr {parts['asr']:.1f} + mt {parts['mt']:.1f}  ({dur:.1f}s audio\"\n                  f\"{', cut at max length' if seg.forced else ''}){flag}\")\n        if not translatable and self.asr is not None:\n            self.stats.empty_asr += 1\n            self.say(f\"[{hms(seg.start_s)}] {label}   (not translated: fewer than {MIN_LETTERS_TO_TRANSLATE} \"\n                     f\"Armenian letters{' in ' + repr(hy) if hy else ''}; {timing})\")\n        else:\n            self.say(f\"[{hms(seg.start_s)}] {label}\\n  HY: {hy}\\n  EN: {en}\\n  .. {timing}\")\n\n        row = {\"source\": seg.source, \"label\": label, \"start_s\": round(seg.start_s, 2),\n               \"end_s\": round(seg.end_s, 2), \"audio_s\": round(dur, 2), \"forced\": seg.forced,\n               \"hy\": hy, \"en\": en, \"latency_s\": round(total, 3),\n               **{f\"{k}_s\": round(v, 3) for k, v in parts.items()}}\n        self.stats.rows.append(row)\n        if self._log:\n            self._log.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n            self._log.flush()\n        if self.save_audio and self.log_dir:\n            from livetrans.audio.wavio import write_wav16k\n            write_wav16k(self.log_dir / f\"{seg.start_s:08.2f}_{label}.wav\", seg.audio)\n\n\ndef summarize(stats: Stats) -> dict:\n    out: dict = {\"segments\": len(stats.rows), \"empty_asr\": stats.empty_asr,\n                 \"failures\": stats.failures, \"max_queue_depth\": stats.max_queue, \"by_source\": {}}\n    for src, label in LABELS.items():\n        lat = np.array([r[\"latency_s\"] for r in stats.rows if r[\"source\"] == src])\n        if lat.size == 0:\n            out[\"by_source\"][label] = {\"segments\": 0}\n            continue\n        rows = [r for r in stats.rows if r[\"source\"] == src]\n        out[\"by_source\"][label] = {\n            \"segments\": int(lat.size),\n            \"latency_p50_s\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 50)), 2),\n            \"latency_p95_s\": round(float(np.percentile(lat, 95)), 2),\n            \"latency_max_s\": round(float(lat.max()), 2),\n            \"over_budget\": int((lat > BUDGET_S).sum()),\n            \"mean_parts_s\": {k: round(float(np.mean([r[f\"{k}_s\"] for r in rows])), 2)\n                             for k in (\"vad\", \"queue\", \"asr\", \"mt\")},\n        }\n    return out\n\n\ndef {s['latency_p50_s']}s, \"\n              f\"p95 {s['latency_p95_s']}s, max {s['latency_max_s']}s, over 5 s: {s['over_budget']}  \"\n              f\"[mean vad {p['vad']} / queue {p['queue']} / asr {p['asr']} / mt {p['mt']}]\")\n    problems = capture_problems + [f\"processing: {f}\" for f in summary[\"failures\"]]\n    print(\"failures: \" + (\"none\" if not problems else \"\"))\n    for p in problems:\n        print(f\"  - {p}\")\n    sys.stdout.flush()\n            pass\n\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--list-devices\", action=\"store_true\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--mic\", type=int)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--loopback\", type=int)\n    # Candidate mitigations for the mic frame       "name": "mcp__remote-devices__device_bash",
      "input": {
        "command": "cd $HOME/mnt/GitHub/live-armenian-translation && cat > livetrans/speakers.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Remote-speaker labels: \"Speaker 1\", \"Speaker 2\", ... for loopback phrases.\n\nEach remote phrase gets a voice embedding (WeSpeaker ResNet34 via onnx-asr); the\ntracker compares it with the speakers seen so far (cosine similarity to each\nspeaker's centroid). Online, incremental - the rules borrowed from Coria et al.\n(diart), nothing else:\n  - similarity >= threshold to the best speaker  -> that speaker;\n  - otherwise a NEW speaker, but only from a phrase long enough to trust\n    (min_new_s); a shorter phrase is given the best existing speaker instead;\n  - a speaker's centroid is updated only from phrases >= min_update_s, so short,\n    noisy phrases cannot drag a voice profile toward someone else;\n  - phrases shorter than min_embed_s are not embedded at all: they inherit the\n    previous remote label (backchannels like «հա» carry too little voice).\nLabels never change after they are printed. Microphone phrases are always \"Me\"\nand never reach this module. Thresholds are tuned in tools/speaker_check.py.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport time\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nRATE = 16_000\n\n\nclass WeSpeakerEmbedder:\n    \"\"\"WeSpeaker ONNX model through onnx-asr (no extra package).\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, model_dir: str | Path, threads: int | None = 2):\n        import onnxruntime as rt\n        from onnx_asr.loader import Manager\n\n        opts = rt.SessionOptions()\n        if threads:\n            opts.intra_op_num_threads = threads\n        self.se = Manager(opts, [\"CPUExecutionProvider\"]).create_se(None, Path(model_dir))\n\n    def __call__(self, audio: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        return np.asarray(self.se.embedding(audio.astype(np.float32), sample_rate=RATE), dtype=np.float32)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Decision:\n    label: str\n    speaker: int                  # 1-based\n    reason: str                   # \"match\" | \"new\" | \"short-inherit\" | \"short-first\" | \"no-new-best\" | \"cap-best\"\n    similarity: float | None      # cosine to the chosen speaker (None if not embedded)\n    embed_s: float                # time spent computing the embedding\n    updated: bool                 # centroid updated with this phrase\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SpeakerTracker:\n    embed: callable\n    threshold: float = 0.45\n    min_embed_s: float = 1.0\n    min_new_s: float = 1.5\n    min_update_s: float = 1.5\n    max_speakers: int = 8\n    sums: list[np.ndarray] = field(default_factory=list)       # unnormalised sums of embeddings\n    counts: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)\n    last: int | None = None\n\n    def _centroids(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        c = np.stack(self.sums)\n        return c / np.linalg.norm(c, axis=1, keepdims=True)\n\n    def _new(self, e: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        self.sums.append(e.copy())\n        self.counts.append(1)\n        return len(self.sums) - 1\n\n    def assign(self, audio: np.ndarray) -> Decision:\n        dur = len(audio) / RATE\n        if dur < self.min_embed_s:\n            if self.last is None:                 # nothing known yet: provisional Speaker 1, no centroid\n                self.last = 0\n                return Decision(\"Speaker 1\", 1, \"short-first\", None, 0.0, False)\n            return Decision(f\"Speaker {self.last + 1}\", self.last + 1, \"short-inherit\", None, 0.0, False)\n\n        t = time.perf_counter()\n        e = self.embed(audio)\n        embed_s = time.perf_counter() - t\n        e = e / (np.linalg.norm(e) + 1e-12)\n\n        if not self.sums:\n            k = self._new(e)\n            self.last = k\n            return Decision(f\"Speaker {k + 1}\", k + 1, \"new\", None, embed_s, True)\n\n        sims = self._centroids() @ e\n        best = int(np.argmax(sims))\n        sim = float(sims[best])\n        if sim >= self.threshold:\n            k, reason = best, \"match\"\n        elif dur < self.min_new_s:\n            k, reason = best, \"no-new-best\"       # too short to found a new speaker\n        elif len(self.sums) >= self.max_speakers:\n            k, reason = best, \"cap-best\"\n        else:\n            k = self._new(e)\n            self.last = k\n            return Decision(f\"Speaker {k + 1}\", k + 1, \"new\", sim, embed_s, True)\n\n        updated = dur >= self.min_update_s\n        if updated:\n            self.sums[k] += e\n            self.counts[k] += 1\n        self.last = k\n        return Decision(f\"Speaker {k + 1}\", k + 1, reason, sim, embed_s, updated)\nEOF\necho ok"

emb((0.003 * np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(24_000)).astype(np.float32))   # warm-up\n    cache, times = {}, []\n    for a, d in zip(audio, durs):\n        if d >= min_embed:\n            t Speaker labels basically work on the real audio, and fingerprints are cheap (35 ms per phrase), but the threshold needed changing. Recorded and committed (`0b09b0e`).

**What the results say:**
- **0.45 was too strict:** it split your sister into 3 different "speakers".
- **0.25–0.35 found exactly two speakers**, and agreed with your labels on 24 of 26 clips (92%). So I've set the default to **0.30**, the middle of that range.
- **The two mistakes at 0.30:**
  - **Clip 8** (brother, 1.35 s) is too short to start a new speaker, so it was put with the sister.
  - **Clip 10** (sister, the one you said was "not clear") sounded different enough that it **became "Speaker 2"**, and the brother's clips then joined it. The two people did end up apart, but "Speaker 2" was started by a muddled clip of the sister, not by the brother.
- **Same-person clips aren't very similar here** (average 0.34, against 0.11 for sister-vs-brother). Meet's audio processing and the brother's distance blur voices, so two similar-sounding people could get merged at 0.30.
- **A → B → A passed at 0.45** (clips 1 → 14 → 16 gave Speaker 1 → 2 → 1), but I haven't checked it at the new threshold yet.

The threshold was tuned on the same clips it's scored on, and the brother has only 4 clips. So this is a starting point; the separate live call is the real test. Labelling stays off by default until that passes.

- **Both remote people close to the phone,** at a similar distance. Last time, the brother's distance was the biggest problem.
- **Take turns with full sentences of 2 seconds or more**, and include a clear **A → B → A** stretch near the start. A few short replies are fine.
- **Note the order**, for example "A, B, A, A, B, …", so I can score it.
- **About 2–3 minutes.**

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --speakers --save-audio
```
The first line should end with `speakers=on (threshold 0.3)`. Remote lines will show **Speaker 1 / Speaker 2**, and your lines stay **Me**. Each line's timing will include a `spk` part, so the latency cost of labelling is measured live.

A → B → A **passes at 0.30** on the real clips (Speaker 1 → 2 → 1), and the fingerprint step costs about 40 ms per phrase. Both are recorded.

Since a second remote person isn't available, I've added a substitute live test (commit `53a9f72`). Instead of a call, two FLEURS readers are played into your headphones:
- **A** = one woman's 29 s recording, cut into 5 pieces.
- **B** = one man's 31 s recording, cut into 5 pieces.
- **Order:** A B A B B A A B A B, so it starts with A → B → A.

The live program hears this through the loopback exactly as it hears a call, and the scorer knows exactly who spoke when. This audio was never used for tuning. It's easier than a real call, though: there's no Meet processing, and a woman against a man is easier to separate than two similar voices. TESTS.md says so. A real two-person call stays part of the final acceptance test.

## How to run it (T-SPK-2)

You need **two PowerShell windows** in the project folder, with the Buds connected as the output and nobody talking.

**Window 1:** start the live program and wait for "Listening…":
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --speakers --save-audio
```

**Window 2:** find the output device whose loopback is `[16]`, which should be the Buds "Headphones":
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\play_speakers.py --list-outputs
```
Then play the sequence, putting that device's index in place of `N`:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\play_speakers.py --output N
```
- It counts down 3 seconds, then plays for about 75 seconds. You'll hear it in the Buds.
- In Window 1, the lines should come up as **Speaker 1 / Speaker 2**.
- When Window 2 says "saved results\play_….json", press **Ctrl+C in Window 1**.

**Then score it** in either window, using the two names it printed:
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\score_playback.py results\play_<time>.json logs\<session folder>
```

Tell me when it's done. I'll read the score (agreement, how many speakers were created, A → B → A, latency including the speaker step). If it passes, I'll switch speaker labelling on by default and record it all.

      "type": "text",
      "text": "A → B → A **passes at 0.30** on the real clips (Speaker 1 → 2 → 1), and the fingerprint step costs about 40 ms per phrase. Both are recorded.\n\nSince a second remote person isn't available, I've added a substitute live test (commit `53a9f72`). Instead of a call, two FLEURS readers are played into your headphones:\n- **A** = one woman's 29 s recording, cut into 5 pieces.\n- **B** = one man's 31 s recording, cut into 5 pieces.\n- **Order:** A B A B B A A B A B, so it starts with A → B → A.\n\nThe live program hears this through the loopback exactly as it hears a call, and the scorer knows exactly who spoke when. This audio was never used for tuning. It's easier than a real call, though: there's no Meet processing, and a woman against a man is easier to separate than two similar voices. TESTS.md says so. A real two-person call stays part of the final acceptance test.\n\n## How to run it (T-SPK-2)\n\nYou need **two PowerShell windows** in the project folder, with the Buds connected as the output and nobody talking.\n\n**Window 1:** start the live program and wait for \"Listening…\":\n```\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --speakers --save-audio\n```\n\n**Window 2:** find the output device whose loopback is `[16]`, which should be the Buds \"Headphones\":\n```\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe tools\\play_speakers.py --list-outputs\n```\nThen play the sequence, putting that device's index in place of `N`:\n```\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe tools\\play_speakers.py --output N\n```\n- It counts down 3 seconds, then plays for about 75 seconds. You'll hear it in the Buds.\n- In Window 1, the lines should come up as **Speaker 1 / Speaker 2**.\n- When Window 2 says \"saved results\\play_….json\", press **Ctrl+C in Window 1**.\n\n**Then score it** in either window, using the two names it printed:\n```\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe tools\\score_playback.py results\\play_<time>.json logs\\<session folder>\n```\n\nTell me when it's done. I'll read the score (agreement, how many speakers were created, A → B → A, latency including the speaker step). If it passes, I'll switch speaker labelling on by default and record it all.",

Speaker labelling passed the held-out live test, so it's **now on by default** (commit `ac95aff`).

| T-SPK-2 (two readers played into the loopback) | Result |
|---|---|
| Remote phrases labelled correctly | **11 of 11** |
| Speakers created | 2 (Speaker 1 = woman, Speaker 2 = man) |
| A → B → A | **PASS**: Speaker 1 → 2 → 1 |
| Latency, typical / worst | 1.26 s / 1.94 s, none over 5 s |
| Cost of the speaker step | about 0.11 s per phrase |

**Two things in the output that might look wrong but aren't:**
- **"Remote: delivered 87.4%"** isn't lost speech. With no call running, Windows only sends loopback audio while something plays: the stream started 9.4 s in, and it pauses between and after the pieces. All 10 pieces were detected, with zero lag events.
- **"Me: no segments"** is right: nobody spoke into the mic.

**Why real calls will be harder (recorded in TESTS.md):**
- **Meet blurs voices.** Here, same-voice similarity was 0.80–0.91. On your Meet call it averaged 0.34, because of Meet's noise suppression and the brother's distance.
- **This was an easy pairing:** a woman against a man, reading clean text.
- **A real two-person call is still needed**, and it stays in the final acceptance test.

**Usage now:** run the program as before, `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16`, and remote lines show **Speaker 1 / Speaker 2 / …**. `--no-speakers` brings back the plain "Remote" label.

**Docs and commits:**
- **TESTS.md:** T-SPK-1 (with the 0.30 re-run) and T-SPK-2 are recorded with question, environment, configuration, results, decision and limitations.
- **DECISIONS.md:** D16 and D20 are updated, and item 2 of the plan is marked done.
- **Earlier play file:** `results\play_20261031-192013.json` is from an attempt before the scored run. I left it uncommitted, since nothing refers to it except a note in TESTS.md. Delete it if you like.

**Next per the plan: the final acceptance test.** I can write a checklist of the brief's requirements (two sources, device selection, HY, EN, labels, latency, local models, README, chat exports) and say how each will be checked. Then we run it in one session, ideally with two real remote people, as the interview will be.

The checklist is in the repo as `ACCEPTANCE.md` (commit `57b2d62`). Each item has a status and its evidence. Real-call results and the playback test are in separate columns, and the pass criteria for the real call are fixed in writing **before** the run.

## Where things stand

| Area | Passed | Failed | Untested |
|---|---|---|---|
| Required features | capture both sources, you still hear the call, device choice, Armenian, English, "Me" label, line format | – | **Speaker 1/2 labels in a real call** (passed only on playback) |
| Constraints | ≤ 5 s in real calls without labelling, Python, your laptop | **README model explanation** | ≤ 5 s in a real call with labelling on; local-only with the network off |
| Deliverables | source code; no weights, audio or keys in the repo | **Repo link, README, `chats/` exports** | – |
| Pre-interview | – | – | fresh install from the README, `--verify` on Windows, real two-person call |

**Recognition, measured so far:**
- **Read speech (FLEURS):** 11.9% of words wrong.
- **Your call clips checked against your references:** 15.0% wrong (9 of 60 words).

**One defect found and fixed during this review (`3c91ec8`):** labelling is now on by default, but a fresh setup wouldn't have downloaded the speaker model, so the program would have failed at start. The model is now part of the standard download, and a clear message appears if it's missing.

## Real-call test

**Pass criteria, fixed in advance:**
- Every line has time, label, Armenian and English.
- Your lines are 100% "Me".
- The number of remote speakers equals the people who actually spoke.
- At least 85% of remote phrases get the right label.
- An A → B → A stretch comes out 1 → 2 → 1.
- No line over 5 s.
- No processing failures.

**0. Pre-flight** (Meet closed):
```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans.models --verify
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --list-devices
```
The first command should end with `ALL OK`. In the second, check that 14 is still the microphone and 16 the Buds loopback.

**1. The call:**
- **Setup:** Google Meet, **two people on the remote side**, you on the laptop mic, the Buds as output. They can be on two devices, or on one phone if both sit equally close to it.
- **Content:** 3–5 minutes of Armenian conversation:
  - start with a clear **A → B → A**, each turn a full sentence;
  - then normal back-and-forth, including you;
  - a few short replies («այո», «հա»).
- **Run:**
  ```
  .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16 --save-audio
  ```
  The first line must end with `speakers=on (threshold 0.3)`. Press Ctrl+C at the end.

**2. Scoring:** tell me it's done. As before, I'll walk you through the remote clips one at a time for who spoke. Then I'll score criteria F1–F7 and update ACCEPTANCE.md and TESTS.md.

## Final repository review (after the call)

1. **README:** I draft it from DECISIONS.md and TESTS.md (setup with audio devices, models and alternatives, architecture, limitations). You review it.
2. **Fresh-install test:** clone the repo into a new folder and follow only the README, including `--verify` and one short playback run. That proves the instructions work on your laptop.
3. **`chats/`:** you export every AI session for this project from the app, one `.md` file each, unedited. I can't export them for you.
4. **Repository link:** you create the GitHub repo and push; I'll give you the exact commands. Before that I re-run the no-weights, no-audio, no-keys check on the final tree.

If the two-person call can't happen before the interview, ACCEPTANCE.md will keep those items marked **untested**, and the README will say so plainly, which the brief explicitly prefers to hiding it.

| Microphone labelled "Me" | ✅ 27 of 27 phrases in the real call |
| Remote voices as Speaker 1/2, same label all session | ✅ In the real call: 2 people became Speaker 1 and Speaker 2, and you judged the labels correct. I can't claim more, because nobody labelled each phrase by hand. |
| Timestamps, and English within 5 s | ✅ Real call: 0 of 45 phrases over 5 s, slowest 2.37 s |
| Local models only | ✅ The program only uses the network to download models during setup. I checked this in the code; it hasn't been tested with the network switched off. |
| README (setup, audio devices, models and alternatives, architecture, limitations, improvements) | ✅ Added in `fd7bce8` |
| No model weights, audio or API keys committed | ✅ I checked the current files and the whole Git history: no audio or model files, no key-like strings. The largest file is 76 KB. |
| `chats/` folder | ❌ Missing. Only you can export the sessions. |
| Repository link | ❌ The repository hasn't been published yet. |

The same commit also adds the real-call run to TESTS.md and updates ACCEPTANCE.md. The pass criteria in its section F were mine, not the brief's, and the file now says so.

`results/play_20261031-192013.json` is left uncommitted on purpose; it's an earlier run that was never scored.

**Two checks only you can run on Windows:**
- `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m livetrans.models --verify` should print `ALL OK`. Nobody has reported its output yet.
- A fresh setup from the README in a new folder hasn't been tried. Doing it once before the interview would confirm the setup steps work.

## Chat exports
- The brief says the folder must be called **`chats/`**, not `/chat`.
- Export every Claude session you used for this project as its own `.md` file: this conversation, all earlier sessions, and any side chats. They must be complete and unedited.
- Put them in `live-armenian-translation\chats\`, then run:
  ```powershell
  git add chats
  git commit -m "Add complete AI chat exports"
  ```
- Don't delete any of the original sessions in the app. The interviewers may compare the exports with them.

## Before publishing: privacy
The `eval/` and `results/` folders contain the text of your family calls, including names (no audio). If the repository is public, anyone can read them. You can make it private and give the reviewers access, or keep it public if you're fine with that. It's your call.

## Publishing
1. On GitHub, create an **empty** repository named `live-armenian-translation`. Don't add a README, .gitignore or licence there.
2. In the project folder:
   ```powershell
   git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-username>/live-armenian-translation.git
   git push -u origin main
   ```
   If you add `chats/` after this push, run `git push` again.
3. On GitHub, check that the README shows on the front page and that there's no `models/`, `logs/` or `recordings/` folder.
4. If the repository is private, give Mathrix's reviewers access.
5. Send Mathrix the repository link (`https://github.com/<your-username>/live-armenian-translation`) the way they asked.

The network is only used once, during\n  setup, to download the models.\n\nBuilt and tested on **Windows 11**, Intel i5-13500H, 8 GB RAM, no GPU,\nPython 3.13. System-audio capture uses WASAPI loopback, so the program runs on\nWindows only (see Limitations).\n\n## 1. Setup\n\nRequirements: Windows 10/11, Python 3.13, about 1.1 GB of disk for the models.\n\n```powershell\ngit clone <this repository>\ncd live-armenian-translation\npy -3.13 -m venv .venv\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt\n\n# download the five models (pinned revisions) into models/ - once, needs internet\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m livetrans.models\n# check file hashes, revisions and package versions\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m livetrans.models --verify     # prints ALL OK\n```\n\n`models/`, `logs/` and `recordings/` are git-ignored. No model weights or\naudio are in the repository.\n\n## 2. Audio devices\n\nWindows offers a **loopback** twin of every output device: it records what\nthat output plays. That covers the brief's \"equivalent\" of BlackHole plus a\nMulti-Output Device on macOS. You keep hearing the call normally and no\nvirtual cable is needed (PyAudioWPatch provides WASAPI loopback).\n\n1. Choose the headphones or speakers that the call app plays to, and make that\n   device the output in the call app (or the Windows default output).\n2. List the devices:\n   ```powershell\n   .\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m livetrans --list-devices\n   ```\n   Note the index of your **microphone** and the index of the **[Loopback]**\n   entry with the same name as your output device.\n3. Use the laptop's built-in microphone, not a Bluetooth headset microphone.\n   Opening a Bluetooth headset's mic switches it to the hands-free profile,\n   which moves the call audio to a different output and the loopback goes\n   silent (found in test T-M0-1).\n\nThe program refuses a loopback index given as `--mic` and the other way\nround. It never picks a device silently.\n\n## 3. Run\n\n```powershell\n.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m livetrans --mic 14 --loopback 16\n```\n\n(14 and 16 are the indices on the development laptop; use yours.) Start-up\ntakes about 10 s while the models load and warm up. Then talk. **Ctrl+C**\nstops the program and prints a summary: latency per source, capture problems\nand the number of remote speakers. A text log of each session goes to\n`logs/<timestamp>/` (git-ignored).\n\nUseful options:\n\n| Option | Default | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `--no-speakers` | speakers on | label every remote phrase \"Remote\" instead of Speaker N |\n| `--spk-threshold` | 0.30 | cosine similarity needed to match an existing speaker |\n| `--min-silence` | 0.5 | seconds of silence that end a phrase |\n| `--max-speech` | 10 | force a cut after this many seconds of speech |\n| `--beam` | 1 | translation beam size |\n| `--save-audio` | off | also keep each phrase as a WAV in the log folder |\n\n## 4. How it works\n\n```\nmic ─────┐                                                          ┌─ \"Me\"\n         ├─ WASAPI capture ─ 16 kHz mono ─ Silero VAD ─ phrase ─┬───┤\nloopback ┘  (PyAudioWPatch)    (soxr)      (per source)          │   └─ WeSpeaker embedding ─ online clustering ─ \"Speaker N\"\n                                                                  ▼\n                                   FastConformer-hy CTC (ONNX) ─ Armenian text ─ NLLB-200 600M int8 ─ English\n                                                                  ▼\n                                         terminal: [time] label / HY / EN / latency\n```\n\n| Module | Does |\n|---|---|\n| `livetrans/audio/` | `devices.py` lists and checks devices. `capture.py` runs one callback stream per device; the callback only time-stamps the buffer. `ChunkAligner` puts both sources on one shared clock. `convert.py` resamples to 16 kHz mono. |\n| `segmenter.py` | Silero VAD (ONNX), frame by frame. 0.5 s of silence ends a phrase; 10 s forces a cut. |\n| `speakers.py` | WeSpeaker ResNet34 embedding per remote phrase, then online clustering (below). |\n| `asr.py` | FastConformer-Hybrid Large (Armenian), CTC head, through `onnx-asr`. |\n| `translate.py` | NLLB-200 distilled 600M, int8, CTranslate2, `hye_Armn -> eng_Latn`. |\n| `pipeline.py` | One worker thread takes phrases from a FIFO queue: speaker, ASR, MT, print. Measures latency from the end of speech and splits it into vad / queue / spk / asr / mt. |\n| `models.py` | Pinned model registry (repo, revision, sha256); download and `--verify`. |\n| `__main__.py` | Command line, start-up, live warnings, session summary. |\n\nDesign choices:\n\n- **One phrase at a time.** Each model runs once per phrase, on whole\n  phrases. ASR on a 2-5 s phrase takes about 0.1-0.3 s on this CPU, so\n  streaming recognition isn't needed to stay under 5 s. One worker keeps the\n  models from competing for CPU.\n- **Speaker rules**, borrowed from diart (Coria et al.) without its\n  segmentation model. Mic phrases are always \"Me\". For each remote phrase:\n  - 1.0 s or longer: it is embedded and compared with each speaker's centroid.\n    At similarity 0.30 or above it gets the best-matching label.\n  - Below 0.30: a new speaker is created only if the phrase is 1.5 s or longer.\n    Otherwise it gets the closest label.\n  - Centroids are only updated from phrases of 1.5 s or longer.\n  - Phrases shorter than 1.0 s keep the previous remote label.\n- **Too little text to translate.** If recognition returns fewer than two\n  Armenian letters, the line is shown without a translation. NLLB invents\n  whole sentences for one-letter input such as «Հ։» (T-OFF-1).\n\nThe development record is in `PLAN.md`, `DECISIONS.md` (decisions D1-D20)\nand `TESTS.md` (every experiment: question, environment, configuration,\nresult, decision, limitations, commit). `ACCEPTANCE.md` checks the brief item\nby item. `tools/` holds the measurement scripts and `results/` their outputs.\n\n## 5. Models: what I chose and why\n\nArmenian is low-resource, so each choice was checked against public\nbenchmarks and then measured on this laptop. All numbers below are from the\nlaptop (Windows) unless marked otherwise.\n\n| Task | Chosen | Size | Licence |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Speech recognition | NVIDIA `stt_hy_fastconformer_hybrid_large_pc`, CTC head, ONNX export by OpenVoiceOS | 115M params, 437 MB | CC-BY-4.0 |\n| Translation | Meta `nllb-200-distilled-600M`, int8 CTranslate2 conversion | 618 MB | CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial) |\n| Speakers | WeSpeaker VoxCeleb ResNet34-LM, ONNX | 26 MB | CC-BY-4.0 |\n| Phrase detection | Silero VAD, ONNX | 2 MB | MIT |\n\nAll revisions and file hashes are pinned in `livetrans/models.py`.\n\n### Speech recognition: FastConformer-Hybrid (hy), CTC\n\n- **Why:** it is the best open model on the independent ArmBench-ASR v1.0\n  leaderboard (combined WER 19.9; Whisper-large-v3 zero-shot 65.1). It is\n  small enough for a CPU, and the ONNX export runs without NeMo or PyTorch.\n- **Measured:**\n  - 11.9 % WER (CER 5.0 %) on 100 FLEURS read-speech clips, 0.15 s per\n    11.7 s clip (E3).\n  - 15.0 % WER on 14 user-checked phrases from real Google Meet calls\n    (9 errors in 60 words).\n- **Alternatives considered:**\n  - **The same weights with the RNN-T head** (Vana-Labs ONNX export), which\n    Karpov et al. (Interspeech 2025) motivated testing. 11.4 % vs 11.9 % WER\n    on the same 100 clips: the difference is not significant (95 % CI\n    -1.3 to +0.3 points), and RNN-T is about 5x slower. **CTC kept** (E3).\n  - **Whisper and its Armenian fine-tunes:** ranked below FastConformer on\n    ArmBench and 7-13x larger. Not run.\n  - **Meta MMS / omnilingual ASR:** lower on ArmBench. Not run.\n- **Risk:** ArmBench reports about 61 % WER on movie dialogue for this model.\n  Conversation is far harder than read speech; see Limitations.\n\n### Translation: NLLB-200 distilled 600M, int8, beam 1\n\n- **Why:** the strongest open translation model that covers Armenian and is\n  small enough to run in well under a second on a CPU with CTranslate2 int8.\n- **Measured:**\n  - FLEURS chrF 61.1 with beam 1 and 61.7 with beam 4 (T-MT-1).\n  - On 5 call phrases, beams 1 and 4 gave the same meaning; median 204 ms vs\n    256 ms. **Beam 1 chosen** (E2).\n- **Alternatives:**\n  - **NLLB-200 1.3B:** might fix the place-name errors, but is about twice\n    the size. Proposed, not tested.\n  - **Large LLM translators:** too slow on this CPU for a 5 s budget. Not\n    tested.\n- **Licence:** NLLB is non-commercial (CC-BY-NC). That is fine for this\n  challenge, but would have to be replaced in a product.\n\n### Speakers: WeSpeaker ResNet34 + online clustering\n\n- **Why:** a 26 MB speaker-embedding model takes about 0.1 s per phrase on\n  the CPU, and it loads through `onnx-asr`, which is already installed.\n  Clustering with fixed rules gives stable labels without a second model.\n- **Measured:**\n  - Recorded voices played into the system audio (never used for tuning):\n    11/11 phrases labelled correctly, A -> B -> A gave Speaker 1 -> 2 -> 1,\n    speaker step about 0.11 s (T-SPK-2).\n  - Real Meet clips: 92.3 % agreement with my labels. The threshold was tuned\n    on these same clips (T-SPK-1).\n- **Alternatives:**\n  - **pyannote 3.x pipeline, diart:** need PyTorch and more CPU. They also\n    re-segment audio that VAD has already cut.\n  - **CAM++ and other embedding models:** not tested.\n\n### Phrase detection: Silero VAD\n\nSmall and fast, runs on 16 kHz frames, and is widely used. Phrase cutting was\nchecked on the first two-voice recording (T-VAD-1).\n\n## 6. Results on the target laptop\n\n| Run | What | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| T-LIVE-8, 2026-11-01 | Real Google Meet call: me on the laptop mic, two people on the remote side, all defaults | 45 phrases (27 Me, 18 remote), 2 remote speakers created; **0 over 5 s**, p50 1.6 s, max 2.37 s; speaker step mean 0.07 s; no processing failures. I judged the Me / Speaker 1 / Speaker 2 labels correct; per-phrase labels were not scored |\n| T-LIVE-5 / T-LIVE-6 | Real calls, before speaker labels | 0/34 and 0/44 phrases over 5 s |\n| T-SPK-2 | Recorded voices played into the loopback | 11/11 labels, max latency 1.94 s |\n| E3 | ASR on 100 FLEURS clips | 11.9 % WER |\n| Call clips | 14 user-checked call phrases | 15.0 % WER |\n\nLatency is measured from the end of the spoken phrase (on the audio clock) to\nthe moment the English line is printed. About 0.5-0.7 s of it is the silence\nthe VAD waits for before it ends a phrase.\n\n## 7. Known limitations\n\n- **Recognition on real calls is the weak part.** Read speech is about 12 %\n  WER. On calls, accents, distance from the mic, Bluetooth mics and Meet's\n  noise suppression make it noticeably worse. My own Western-influenced\n  pronunciation was not tested separately. Wrong Armenian gives wrong English.\n- **Meet removes quiet speech.** Meet replaces quiet or distant speech with\n  digital silence before it reaches the laptop, so that speech never arrives\n  (T-INSP-1).\n- **Translation errors:** place names («Վանաձոր» became \"Vancouver\"). Very\n  short replies are sometimes over-translated («Այո» became \"I did.\").\n  Phrases under two Armenian letters are shown untranslated.\n- **Speaker labels:**\n  - One label per phrase: if two people talk inside one phrase, both get the\n    same label.\n  - Phrases under 1 s keep the previous remote label.\n  - The threshold was tuned on little real data (two remote voices).\n  - Two similar voices are harder to separate than the voices tested.\n  - Labels are least reliable in the first minute.\n- **Echo** (my voice coming back through a remote device) shows up as a remote\n  phrase. Echo handling is out of scope in the brief.\n- **Microphone frame shortfall (open, cause unknown).** On this laptop's mic,\n  the stream sometimes delivers fewer samples than expected: 95.8-99.2 % in\n  the latest runs, as low as 84 % on the first day. It happens with the\n  models off too. The aligner re-anchors the timeline with zeros, which can\n  land inside a word.\n- **Windows only.** Capture uses WASAPI loopback. macOS would need BlackHole\n  plus a different capture module.\n- **Mic and system audio share one processing queue.** If many phrases end\n  at the same time they wait in line. The queue never grew beyond one phrase\n  in the tests.\n\n## 8. What I would improve with more time\n\n1.
